constraints: Model proposes, code decides: models may interpret, phrase or suggest, but never award passes, change objective marks, select a learner, replace a transcript, or advance state without code validation (curriculum/service.py:1-5; docs/DECISIONS.md D-12, D-18; docs/LEARNING_AGENTS.md:39-57).

Four skills stay separate; no merged score, no CEFR certification claim, no pronunciation scoring (curriculum/service.py:33-38 POLICY; practice/acceptance.py:42-43 no_score_or_level_stored; DECISIONS D-16, D-20).
Typed input never counts as speaking practice (practice/turns.py:253-257; acceptance A03).
Points reward doing and are never a judgement of the learner's Dutch (stories/today.py:1; DECISIONS D-19).
Every paid provider call must be reserved against usage counters first; production requires Azure providers and PAID_USAGE_ENABLED=true (usage/service.py; config.py:149-171).
Replays/retries must never double-charge or double-score: request ids, client_turn_id, payload fingerprints (pinned in test_topics, test_coaching, test_topic_conversations, test_turns).
All fixed and generated content must remain labelled unreviewed/generated (content_status fields; content/schemas.py LocalizedText.review_status).
Trilingual support nl/en/fa with Persian RTL help ladder (content/schemas.py:69-83; curriculum/schemas.py:15-18); Belgian Standard Dutch in all prompts (stories/prompts.py:12-18).

Coach must need at least two assessed attempts before labelling repeated difficulty, ignore stale content versions, and the learner may ignore any plan (LEARNING_AGENTS.md:53-57; tests/test_coaching.py:56-102).
Content review is admin-only and never publishes (routes_content_review.py:17-20; content_review/service.py:1).

Tests pin: GET /today queues an episode on first visit (test_stories.py:164-170); story/video answers are graded once and re-answer is 409 (test_stories.py:258-291); SM-2 intervals 1->6->>=15 and 10-minute lapse (test_stories.py:123-136); read-aloud response has no 'score' key (test_stories.py:384); topic banks need >=100 distinct topics per skill (test_topics.py:62); exactly ten pilot conversations (test_topic_conversations.py:145); complete_once never retries (test_single_model_call.py:74).
Background work runs in the in-process JobLoop on a warm 0.25 vCPU API (DECISIONS D-17); chat adapter concurrency is 2 per process (chat_openai_compatible.py:98).
open_questions: Whether library story questions are graded only client-side in the web app (grammar practice is confirmed client-only in CurriculumControls.tsx; library story component not inspected).

Whether the deployed Azure OpenAI model (STATUS.md mentions gpt-4.1-mini) is used for both chat and chat_strong in production and whether it supports strict json_schema structured outputs/tool calling (not verified in infra).
Whether the learner's support language (Learner.support_language, default 'fa') is ever updated server-side; no route updating it was found in the API.
Actual production usage limits (Bicep parameters may override config.py defaults of 200 model calls/day, 200k tokens/day, 1800 audio s/day, 300 video s/day).
Whether the owner is willing to relax the 'no score/no level' policy to show mastery estimates, or wants estimates labelled as practice indicators only.
Whether the platform is intended to remain single-learner (identity/models.py:14 'Release 0.1 has exactly one learner') or support multiple learners, which affects agent cost design.
Whether the templated content banks should be regenerated offline, replaced by on-demand generation, or retired in favour of the serial and role-play.

areas.area: LLM layer: how agentic the system is today, and where real agents would help (Azure production target)
areas.overview:
HOW IT WORKS. Every model call goes through the `ChatModel` interface (apps/api/src/dlp/providers/base.py:48-92), which has two methods. `complete` retries. `complete_once` sends exactly one HTTP request. Its contract is at base.py:75-81 and apps/api/tests/test_single_model_call.py enforces it.

There is one real client, `OpenAICompatibleChatModel` (providers/chat_openai_compatible.py:91-243). It uses raw httpx with no openai SDK; pyproject only lists httpx and langgraph. The same client serves Ollama (`llama3.1:8b`) and Azure OpenAI.

On Azure it uses Chat Completions only. With `AZURE_CHAT_API_VERSION=v1` the URL is `{endpoint}/openai/v1/chat/completions` (chat_openai_compatible.py:43-48; Bicep sets v1 at infra/main.bicep:344). Authentication is a managed-identity bearer token (scope `https://ai.azure.com/.default`, registry.py:41-54) or an api-key.

The request body is: model, messages, temperature and `max_tokens`. When a schema is given, it also adds `response_format: {type: json_object}` and a system message with the Pydantic JSON schema (`schema_instruction`, :84-88, :174-184). The body never contains tools, `stream`, a strict `json_schema` or a seed. `ChatMessage.role` allows only system, user or assistant (base.py:12).

On the reply side, `extract_json_object` pulls out the JSON and Pydantic validates it. `complete` then:
- repairs schema errors by appending the bad reply plus the error (at most `CHAT_MAX_ATTEMPTS=3`);
- doubles `max_tokens` when `finish_reason=length`;
- retries 408/409/425/429/5xx with jittered backoff;
- fails fast on ConnectError.

A BoundedSemaphore per model instance limits concurrency. Token usage is read from the final response only.

There are two tiers: `providers.chat` (small) and `providers.chat_strong`. The strong tier falls back to small; Bicep points STRONG at 'chat-small' when no strong model is configured (main.bicep:346). The live model is gpt-4.1-mini (docs/STATUS.md:10). `FixtureChatModel` answers by prompt_version using keyword rule tables (fixtures.py:33-88). Prompts are inline Python strings with version tags; there are no template files.

INVENTORY (feature | entry | prompt | output contract | validation | model calls per user action | state | failure handling):
1. **Mission role-play turn** | practice/workflow.py:run_turn, called from practice/turns.py:submit_turn (POST /practice/sessions/{id}/turns[/speech]) | Dutch `propose_action_messages` (propose-action-v3: scenario, slots, appointment state, last 6 turns), then `character_reply_messages` (character-reply-v1: persona, phase anchor `fixed_line`, code decision note) | `ProposedActionReply` → `CharacterReply{reply_nl}` | `apply_action` in code (practice/actions.py:93-188); `_contradicts_decision` keyword guard; service scenarios always use fixed lines | 2 logical calls via `complete` (1 for service scenarios), each up to 3 HTTP requests; reserves 2 calls / 1800 tokens | PracticeSession.state.appointment / step_progress; PracticeTurn.model_meta (prompt versions, tokens, latency) | If the first call fails, the turn is marked failed and returns 502 with reservations released. If the reply call fails, the fixed line is used.
2. **Guided topic conversation** | topic_conversations/workflow.py:run_turn, called from service.turn (POST /topic-conversations/{id}/turns) | English system prompt with JSON goal/choices; user JSON {last 2 turns, learner_response} (topic-conversation-intent-v1) | `TopicInterpretation{intent, goal_id, met, language_is_dutch, quote, choice_id}` | `validate_meaning`: quote is a substring, anchor groups, choice aliases and negation, injection regex. The partner reply is always authored text (hint / cue / accepted + next cue / success). | 1 `complete_once` call (0 for hint/repeat), 400 output tokens | TopicConversation.history JSON, step_index, assisted_steps; a PracticeObservation on finish | Commits a conservative usage estimate, does not add the turn, returns 503.
3. **Mission step feedback** | feedback/service.py:generate_feedback | Dutch coach prompt with evidence handles E1..En (feedback-v2) | `FeedbackModelReply` (nl/fa/en summary, points) | `check_expectations` before the call; `resolve_handles` plus quote-in-evidence check; dropped points are stored | 1 `complete` (up to 3 HTTP) | FeedbackReport row; note on SkillRecord | Releases reservations and raises.
4. **Productive skill assessment** | curriculum/service.py:assess_productive, used by save_practice, submit_attempt (2 calls) and topics.save_topic_practice | English rubric prompt (curriculum-rubric-v1) on chat_strong | `ProductiveReply` (criteria with quote, feedback nl/en/fa) | `validate_productive_reply`: every criterion covered, quote grounded, word bounds | 1 (final check: 2) | CurriculumPractice / TopicPractice / CurriculumAttempt.results; PracticeObservation | Releases reservations; 503.
5. **Writing corrections** | curriculum/writing.py:writing_feedback (writing-corrections-v1, chat_strong) | `WritingReply` (at most 5 span corrections) | `validate_corrections`: unique exact span, word boundaries, no overlap, at most +5 words. Any violation rejects the whole reply. | 1 | Not persisted | 503.
6. **Story episode writer** | stories/service.py:generate_episode (job `story_episode`) | WRITER_SYSTEM plus bible, last 4 recaps, brief, known/candidate words (story-episode-v1, temperature 0.7) | `EpisodeDraft` | `validator.validate_draft` (10 checks) → one rewrite using `feedback_text`, best of 2 kept | Up to 2 logical (up to 6 HTTP) | StorySeries.memory (last 12 recaps with choices); StoryEpisode.checks | Error codes provider / quality / allowance / interrupted.
7. **Paragraph translation** | stories/service.py:translate_paragraph | story-translate-v1 | `Translation` | Schema only | 1 `complete_once` | Cached in paragraphs[i].fa | Commits the estimate and raises.
8. **Video script** | videos/service.py:_write (job `video_script`) | video-script-v1 | `VideoScript` | `check_script` = `validate_draft` + scene counts + minimum seconds; one rewrite | Up to 2 | VideoLesson | Same pattern as the story writer.
9. **Coach ordering** | coaching/service.py:_rank_once (POST /coach/plan) | English "Order these three existing activities" (practice-plan-v1) | `PlanRanking` (exactly 3 ids) | `validate_ranking` | 1 `complete_once`, or 0 if cached or fixture | CoachPlanRequest cache keyed by history_version | Falls back to the deterministic plan.
10. **Content review (admin)** | content_review/service.py:process_review (job `content_review`) | topic-editorial-v1 | `ReviewReply` (at most 12 issues) | `validate_reply`: path exists and quote is in the content | 1 `complete_once` per topic | ContentReview cache | Marked failed with a code; at-most-once claim.
11. **Offline benchmark** | benchmarks/language/harness.py | Generic prompt (benchmark-v1), 40 cases | — | — | — | — | Not tied to the production prompts.

CLASSIFICATION. On the spectrum from single prompted call → validated generation pipeline → tool-using agent → multi-agent, the system sits at **validated generation pipeline**, on purpose:
- Features 3, 4, 5, 7, 9 and 10 are single calls with a post-hoc validator.
- Features 1, 2, 6 and 8 are fixed pipelines. Features 1 and 2 are LangGraph graphs with three linear nodes, no conditional edges, no ToolNode and no checkpointer (practice/workflow.py:123-131; topic_conversations/workflow.py:118-126). Features 6 and 8 are generate → deterministic validator → one rewrite loops.

Nothing is a tool-using agent: the client has no tool schema or tool role. Nothing is multi-agent. docs/LEARNING_AGENTS.md calls these "roles", and says they have "no open tool loop".

WHERE AGENTS WOULD HELP:
- (a) **A tool-using study guide** using existing deterministic functions as tools: candidate_plan, history_page, vocab.due_items, today.streak, stories.today_episode, videos.today_summary, topics.topic_page, library.vocabulary_page. This replaces today's coach, which only reorders 3 items. It directly targets the owner's "confused at start".
- (a) **A generative conversation partner** in place of the canned cue repetition, anchored the way mission compose_reply already is.
- (a) **A multi-round writing / grammar tutor** with memory of recurring errors.
- (b) **Agents are the wrong tool for:** grading, final checks, apply_action, SRS, points and usage. The per-turn interpretation hot path should also stay a single call.
- (c) **Seams that already exist:** the ChatModel interface and tiers, the durable PostgreSQL job runner, usage reserve/commit/release with request-id deduplication, `paid_model_guard`, prompt version tags, validators, fixture rule tables, and LangGraph already installed.
- (c) **What is missing:** tool and function calling, strict structured outputs, streaming, a Responses API / reasoning-model path, LLM spans and per-feature metrics, evals built on the production prompts, a learner memory/profile, per-run agent budgets, and a lease heartbeat.

AZURE AI PROVISIONING. infra/main.bicep:237-265 provisions one `Microsoft.CognitiveServices/accounts` of kind 'OpenAI' with `disableLocalAuth`, deployments `chat-small` and an optional `chat-strong` (NoAutoUpgrade), and the role 'Cognitive Services OpenAI User' for the API identity. It also provisions Application Insights. There is no Foundry project, AI Search/vector store, or agent service. The API is a single replica (0.25 vCPU) running the job loop in-process.

key_files.role: ChatModel interface (complete / complete_once), ChatMessage (roles system|user|assistant only), ChatResult with token/attempt accounting
Only real chat client: raw httpx Chat Completions for Ollama and Azure v1, json_object mode + schema-in-prompt, repair/truncation/transport retries, semaphore, usage extraction
build_chat(settings, tier) small/strong; Azure managed-identity token provider; Providers dataclass (chat, chat_strong, stt, tts, blob, video)
FixtureChatModel: canned replies keyed by prompt_version with keyword rule tables and failure injection; used by CI and browser tests
LangGraph propose_action → validate_action → compose_reply mission turn; contradiction guard; fixed-line fallback
propose-action-v3 and character-reply-v1 prompt builders, fixed_line anchoring, phase_for
submit_turn: usage reserve (2 calls/1800 tokens), run_turn, evidence writing, skill record, TTS of reply
apply_action: deterministic authority over appointment/service state
interpret (1 complete_once) → validate_meaning → compose with authored replies only
Conversation lifecycle, 6-turn cap, usage reservation, observation on finish
candidate_plan (pure code), _rank_once LLM reordering of 3 activities, validate_ranking, fallback, paid_model_guard advisory lock
Evidence-handle-cited feedback with citation/quote validation and dropped points
assess_productive rubric call + validate_productive_reply; objective_result; final-check submit_attempt
Span-level writing corrections with validate_corrections (reject whole reply on any violation)
Story writer job (generate → validate → one rewrite), translation call, learner actions, memory
Deterministic quality gate (Dutch, length, sentence length, coverage, glossary, question evidence) + feedback_text for rewrite
Video script writer reusing validate_draft, render jobs, video_seconds usage
Admin editorial review job, at-most-once claim, path/quote validation
SQL-enforced reserve/commit/release per metric (model_calls, tokens, audio_seconds, video_seconds), request-id dedup
Durable PostgreSQL job queue: registry, enqueue idempotency, lease claim, backoff, single-thread JobLoop
HTTP-only OpenTelemetry to App Insights; prompts/bodies never exported; provider auto-instrumentation disabled
Chat/usage/job settings and production rules (Azure chat required, PAID_USAGE_ENABLED required)
Enforces complete_once = exactly one HTTP request, no repair/retry, no leaking of learner text
Role/responsibility table (model may / application decides), cost rules, 'no open tool loop'
D-12 (turn shape, model never decides), D-18 (model proposes, validator decides), D-17 paid usage, D-19/D-20 points and no pronunciation score
Story writer flow, validator table, memory and choice rules, cost limits
Video script flow reusing story validator, renderer and seconds budget

Azure OpenAI account (kind OpenAI), chat-small / optional chat-strong deployments, role assignment, API env (v1, deployments, usage caps 80 calls/80k tokens per day), App Insights
Local/Azure chat settings, usage limit defaults (200 calls/200k tokens per day)
UI for coach plan; 'Stem de volgorde op mij af' button triggers the only coach model call
UI for guided conversations: respond / repeat / hint buttons, 6-turn bounded flow

strengths: Clean provider seam: application code depends only on ChatModel (providers/base.py) and a single registry decides local/Azure/fixture (providers/registry.py:57-77), so a new agent runtime or Responses-API adapter can be added behind one interface.

Consistent 'models propose, code validates' discipline with explicit validators per feature (apply_action, validate_meaning, validate_ranking, resolve_handles, validate_productive_reply, validate_corrections, validate_draft, validate_reply) — exactly the guardrail layer an agent's tool results need.

Grounding by quotation everywhere: model claims must quote exact learner text or content paths (topic_conversations/workflow.py:72-74, curriculum/service.py:197, feedback/service.py:183-193, content_review/service.py:66-68).

Cost safety is engineered, not hoped for: SQL-enforced reserve/commit/release with request-id dedup (usage/service.py:104-172), conservative commit on uncertain failures for complete_once paths, PAID_USAGE_ENABLED gate, advisory-lock paid_model_guard (coaching/service.py:51-57).
complete_once contract plus a dedicated test suite prevents silent multiplication of paid calls (base.py:65-89; tests/test_single_model_call.py).

Durable PostgreSQL job runner with leases, idempotency keys and at-most-once 'running/generating' claims for paid background generation (jobs/service.py; stories/service.py:219-222; content_review/service.py:159-162).

Prompt versions are stored with results (PracticeTurn.model_meta, FeedbackReport.prompt_version, StoryEpisode.prompt_version, VideoLesson.prompt_version) and fixture replies are keyed by version, enabling regression tests per prompt.
Story/video writer already implements a validator-in-the-loop rewrite with actionable findings (stories/validator.py:238-263), a proven pattern to generalise.
Prompt-injection framing ('untrusted quoted evidence, never instructions') is present in every learner-text prompt, plus a regex guard in validate_meaning.
Privacy-aware telemetry: no prompts/bodies exported (observability.py:1), provider errors never forwarded (chat_openai_compatible.py:115-117).

findings.title: Conversation partner never speaks generatively; only 10 conversations exist
findings.evidence: apps/api/src/dlp/domains/topic_conversations/workflow.py:106-116 (compose returns step.hint / step.cue / accepted+next cue / success — all authored); topic_conversations/schemas.py:103 `conversations: list[Blueprint] = Field(min_length=10, max_length=10)`; docs/LEARNING_AGENTS.md:4-5 'ten now also have a short, turn-by-turn conversation'; MAX_TURNS = 6 (topic_conversations/service.py:23)
findings.detail: Whenever an answer is not accepted, the partner repeats exactly the same authored cue. The model only classifies intent and quotes. Only 10 of the roughly 1,200 topic×stage situations have a conversation at all. This is the most likely cause of the owner's 'very limited and boring'. The mission role-play (practice/workflow.py) already has a generative compose_reply step anchored on a fixed line and guarded by `_contradicts_decision`, but the topic conversations do not use it.
findings.recommendation: Add a bounded generative partner reply to topic conversations using the mission pattern: the model phrases the reply, the authored cue/accepted text is the anchor, and a contradiction guard plus fallback to authored text apply. This becomes a second call, so 'one complete_once per turn' in LEARNING_AGENTS.md must be consciously revised. Scale the number of blueprints with an offline generation pipeline (validator + content_review queue) instead of hand-writing them. Optionally let the partner call read-only tools (lookup a word in library_for(stage).vocabulary, give the next hint rung).

findings.title: The 'coach' is a paid reorder of three deterministic items and cannot explain how the app helps
findings.evidence: apps/api/src/dlp/domains/coaching/service.py:289-331 (_rank_once: prompt 'Order these three existing Dutch practice activities'; PlanRanking exactly 3 ids, coaching/schemas.py:18-21); candidate_plan is pure code (160-221); apps/web/components/PracticeCoach.tsx:53 button 'Stem de volgorde op mij af'
findings.detail: The owner felt confused at the start and unsure how the app helps them learn Dutch. Nothing in the LLM layer explains the path, adapts to stated goals, or links the features together: the word bank, story serial, videos, topic practice, missions and the curriculum path are all separate. The only 'coach' model call changes the order of three cards. The underlying deterministic signals already exist: observations, failed_refs, due words, streak, today's episode and video readiness.
findings.recommendation: Build a tool-using study-guide agent. It is the clearest case where an agent adds visible value. Expose read-only tools wrapping existing functions: coaching.candidate_plan / history_page, stories.vocab.due_items / stats, stories.today.streak / recent_days, stories.service.today_episode, videos.service.today_summary, curriculum.topics.topic_page / topic_detail, curriculum.service.catalogue. The agent produces a short natural-language plan and an onboarding explanation. Activity IDs and deep links are restricted to tool-returned IDs and validated in code (generalise validate_ranking). Keep a deterministic fallback, cache by history_version as CoachPlanRequest does, and cap steps and tokens per run.

findings.title: Chat client cannot do tool calling, strict structured outputs, streaming or reasoning/Responses models
findings.evidence: providers/base.py:12 `Role = Literal["system", "user", "assistant"]`; chat_openai_compatible.py:174-184 body has only model/messages/temperature/max_tokens/response_format json_object; chat_openai_compatible.py:43-48 Chat Completions URLs only; docs/GO_LIVE.md:49-51 'This client requires Chat Completions, JSON mode, `temperature` and `max_tokens`. A reasoning-only deployment with different request semantics is not interchangeable.'; docs/ENGINEERING.md:156 'Streaming is not part of 0.1.'

findings.title: Semantic validators sit outside the repair loop, so grounded-but-imperfect replies become 503s
findings.evidence: curriculum/writing.py:55-65 raises ProviderError on any non-unique or partial span, and 149-151 returns the whole reply as failed; curriculum/service.py:190-191 'assessment response did not cover the required criteria'; coaching/service.py:320-325 falls back; only stories/service.py:291-302 and videos/service.py:220-230 feed validator findings back to the writer
findings.detail: The provider's `complete` repair loop only fixes JSON/schema errors. Domain validation runs after usage has been committed. A single bad correction span therefore discards all five corrections, and the learner sees 'temporarily unavailable', even though the model answered and was paid for. This is a cheap win that does not need agents.
findings.recommendation: Generalise the story pattern into a reusable helper: generate → domain validator returns findings → one targeted retry with the findings → keep the best valid result. For writing, drop only the invalid corrections instead of rejecting all of them. Account for the extra call through usage.reserve.

findings.title: Usage accounting undercounts retried calls; failure policies differ between legacy and complete_once paths
findings.evidence: chat_openai_compatible.py:216-233 (token usage taken from final response only; attempts returned but earlier attempts' tokens dropped); feedback/service.py:173-174 commits 1 call regardless of result.attempts; practice/workflow.py:112-114 a failed compose_reply is not added to model_calls, so turns.py:186-188 commits fewer calls; legacy paths release on ProviderError (feedback/service.py:169-172, curriculum/service.py:238-241, writing.py:143-146, turns.py:177-179) while complete_once paths commit the estimate (topic_conversations/service.py:223-228); docs/LEARNING_AGENTS.md:76-77 'Legacy retrying workflows retain their existing limits.'
findings.detail: With `complete` making up to 3 HTTP requests (plus truncation doubling), real token spend can be about 3× what is committed. A refused or failed call may still be billed, yet the legacy paths refund it. A multi-step agent loop would amplify this gap.
findings.recommendation: Accumulate input and output tokens across attempts in `_complete`, and commit `attempts` as model_calls. Apply the complete_once policy everywhere: commit the estimate on uncertain failure. For agents, reserve a per-run budget (max steps × estimate) under a run id and commit per step.

findings.title: No LLM observability or production-prompt evals
findings.evidence: observability.py:1 'Never export bodies, prompts...'; observability.py:22-28 disables httpx/azure_sdk auto-instrumentation; only http.request spans exist (39-50); topic_conversations/service.py:236-241 history stores no model/prompt_version/tokens; writing.py returns an unpersisted dict; benchmarks/language/harness.py:39-46,116-120 uses its own generic prompt 'benchmark-v1', not propose_action_messages / messages_for / feedback_messages; benchmarks/language/README.md:13-15 dry runs are plumbing only
findings.detail: No telemetry shows per-feature model latency, tokens, attempts, validator rejections or fallback rates. There is no golden set for the production prompts (intent classification, rubric judgements, correction grounding), so neither prompt changes nor agent introduction can be measured. Episode ratings (StoryEpisode.rating) are stored but not used as an eval signal.
findings.recommendation: Add OpenTelemetry GenAI-style spans that carry only metadata: feature, prompt_version, deployment, input/output tokens, attempts, latency, validator outcome, reply_source. This fits the no-body rule. Extend benchmarks/language with per-feature case files that call the real message builders and validators, run them in CI against the fixture provider and on demand against Azure, and record the results in DECISIONS.md as the README already prescribes.

findings.title: No learner memory or profile shared across features
findings.evidence: practice/prompts.py:98,123 history[-6:]; topic_conversations/workflow.py:46 history[-2:]; coaching/service.py:292-293 sends only id/skill/title/basis/evidence_ids; writing.py:89-151 corrections not persisted; stories/service.py:230-237 is the only feature using learner data (saved words); docs/GO_LIVE.md:35-36 'no ... separate vector store'
findings.detail: No component remembers recurring error categories, weak grammar points, preferred topics or the learner's stated goal. That is why every interaction feels stateless. An agent without memory would add little over today's pipelines.

findings.title: Usage caps are sized for one or two calls per action
findings.evidence: infra/main.bicep:43-49 dailyModelCalls=80, dailyTokens=80000 (production defaults); config.py:125-128 200 calls/200k tokens locally; practice/turns.py:27-28 MODEL_CALLS_PER_TURN=2, TOKENS_PER_TURN_ESTIMATE=1800; docs/DECISIONS.md D-17 'A budget alert is not a hard currency cap.'
findings.detail: A tool-using agent with 3–5 rounds per message would exhaust 80 calls per day within a single study session. Reservations are hard-coded per feature rather than per run.
findings.recommendation: Add per-feature or per-run budget policies (max_steps, max_tokens) reserved up front through usage.reserve, raise caps deliberately for the agent features, and surface the remaining allowance in the agent UI. Fill the PricingEntry table so `estimated_cost` (usage/service.py:194-200) becomes real.

findings.title: Wrong place for agents: grading, progression, actions, scheduling, points
findings.evidence: docs/ENGINEERING.md:59-61 'Dates, availability, permissions, task completion, usage limits and submissions are decided in application code.'; docs/DECISIONS.md D-12 'The model interprets and phrases; it never decides.'; docs/LEARNING_AGENTS.md:53 'No helper awards a final-check pass, locks a stage or declares CEFR mastery.'; curriculum/service.py:3-4 'Models may propose language judgements, but cannot select a learner, replace an audio transcript or change objective marks.'; D-19 'Points reward doing and are never a judgement of the learner's Dutch.'
findings.recommendation: If agents are introduced, give them read-only tools plus narrowly scoped 'propose' tools whose effects go through the existing validators (for example, propose an activity id that is then validated). Never give them tools that write results, passes, points or schedules.

findings.title: Wrong place for agents: the per-turn interpretation hot path
findings.evidence: topic_conversations/workflow.py:95-96 a single complete_once with 400 tokens; docs/LEARNING_AGENTS.md:61-63 'A submitted conversation response uses one `complete_once` request with a 400-token output ceiling.'; tests/test_single_model_call.py:1 'New role invocations cannot silently multiply paid model requests.'; docs/VERIFICATION.md:42 live typed turn 0.9 s on gpt-4.1-mini
findings.detail: Interpreting a learner utterance is a classification task, and it is fast and cheap today. Wrapping it in an open tool loop would add latency and cost on every turn and make it non-deterministic, with no gain in understanding.
findings.recommendation: Keep interpret → validate as one bounded call. Put agentic behaviour beside it, in the study guide, the tutor Q&A or the writing coach, not inside it.

findings.title: Agent opportunity: multi-round writing and grammar tutor
findings.evidence: curriculum/writing.py:20 MAX_CORRECTIONS = 5, single pass, not persisted; feedback/service.py:128-131 at most three points per step; stories/service.py:461-490 translation is the only on-demand help in the reader
findings.detail: Learners get one-shot corrections with no follow-up. They cannot ask 'why?', request an exercise on the same rule, or have the app remember that they repeatedly confuse word order.

findings.title: Agent opportunity: writer self-checks before returning (story and video)
findings.evidence: stories/service.py:255-302 (at most 2 attempts, rewrite after validation); docs/VERIFICATION.md:42 the first live episode failed on sentence length; stories/validator.py:121-133 coverage(), 162-235 validate_draft()
findings.detail: The writer only learns about vocabulary and sentence-length problems after a full draft and a paid rewrite. Generation runs as a background job, so a few extra calls are tolerable.
findings.recommendation: Optionally expose validator functions as tools, for example `check_text(paragraphs)` returning coverage, unknown words and sentence lengths, so the writer can check itself before final output. Keep validate_draft as the final authority and keep the ≤2 final-draft budget, or explicitly revise D-18 ('two model calls per episode at most').

findings.title: Background job lease is shorter than an LLM call, and the job loop is single-threaded
findings.evidence: config.py:137 job_lease_seconds=60 vs config.py:69,73 chat_timeout_seconds=120 and chat_max_attempts=3; jobs/service.py:84-156 has no lease heartbeat; jobs/service.py:167-201 one JobLoop thread processes jobs serially; docs/STORY_ENGINE.md:90-91 'A local 8B model takes one to three minutes per episode'; infra/main.bicep:376 minReplicas=maxReplicas=1
findings.detail: A long writer call can exceed its lease. The at-most-once 'generating → failed interrupted' claim stops a duplicate paid call but can fail a healthy job if a second worker claims it. Story, video and review generation also block render polling and each other. Longer agent runs would make this worse.
findings.recommendation: Add lease heartbeat or extension around provider calls, or set the lease longer than the worst-case call budget. Consider a separate worker container or a concurrency of more than one for LLM jobs before running agent work in jobs.

findings.title: LangGraph is a dependency used only for fixed linear pipelines
findings.evidence: pyproject 'langgraph>=1.0,<2'; practice/workflow.py:123-131 and topic_conversations/workflow.py:118-126 use START→a→b→c→END with no conditional edges, ToolNode or checkpointer; practice/workflow.py:151-157 compiles the graph on every turn
findings.detail: The framework that would host a real agent (conditional routing, tool nodes, persisted state) is already installed but none of its agent features are used.
findings.recommendation: If agents are adopted, use LangGraph for the agent loop: conditional edges, tool nodes wrapping domain functions, and a PostgreSQL checkpointer for agent state. Compile graphs once at module load. Otherwise consider plain functions and drop the dependency.

findings.title: Concurrency semaphore is per model instance and held during backoff
findings.evidence: providers/registry.py:159-160 builds separate chat and chat_strong instances; chat_openai_compatible.py:105 BoundedSemaphore per instance; chat_openai_compatible.py:188-242 the `with self._semaphore` block includes time.sleep backoff
findings.detail: Effective concurrency can reach 2× MAX_CONCURRENT_MODEL_CALLS against the same Azure deployment when no strong model exists. A retrying call keeps its slot while it sleeps.
findings.recommendation: Share a semaphore per endpoint/deployment and release it during backoff sleeps.

findings.title: Writing corrections are neither idempotent nor persisted

areas.area: Web app architecture and code quality (apps/web: Next.js 16 / React 19 front end, BFF proxy, client libs, styling, i18n, a11y, tests)
areas.overview:
apps/web ("dlp-web" 0.2.0) uses Next 16.3.5, React/React-DOM 19.3.0, TypeScript 5.9.3 in strict mode, ESLint 9.39 with eslint-config-next 16.3.5 (core-web-vitals + typescript), jose 6.2.12, @fontsource-variable DM Sans + Vazirmatn, Playwright 1.56.0 and @axe-core/playwright 4.13. Those versions come from package.json and package-lock. There is no UI library, animation library, data-fetching library, i18n library, CSS framework or formatter. `server-only` is imported but is not in package.json or the lockfile.

**Request path.** The browser only calls the same-origin `/api/*`. `app/api/[...path]/route.ts` is a Node-runtime catch-all BFF. For each request it:
- picks the request id;
- resolves the principal with `lib/server/identity.ts::resolvePrincipal` (a localhost-only fixture in development, or Azure Easy Auth `X-MS-CLIENT-PRINCIPAL` headers);
- enforces CSRF (`X-Requested-With: fetch` on unsafe methods, plus Sec-Fetch-Site and Origin);
- signs a 60-second HS256 assertion (`lib/server/assertion.ts::issueAssertion`: iss dlp-web, aud dlp-api, jti);
- forwards an allow-list of headers to `API_INTERNAL_URL` with a 6 MB body cap;
- streams the upstream body back.

`proxy.ts` is Next 16's renamed middleware. It sets a per-request CSP nonce (`script-src 'nonce' 'strict-dynamic'`, `connect-src 'self'`, `font-src 'self'`), `no-store` caching and HSTS in production. `next.config.ts` adds the security headers and an opt-in `output: standalone`. The Dockerfile is a two-stage node:22-alpine build that runs as a non-root user.

**Rendering and data.** `app/layout.tsx` is `force-dynamic` (needed for the nonce). It wraps everything in the client `LanguageProvider` and `AppShell`. Every route `page.tsx` is a 4–11 line async server component that only awaits params and renders one client component. 41 of 42 components are `"use client"`; only `Icon.tsx` is not. There is no server-side data fetching, no `loading.tsx`, no Suspense or streaming, no Server Actions and no `generateMetadata`.

Each feature component fetches on mount with `useEffect` + `AbortController` + `useState`, using `lib/client/api.ts` (`apiFetch`/`apiJson`/`ApiError`/`newRequestId`). `apiFetch` also fires a `dlp:connectivity` window event, which `ConnectionBanner` consumes. Shared cache, deduplication and invalidation do not exist. Polling is hand-rolled with `setTimeout` in TodayHome, VideoLibrary and ContentReviewQueue. Retries are `attempt`/`revision` counters. Stale-response guards use a "result keyed by JSON.stringify(params)" pattern, chosen to satisfy the project rule "no state-setting inside effect bodies" (docs/ENGINEERING.md:98).

**State.** State is local `useState`, with up to 24 hooks in one component. Cross-cutting state uses module singletons with `useSyncExternalStore`:
- the language mode in localStorage;
- `PhraseAudioController`;
- the `audio-focus` recording lock.

A React context (`lib/client/navigation.ts`) lets steps register a leave-guard. AppShell intercepts link clicks so writing autosave finishes before navigation. Drafts, test attempts, conversations and read-marks persist in sessionStorage/localStorage under `taalstudio.*` keys. The concurrency engineering is careful: idempotent request ids reused on retry, `DraftSaver` serial writes, `MicrophoneRequestGate`, a single audio focus, and focus moved after commit.

**Types.** Types are hand-written and scattered:
- `lib/types.ts` (header says "release 0.1"; covers missions and practice);
- `lib/client/{curriculum,topics,learning-agents,stories,videos}.ts`;
- many inline component types.

`LearningCopy` is defined in a component (`LanguageSupport.tsx`) and imported by lib files. There are three different multilingual shapes. FastAPI exposes `/openapi.json` only in development, and its routes return untyped `dict` with no `response_model`, so generating types from OpenAPI would yield empty response schemas today.

**i18n.** Interface chrome is hard-coded Dutch JSX. Translatable learning text uses `<LearningText text={{nl,en,fa}}/>`, with 51 inline literal objects spread across components and no message catalogue. Persian RTL is applied per span with `lang="fa" dir="rtl"` and the `.fa` class. `<html lang="nl">` is fixed. The support mode defaults to nl-en on the server, so it flashes for Persian users. The formal register (u/uw) appears in 9 files, while the rest uses je/jij.

**Styling.** Ten global plain-CSS files (~2,845 lines, ~105 KB) are all imported in the layout, so they load on every route. `:root` tokens are redefined four times with conflicting values:
- globals.css: green accent;
- design.css: another green;
- learning.css: blue accent, which wins by import order;
- stories.css: warm tones.

`.button` is defined three times. The CSS uses 356 unique hex colours, ~61 font-size declarations of 7–10px, one @keyframes, no dark mode and about 35 apparently unused legacy classes. docs/ENGINEERING.md:276 records a deliberate "restrained navy and blue" palette.

**Component size.** `wc -l` understates size because JSX is written as very long single lines; byte size is the better measure.

| Component | Lines | Bytes | Longest line (chars) |
|---|---|---|---|
| SpeakingStep | 464 | 20.8 KB | — |
| SkillTopicPractice | 186 | 19.6 KB | — |
| TopicConversation | 189 | 19.0 KB | — |
| LearningLibrary | 128 | 15.5 KB | — |
| LessonShell | 371 | 15.4 KB | — |
| EpisodeReader | 168 | 14.8 KB | — |
| TodayHome | 173 | 13.9 KB | — |
| CurriculumLesson | 100 | 13.8 KB | 1,597 |
| CurriculumTest | 115 | 13.5 KB | 3,274 |
| CurriculumControls | 163 | 12.5 KB | — |
| VideoPlayer | 162 | 12.1 KB | — |
| VideoLibrary | 142 | 10.4 KB | — |

All components total 5,130 lines and 323 KB. design.css alone is 1,711 lines.

**Information architecture.** The shell has nine nav items, six on mobile. Overlapping features: a generated serial (/verhalen) versus a static "Story Time" inside /learn; SRS words (/woorden) versus a stage word bank; missions versus topic conversations. Level is chosen in four places with different defaults. There is no onboarding.

**Tests.**
- 6 node:test unit files over pure lib modules (run with `--experimental-strip-types`).
- 18 Playwright specs with ~80 tests: Chromium only, 1 worker, real API stack via `scripts/run.py e2e`, many `page.route` mocks.
- Axe on 5 top screens and the mission lesson.
- Screenshots are attached but never compared.

`tsconfig` excludes `tests`, so specs are not typechecked. There are no component or hook tests. CI runs lint, typecheck, unit tests and e2e.

findings.title: Server components unused: every page is a client island that fetches on mount (no RSC data, no Suspense/loading.tsx)
findings.evidence: app/page.tsx:4-5, app/leerpad/page.tsx:4-5, app/videos/page.tsx:4-5 (thin wrappers); 41/42 components start with "use client" (only components/Icon.tsx is not); TodayHome.tsx:27-30, CurriculumPath.tsx:15-19, VideoLibrary.tsx:62-65 fetch in useEffect; no loading.tsx files exist; layout.tsx:37 force-dynamic
findings.detail: Every first paint shows a text placeholder ('Je dag voorbereiden…', 'Je leerpad laden…' – class .path-loading), then a browser→Next→FastAPI round trip. The server already knows the principal and can sign assertions, but no server-side fetch helper exists. No skeletons or streaming, and dynamic routes have no metadata (learn/[stageId]/page.tsx, missions/[missionId]/page.tsx, speech-check/page.tsx lack titles).
findings.recommendation: Add lib/server/api.ts. It should read headers() in server components, call resolvePrincipal + issueAssertion, and fetch FastAPI directly. Fetch initial data in async page.tsx and pass it into client islands as props/initialData. Add per-segment loading.tsx skeletons and Suspense boundaries, plus generateMetadata for episode/video/stage titles. Keep the /api proxy for mutations, audio and polling.

findings.title: Ad-hoc fetching with no cache, dedupe or invalidation; repeated endpoints, waterfalls and three hand-rolled pollers
findings.evidence: 'curriculum' catalog fetched separately by CurriculumPath.tsx:17, CurriculumProgress.tsx:19, CurriculumTest.tsx:43, ContentReviewQueue.tsx:28; LessonShell.tsx:45-56 runs mission→progress→sessions→each session detail sequentially; lib/client/learning.ts:38 always fetches hard-coded 'missions/appointment-change' (used by Settings/Progress only for profile); polling in TodayHome.tsx:10-37, VideoLibrary.tsx:11-72, ContentReviewQueue.tsx:62-66; StoryLibrary.tsx:18-22 shows pending episodes but never polls; UsagePanel.tsx:38-42 has no AbortController; topic-conversations catalog fetched in both TopicConversation.tsx:21 and :36
findings.detail: Each component reimplements loading/error/retry/abort/stale-guard state. That causes duplicated network traffic, inconsistent freshness (e.g. after saving a word, Today's counts are stale until reload) and large components. The key-matching pattern (SkillTopicPractice.tsx:32-34, LearningLibrary.tsx:59-60) exists only to satisfy lint rules that a query library handles natively.
findings.recommendation: Adopt TanStack Query v5 (or SWR) over apiJson. Use typed query-key factories per domain (curriculum, today, words, stories, videos, topics, coach), refetchInterval while status is queued/generating/rendering, invalidateQueries after mutations, and useMutation with optimistic updates (word save, rating, grade). Hydrate from RSC initialData. Parallelise LessonShell.loadMission with Promise.all.

findings.title: Hand-written, fragmented API types with no contract with FastAPI
findings.evidence: lib/types.ts:1 ('release 0.1'); types also in lib/client/curriculum.ts:4-31, topics.ts:5-27, learning-agents.ts:4-30, stories.ts:5-43, videos.ts:6-23; inline types in LearningLibrary.tsx:12-16, WritingCoach.tsx:9-10, UsagePanel.tsx:7-20, StatusPanel.tsx:8-13, SpeechCheck.tsx:10-18, CurriculumProgress.tsx:10-11, ContentReviewQueue.tsx:9-12; LearningCopy defined in components/LanguageSupport.tsx:6 and imported by lib/client/curriculum.ts:1, topics.ts:1, learning-agents.ts:1; apps/api/src/dlp/main.py:75-77 (openapi only in development); API routes return `-> dict` with no response_model (e.g. routes_missions.py:49, routes_progress.py:28)
findings.detail: Drift between API and UI is caught only by e2e. Multilingual text has three shapes: LocalizedText {nl,en?,fa,review_status} in types.ts:6, LearningCopy {nl,en?,fa?}, and flat meaning_en/meaning_fa or text_nl/text_fa/text_en fields in GlossaryItem, WordItem and FeedbackPoint. lib imports a type from a component, which inverts the dependency direction.
findings.recommendation: Add Pydantic response models to FastAPI routes, export openapi.json in CI, and generate TS with openapi-typescript (+ openapi-fetch typed client) into lib/api/schema.d.ts. Move LearningCopy/LocalizedText into lib/i18n or lib/types. Optionally validate at the boundary with zod. Short term: consolidate all hand types under lib/api/<domain>.ts.

findings.title: CSS architecture is a stack of global overrides: 4 conflicting :root token blocks, triple .button, 356 hex colours, tiny type
findings.evidence: globals.css:1-18 (--accent #0b5d4b), design.css:2-17 (--accent #225b49, --radius 18px), learning.css:2-12 (--accent #2455b5, --radius 16px — wins by import order layout.tsx:10-19), stories.css:2-12 (warm + tone-1..6); .button at globals.css:144, design.css:409, learning.css:37; .card at globals.css:101 and design.css:855; body font-size 14px (design.css:19) then 15px (learning.css:13); font-size 7–10px declared ~61 times (e.g. .brand-caption 8px design.css:113 & learning.css:19, .eyebrow 10px learning.css:36); only one @keyframes (stories.css writing-dots); no prefers-color-scheme; ~35 apparently unused classes (mission-hero, art-*, hero-*, skill-card*, site-header, site-nav, studio-card, stage-locked…); all ~105KB CSS loaded on every route
findings.detail: Visual identity changed through successive layers ('restrained navy and blue', docs/ENGINEERING.md:276) instead of edits, so tokens are untrustworthy and colour is ad hoc. Very little motion or feedback styling exists, which matches the owner's 'boring/limited' impression. Skill colours exist as data (components/LearningOverview.tsx:7-42 sage/sand/lilac/peach, used only by ProgressOverview .icon-tile), and episode cover gradients exist (stories.css tone-1..6), but neither forms a system.
findings.recommendation: Create one token source covering colour scales, semantic tokens, per-skill accent tokens (reading/listening/speaking/writing), a type scale in rem with a minimum of 12px, spacing, radius, shadow and motion durations/easings, plus a dark theme. Move components to CSS Modules (or Tailwind v4 @theme) and delete override layers and dead classes. Build primitives (Button, Card, Badge, Tabs, ProgressRing/Bar, Skeleton, Toast, Dialog, Chip) and add purposeful motion (Motion for React or CSS View Transitions) respecting reduced-motion. Update docs/ENGINEERING.md:276.

findings.title: God-components with multi-thousand-character JSX lines and no formatter
findings.evidence: CurriculumTest.tsx:102 is a single 3,274-char line; CurriculumLesson.tsx:81-95 lines up to 1,597 chars; byte sizes: SpeakingStep 20.8KB/464 lines, SkillTopicPractice 19.6KB/186 lines (24 useState refs), TopicConversation 19.0KB/189 lines (17 useState, 7 useEffect), LearningLibrary 15.5KB (24 useState refs), LessonShell 15.4KB/371, EpisodeReader 14.8KB, TodayHome 13.9KB, CurriculumLesson 13.8KB, CurriculumTest 13.5KB, CurriculumControls 12.5KB, VideoPlayer 12.1KB; no prettier/biome/editorconfig in repo; 36 inline style={{}} occurrences
findings.detail: Line counts hide the real size. Flows such as the final test (intro/in-progress/locked/results) and the conversation (restore/start/active/409/finished) are encoded as boolean soups across many useState hooks, which is hard to change safely during a UX redesign.
findings.recommendation: Add Prettier (or Biome) and reformat. Split by view state into subcomponents (e.g. TestIntro/TestWorkspace/TestResults; ConversationSetup/ConversationThread/Composer/Summary). Move flow state into useReducer or a small state machine, and extract hooks (useTopicDraft, useConversationSession, usePolling).

findings.evidence: Multiple-choice UIs: CurriculumControls.tsx:12-19, QuestionList.tsx:26-128, EpisodeReader.tsx:147-168, VideoPlayer.tsx:141-162. Recorder UIs: SpeakingStep.tsx:333-346 (hold), SpeechCheck.tsx:109-118 (hold), CurriculumControls.tsx:96-163 (click toggle), EpisodeReader.tsx:101-126 (toggle). Stage lists: practiceStages learning-agents.ts:31, stageLabels stories.ts:45, stageLabel() curriculum.ts:35. Paginated filtered list: SkillTopicPractice.tsx:20-69, LearningLibrary.tsx WordLibrary/StoryTime; pager x3 (LearningLibrary.tsx:50, SkillTopicPractice.tsx:66, ContentReviewQueue.tsx:127). Cross-component imports of helpers: EpisodeReader→TodayHome.coverClass (EpisodeReader.tsx:8), VideoPlayer→VideoLibrary.failureCopy (VideoPlayer.tsx:8), ListeningStep/WritingStep import StepProps from ReadingStep
findings.detail: The same learning interaction looks and behaves differently across features: hold-to-talk versus click-to-record, and four different answer-check visuals. This contributes to the inconsistent, confusing feel and multiplies redesign effort.
findings.recommendation: Build a shared learning-kit: <ChoiceQuestion/> (with instant animated feedback), <Recorder variant>, <AudioButton/> (PhraseAudio), <Glossary/> (save-to-words), <ComprehensionQuiz/>, <RatingBar/>, <PagedList/>, a single errorMessage(ApiError) and a single skills/stages registry in lib/domain.

findings.title: No real i18n layer; interface language fixed to Dutch, mixed register, SSR language flash
findings.evidence: Hard-coded Dutch chrome in AppShell.tsx:14-46 and every component; 51 inline `text={{ nl: ...` literal objects across components; layout.tsx:41 <html lang="nl"> fixed with no dir switching; LanguageSupport.tsx:24 server snapshot 'nl-en' (Persian users re-render after hydration); RTL only via per-span lang/dir (8 dir="rtl" occurrences) and .fa in globals.css:203-208; formal 'u/uw' in 9 files (SpeakingStep.tsx:151,233; ConnectionBanner.tsx:45-48; FeedbackPanel.tsx:66; WritingStep.tsx:163,206; MissionCatalog.tsx:26; app/missions/page.tsx:6...) vs informal 'je' elsewhere; English label 'Story Time' in Dutch UI (CurriculumLesson.tsx:24,82)
findings.detail: The support-language switch only adds translations under learning content; navigation, buttons and instructions remain Dutch. This likely explains why a beginner (pre-A1) 'feels confused at the start'. Strings cannot be reviewed or edited centrally.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a typed message catalogue (next-intl or a small t() with nl/en/fa JSON). Separate 'interface language' from 'support languages'. Persist the preference in a cookie so the server renders the correct lang/dir and the html dir can switch for a Persian interface. Use CSS logical properties, and pick one register (je).

findings.title: No onboarding; fragmented information architecture and four independent level selectors
findings.evidence: No onboarding/placement code (grep for onboard/welkom/placement/intake: none). 9 nav items AppShell.tsx:14-46. Level chosen in TodayHome.tsx:139-144 (story level via stories.level), PracticeCoach.tsx:11-16 (localStorage 'taalstudio.practice-stage', default 'a1'), VideoLibrary.tsx:57,63 (default_stage), CurriculumPath.tsx:20 (first unpassed stage → pre-a1). Overlaps: /verhalen serial vs Story Time (LearningLibrary.tsx:83-128), /woorden SRS vs WordLibrary/VocabularyRecall, /missions vs topic conversations (TopicConversation.tsx)
findings.detail: The learner has no single 'my level / my goal / today's plan' model on the client. Home ('/') centres the generated serial, while the structured curriculum lives under 'Mijn leerpad', so the path from day 1 to progress is not visible.
findings.recommendation: Add a server-backed learner profile (level, goal, minutes/day, support language) captured by a first-run onboarding flow (optionally a placement mini-check). Derive all level selectors from it. Consolidate the nav to about 4–5 destinations (Vandaag, Leren/Pad, Oefenen, Woorden, Profiel). Make Today a unified daily plan mixing curriculum steps, review, story and conversation.

findings.title: Developer/operational details leak into learner UI
findings.evidence: ConnectionBanner.tsx:48 tells learners to run `python scripts/run.py dev`; TodayHome.tsx:90-91 and StoryLibrary.tsx:54 / VideoLibrary.tsx:45 render raw failure_reasons codes; SpeakingStep.tsx:324-330 shows 'audio: {x-audio-label}'; EpisodeReader.tsx:79 and VideoPlayer.tsx:99 show model/provider names; TodayHome.tsx:90 references 'Instellingen › Technische ondersteuning'
findings.detail: These make the product feel like a dev tool and add cognitive load.
findings.recommendation: Gate diagnostics behind APP_ENV !== 'production' or an admin flag (admin_bypass already exists in CurriculumCatalog). Replace them with friendly, action-oriented learner copy.

findings.title: Accessibility gaps in recording controls and typography
findings.evidence: talkButtonHandlers handles pointer + Space only, no Enter/click path (recorder.ts:139-160) used by SpeakingStep.tsx:339 and SpeechCheck.tsx:114, while CurriculumRecorder uses click toggle (CurriculumControls.tsx:159-162); ~61 font-size declarations ≤10px incl. 7px and 8px; 115 role=status/alert/aria-live occurrences (many on loading text); TodayHome.tsx:111 empty <li> day dots conveyed only via title/colour; emoji 👍/👎 in status text (VideoLibrary.tsx:43, StoryLibrary.tsx:53)
findings.detail: Hold-to-talk is hard for switch, screen-reader and some touch users, and is inconsistent with other recorders. Tiny text undermines readability despite axe passing.
findings.recommendation: Use one recorder pattern: a click-to-start/stop toggle, with hold-to-talk as an optional enhancement, a visible timer and level meter. Set a minimum 12px (0.75rem) type and reserve live regions for results and errors. Give day dots visually-hidden text.

findings.title: Testing gaps: no component tests, e2e untyped, Chromium-only, screenshots not asserted, copy-coupled locators
findings.evidence: tsconfig.json:38-41 excludes tests (tsc --noEmit skips e2e); unit tests only for lib (tests/unit/*.test.mjs, 6 files, node --experimental-strip-types); playwright.config.ts:15-17 workers 1, retries 0, chromium only, tablet/phone projects limited to lesson|steps (lines 35-36); design.spec.ts:62-65 attaches screenshots without toHaveScreenshot; e2e uses 413 getByRole/Text/Label (mostly Dutch copy) + 165 getByTestId + class locators (e.g. '.conversation-status', '.practice-feedback'); page.route mocks in 12 specs (stories 6, videos 7, library-writing 7, skill-topics 6, curriculum 6)
findings.detail: A UX/copy redesign will break many e2e tests while giving no fast feedback at component level. Untested logic includes LessonShell.mergeDetail, apiJson error mapping, useRecorder, topicHref and countWords.
findings.recommendation: Add Vitest + React Testing Library (+ MSW, reusing the e2e mock payloads) for components and hooks. Include tests in a typecheck tsconfig. Add toHaveScreenshot visual baselines for key screens and Firefox/WebKit smoke projects. Prefer role and testid locators, and centralise copy so tests can import message keys.

findings.title: Proxy does not propagate client aborts or bound upstream time
findings.evidence: app/api/[...path]/route.ts:116 `fetch(target, { method, headers, body, cache: 'no-store', redirect: 'manual' })` — no signal; request body fully buffered (line 108); only GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE exported (131-145)
findings.detail: Client-side AbortController cancellations (used extensively) stop at the Next tier, so FastAPI keeps running LLM/STT work for abandoned requests. A hung API holds Node requests indefinitely.
findings.recommendation: Pass `signal: AbortSignal.any([request.signal, AbortSignal.timeout(N)])` (longer N for generation routes), map timeouts to 504, and consider forwarding Last-Event-ID/Accept for future SSE agent streams.

findings.title: Sign-out does not clear all learner-scoped browser storage (docs claim it does)
findings.evidence: AccountSettings.tsx:20 clears only 'taalstudio.draft.', 'taalstudio.test.', 'taalstudio.stories.'; other keys exist: 'taalstudio.topic-draft.' (SkillTopicPractice.tsx:85), 'taalstudio.conversation.' (TopicConversation.tsx:48), 'taalstudio.practice-stage.' (PracticeCoach.tsx:12), 'taalstudio.language-support' (LanguageSupport.tsx:7); docs/ENGINEERING.md:269-270 says drafts are cleared on sign-out
findings.detail: Topic drafts and conversation drafts can survive sign-out in the same tab.
findings.recommendation: Centralise storage keys in one module (e.g. lib/client/storage.ts) and clear by the 'taalstudio.' prefix, keeping only non-personal preferences.

findings.title: Hard-coded values and content inside components
findings.evidence: WritingStep.tsx:231 WritingCoach stageId="a2" for every mission; 'De Lindestraat' hard-coded TodayHome.tsx:51,165 and EpisodeReader.tsx:38 although series.title/town come from API; CommunicationCoach.tsx:7-11 learning phrases embedded in code (bypasses content/ pipeline and review labels); lib/client/learning.ts:38 fixed mission id
findings.detail: These make the app harder to extend: another series, mission CEFR levels, or reviewed content.
findings.recommendation: Derive the stage from mission.cefr_target, use series data, and move coaching phrases into content/ JSON with review_status.

findings.title: Modern React/Next capabilities unused (perf & UX polish)
findings.evidence: No next/dynamic/lazy (grep), CurriculumLesson.tsx:4-13 eagerly imports WordLibrary, StoryTime, AlphabetPractice, SkillTopicPractice, WritingCoach, CommunicationCoach; fonts via @fontsource CSS imports (layout.tsx:7-8) rather than next/font; no reactCompiler in next.config.ts; no useOptimistic/useActionState/useTransition; PhraseAudio.tsx:10-31 creates a module-level singleton with side effects at import
findings.detail: The learn route ships every section's code up front. Word saves, ratings and grades wait for a round trip before UI feedback.
findings.recommendation: Lazy-load section panels, use next/font for preload and size-adjust, consider enabling the React Compiler, and use useOptimistic for save/rate/grade with instant animated feedback. Measure with @next/bundle-analyzer.

constraints: Browser must never call FastAPI directly. All browser traffic goes through same-origin /api with X-Requested-With: fetch on unsafe methods, and the proxy signs the assertion (docs/DECISIONS.md D-03/D-04; route.ts:46-104).

CSP from proxy.ts:8-20: script-src nonce + strict-dynamic; font-src/connect-src/img-src 'self' (+data:/blob:); style-src allows 'unsafe-inline'. External CDNs (Google Fonts, hosted Lottie/animations, analytics) need CSP changes, and third-party scripts need the nonce. Root layout must stay dynamic for per-request nonces (layout.tsx:37, ENGINEERING.md:28-29).
Project lint rule: no state-setting inside effect bodies (docs/ENGINEERING.md:98; eslint-config-next 16 react-hooks rules). New code must respect it; a query library would ease this.
Primary app navigation must wait for writing autosave (D-17; AppShell.tsx:71-103, lib/client/navigation.ts). Any new shell/router must keep the leave-guard.

No fictitious scores, certificates or pronunciation/accent scores; typed input never counts as speaking practice; read-aloud compares words only (D-16, D-17, D-20). Gamification (points/streaks/XP) must stay evidence-based and honest.

Audio is never autoplayed or prefetched; playback requires an explicit click and one speaker at a time via audio-focus (unit tests phrase-audio.test.mjs:29, e2e phrase-audio.spec.ts, library-writing.spec.ts:92).
Unreviewed or generated content must stay visibly labelled (ContentLabel, course-note copy); synthetic voices and the virtual presenter must be labelled.
Dutch always remains the practice language; support lines are English and/or Persian with lang/dir set; Persian uses RTL and the Vazirmatn font (ENGINEERING.md:267-270).
Idempotent request ids must be reused on retry for session/turn/test/story/video creation (LessonShell.tsx:96, SpeakingStep.tsx:148-185, CurriculumTest.tsx:69).
Docs currently mandate a 'restrained navy and blue' design (ENGINEERING.md:276). A more colourful redesign is a conscious revision and must update the docs.

E2E tests are tightly coupled to Dutch visible copy (413 role/text/label locators), 83 data-testid attributes and some CSS classes. UI/copy changes require coordinated test updates; keep data-testids stable where possible.

Unit tests run with node --experimental-strip-types (Node >= 22.6, package.json engines). lib modules imported by them must stay free of React/Next imports and path aliases (they import ../../lib/...ts directly).
Production identity is Azure Container Apps Easy Auth headers; sign-out is /.auth/logout (AccountSettings.tsx:90). Onboarding must work behind Easy Auth, with no custom login.
Container build uses NEXT_OUTPUT=standalone (Dockerfile:8-10); no public/ directory exists today.
open_questions: How `import "server-only"` resolves: it is not in package.json or package-lock (presumably Next's built-in alias); not verified by building.
Actual client bundle sizes and route-level JS/CSS weight were not measured (no build was run, per read-only rules).

Whether the API team will add Pydantic response models so OpenAPI-generated TS types become meaningful (routes currently return untyped dict); also whether /openapi.json can be exported in CI (it is enabled only in development, main.py:75-77).
Whether the owner wants English/Persian as a full interface language (navigation, buttons) or only as support lines under Dutch content.
Whether a server-side learner profile endpoint (level, goals, preferred support language) exists or is planned in the API; the web currently derives the level in four different places.
The ~35 'unused' CSS classes come from a heuristic grep (dynamic class names such as tone-N, grade-*, kind-*, status-* were excluded manually); confirm before deleting.
Whether streaming (SSE) responses from FastAPI are planned for agent/tutor features; the proxy streams bodies, but apiJson consumes only complete JSON.
Whether Firefox/Safari (iOS) support matters to the owner; recording MIME candidates include audio/mp4, but e2e runs on Chromium only.
Real-world latency of LLM story/video generation that drives the 5–6s polling cadence (TodayHome POLL_MS 5000, VideoLibrary 6000) and the stalled-state UX.
