strengths: The episode loop is a genuinely good comprehensible-input design: per-paragraph TTS, English line under each paragraph, on-demand Persian translation, read-aloud with recognised and missed words, a glossary that feeds an SM-2 word bank, evidence-backed questions and an A/B choice that steers the next episode (EpisodeReader.tsx:36-82, 85-168).

Today already has the bones of a daily plan: a server-computed next_step, streak, 20-point daily goal, 14-day history, due-word count, and video readiness in one call (routes_stories.py:60-89; TodayHome.tsx:48-55).
Pre-generation keeps one unread episode buffered, so after the first visit the next episode is usually ready when the app opens (stories/service.py:178-189).
There is a warm, colourful visual vocabulary in stories.css (six gradient cover tones, a warm streak ring, gradient goal bar) that the rest of the app does not yet use (stories.css:3-11, 49-70).

Trilingual content infrastructure already exists: LearningCopy {nl,en,fa} everywhere in curriculum, topics and stage titles; Persian has proper lang/dir and the Vazirmatn font (LanguageSupport.tsx:35-43; layout.tsx:7-8).

There is a beginner-ready, LLM-free day-one activity in AlphabetPractice: letter names, a listen-and-pick quiz and kat/maan contrasts, fully trilingual (AlphabetPractice.tsx:9-36). VocabularyRecall offers 5-word recall rounds (VocabularyRecall.tsx:10-40).
The personalised practice coach (/coach/plan) already returns 3 suggestions with a trilingual reason per item (PracticeCoach.tsx:49-53; learning-agents.ts:25-30).
Robust states: every list has loading, error and retry. Navigation is guarded while recording or saving (AppShell.tsx:71-103). An accessibility gate in e2e enforces axe WCAG 2.1 AA at three widths.
Honest by design: no fictitious scores or certificates, and no pronunciation score (DECISIONS.md D-17, D-19, D-20). This is a strength to keep, but its presentation is currently noisy.

findings.title: No onboarding: the first visit lands on a waiting screen with no explanation of the method
findings.evidence: app/page.tsx:4-5 renders TodayHome with no first-run branch. A grep of the repo for onboard/welcome/placement/intake finds nothing in apps/web. Learner model has no level/goal fields (identity/models.py:13-27). GET /today queues episode 1 on the first call (stories/service.py:370-372, 178-189; README.md:91-93: "the first episode is queued on the first visit and takes one to three minutes"). The first screen is then TodayHome.tsx:53 headline "Je volgende aflevering wordt geschreven." plus TodayHome.tsx:70-71 "De schrijver is bezig… Dit duurt meestal één tot drie minuten." Polling: 5 s × 48 = 4 min (TodayHome.tsx:10-11, 33-37), then "Het duurt langer dan verwacht. Vernieuwen" (:73). Fallback copy at :95: "Je eerste aflevering komt eraan. Vernieuw zo meteen deze pagina." The only description of the method is the subtitle at :60, "Eén aflevering, een paar woorden, één gesprek. Twintig minuten volstaan." The 6-step learning loop in LEARNING_DESIGN.md:8-15 is never shown to the learner.
findings.detail: A brand-new adult beginner gets no welcome and is never asked their level, goal or support language. Nobody tells them how stories, word review, the leerpad, conversations and the eindtoets fit together. The very first thing they see is a model writing in the background, surrounded by zero-valued stats. The docs/previews screenshots show the ready fixture state, so this first-visit experience is invisible in the docs.
findings.recommendation:
Add a first-run flow, either as a /welkom route or a TodayHome branch. Show it when the learner has no profile and no learning_days. Three short steps, each glossed via LearningText:
1. Choose support language (EN / FA / both). Persist it server-side via the existing Learner.support_language column plus a small PATCH /me endpoint.
2. Self-placement in plain words, e.g. "I know no Dutch", "I know some words", "I can have simple conversations", mapped to pre-a1 / a1 / a2. Store it as one learner level and also call POST /stories/level.
3. Daily minutes (5 / 10 / 20), which sets the goal target.
End with a 4-card "How Taalstudio works" explainer (Read/listen → Save words → Review → Speak & write → Check), using the existing skills array icons and colours. While episode 1 is being written, start the learner on a 3-minute activity: AlphabetPractice for pre-A1, or a VocabularyRecall round from the stage library for A1. Pre-queue episode 1 at the start of onboarding so it is usually ready when onboarding ends.

findings.title: No single 'my level': three to four level controls disagree
findings.evidence:
The level is set in four disconnected places:
- Stories: default_stage maps pre-a1 to "a1" (stories/service.py:55-58). Today shows a select "Niveau van de verhalen" (TodayHome.tsx:139-144). The screenshot today-desktop.png shows "AFLEVERING 1 · A1 · 127 WOORDEN" for a new learner.
- Leerpad: suggests the first unpassed stage, i.e. pre-A1 (CurriculumPath.tsx:20, 29: "VOORGESTELD STARTPUNT").
- PracticeCoach: its own "Mijn oefenniveau" select in localStorage, default a1 (PracticeCoach.tsx:11-16, 46).
- Videos: a "Niveau" select defaulting to series.stage_id (VideoLibrary.tsx:63, 114; videos/service.py:472).
Curriculum POLICY open_stage_access=True (curriculum/service.py:33-38) and the copy "Alle niveaus zijn open. Kies je startpunt" (CurriculumPath.tsx:33).
findings.detail: The learner never states a level. The app guesses differently per module and shows CEFR codes (pre-A1, A1, …) without explanation. A true beginner reads 127-word A1 stories on Today while the leerpad says they should start at pre-A1 letters and first words.
findings.recommendation: Introduce one server-side learner level, set during onboarding and editable in Settings. Show it as a header chip, e.g. "Jouw niveau: A1 · Beginner" with an EN/FA gloss. Use it as the default for the story series, the PracticeCoach (drop its localStorage key), videos and the leerpad continue panel. Keep per-request overrides as an "Advanced" disclosure. Use plain-language level names with a one-line can-do statement from path.json title/description (e.g. pre-a1 "First words: welcome"). Promote the level automatically when the stage eindtoets passes; default_stage already reads passed stages.

findings.title: The interface is Dutch-only; support languages reach only content blocks
findings.evidence: layout.tsx:41 sets html lang="nl". Nav labels are plain Dutch strings (AppShell.tsx:14-46). The Today headline has no gloss (TodayHome.tsx:59). Buttons are Dutch-only: "Lees aflevering", "Schrijf dit", "Maak een video", "Toon de betekenis". So are the streak labels "dagen op rij / Beste reeks / Actieve dagen" (TodayHome.tsx:102-107) and the cast roles (TodayHome.tsx:149; series_view returns only name/role in Dutch, stories/service.py:84). LearningText is the only gloss mechanism (LanguageSupport.tsx:35-43). The mode defaults to nl-en in localStorage (LanguageSupport.tsx:9, 12-16), but the server default is support_language="fa" (identity/models.py:23); grep confirms no endpoint writes support_language. The switcher label is "Taalhulp / language" (LanguageSupport.tsx:48). Formality is inconsistent: "Uw oefenbibliotheek… uw eigen tempo" (missions/page.tsx:6), "Wat wilt u vandaag oefenen?" (MissionCatalog.tsx:26), "Uw werk blijft staan" (ConnectionBanner.tsx:45-48), coach notices in 'uw' (coaching/service.py:214, 218, 249, 328), "wat u zei" (SpeechCheck.tsx:139), and stage descriptions "Stel uzelf…" vs "je" everywhere else. English islands: "Story Time" (CurriculumLesson.tsx:24; LearningLibrary.tsx:118, 123).
findings.detail: An adult beginner whose support languages are English or Persian cannot read the controls that tell them what to do. The support language only appears under content paragraphs. Persian users get English by default. Mixing formal and informal address reads as unpolished.
findings.recommendation: Create a small UI-copy dictionary, e.g. lib/client/ui-copy.ts with LearningCopy entries per key, and a `<UiText k="nav.today"/>` helper built on LearningText (compact variant: a second line or tooltip under nav and button labels). Show the glosses by default for stages up to A2 and let them fade (setting: "Show translations of buttons"). Persist the support mode server-side and initialise from Learner.support_language. Give cast roles en/fa in the bible (or translate on the client from a fixed map). Standardise on 'je' across UI, coach notices and content descriptions. Rename "Story Time".

findings.title: Nine competing destinations with overlapping concepts and inconsistent names and icons
findings.evidence:
9 sidebar items, 6 on mobile (AppShell.tsx:14-46, 195-206). Missions ("Praktijkgesprekken") has no mobile flag (AppShell.tsx:21-26). The same destination has four names: nav "Praktijkgesprekken", mobile short "Oefenen", metadata "Oefenmissies" (missions/page.tsx:4), h1 "Uw oefenbibliotheek" (:6), and ProgressOverview h2 "Praktijkgesprekken" (ProgressOverview.tsx:22). Duplicated concepts:
- 'Verhalen' (generated serial, StoryLibrary) vs 'Story Time' (static library inside the leerpad, LearningLibrary.tsx:83-128).
- Nav 'Woorden' (personal SM-2 bank, WordReview) vs leerpad section 'Woorden' (static stage word library, CurriculumLesson.tsx:21, 87).
- Missions (LessonShell) vs topic conversations under Spreken (SkillTopicPractice.tsx:57, 165) vs CommunicationCoach.
Icons are inconsistent: Woorden=check and Leerpad=home in the nav, while Today's bottom links use chart for Leerpad and book for Praktijkgesprekken (AppShell.tsx:19-25 vs TodayHome.tsx:155-156). The breadcrumb "Leeromgeving > X" (AppShell.tsx:162-166) and sidebar label "JOUW LEEROMGEVING" (:125) add noise. LEARNING_DESIGN.md:45 states support tools should not add main navigation.
findings.detail: The learner cannot tell where the 'course' is. The structured path is the fifth nav item, and pages with the same name lead to different things. Today adds 6 more outbound links. The mental model becomes a set of separate apps rather than one method.
findings.recommendation:
Regroup the nav around 4-5 jobs, each with a glossed label:
1. Vandaag (today's session)
2. Leren (the path; stories, videos and topic tasks become lesson types inside it, or under one 'Lezen & kijken' hub)
3. Spreken / Oefenen (missions + topic conversations + Spraakstudio as a warm-up)
4. Woorden (personal bank only)
5. Voortgang
Move Instellingen to the profile menu. Rename the leerpad section 'Woorden' to 'Woordenschat van dit niveau' and fold Story Time into a 'Korte verhalen' tab of Verhalen, or retire it per STATUS.md:26-27. Use one icon per concept. Replace the breadcrumb with the level chip and today's progress. Update the e2e selectors listed in constraints.

findings.title: Today shows about 10 equal-weight regions instead of ONE next action with its benefit; next_step ignores the course
findings.evidence: next_step can only be read, choose, review, wait or explore, all computed from stories and words (routes_stories.py:66-76). Headlines (TodayHome.tsx:50-54): for 'review' the h1 says "N woorden wachten op je.", but the only CTA is the sidebar words card (:113-117). For 'explore': "Kies waar je vandaag mee begint." with no specific action. The page renders: episode card, streak card, words card, video card, wish form + level select, cast card + memory, and 3 bottom links (TodayHome.tsx:63-158). The subtitle promises "één gesprek" (:60), but Today offers no conversation. LEARNING_DESIGN.md:43 says "One visible next step". No card explains why an action helps; e.g. the words card says only "woorden om te herhalen".
findings.detail: The learner sees many options of similar visual weight, none framed as part of a session. The structured course (leerpad), speaking practice and the promised conversation are never the 'next step'. Benefits are never stated (why read, why review, why speak).
findings.recommendation:
Turn Today into a 'Je sessie van vandaag' stepper, built from the existing TodayPlan plus the curriculum and coach data:
1. Warm-up: review due words (or 5 starter words).
2. Read/listen: the episode, or a leerpad lesson step.
3. Speak: one topic conversation or mission step chosen from /coach/plan.
4. Wrap-up: save words / choose the next episode.
Each step shows minutes, points and a one-line trilingual benefit ("Herhalen op het juiste moment helpt je onthouden"). One primary button: "Start / Ga verder (±15 min)". Extend server next_step to include 'lesson' and 'speak'. Move the wish form, story level and cast to /verhalen, behind a 'Meer' disclosure on Today.

findings.title: Progress feedback is fragmented: course work earns no points, and the streak and points live only on Today
findings.evidence: add_points is called only from stories (stories/service.py:46, 396, 417-419, 432-434, 519-520), vocab (vocab.py:23, 123) and videos (videos/service.py:55, 493, 514-516). A grep shows no curriculum, topic, mission, conversation or speech code imports today. DECISIONS.md:205-207 (D-19) lists only story/word actions. /progress (progress/page.tsx:6) shows CurriculumProgress (12 rows × 4 text statuses: "Nog niet geoefend" / "Geoefend · nog niet getoetst", CurriculumProgress.tsx:35) and hides mission progress in a <details>. The mission progress uses a hard-coded default mission (ProgressOverview.tsx:16; learning.ts:38 always fetches missions/appointment-change). /progress shows no streak, points, saved or learned words, episodes read or topics practised. Points rules are never explained; only read-aloud shows "+N punten" (EpisodeReader.tsx:122). The 14 day-dots show their data only via title tooltips (TodayHome.tsx:111), which are unusable on touch.
findings.detail: A learner who does the 'real' course (leerpad lessons, topic tasks, missions) sees 0/20 points and a broken streak. The progress page reads as a compliance table, not a sense of growth. This explains the owner's 'not sure how it helps me'.

findings.title: The leerpad overwhelms a beginner: 12 open stages, a second level control, and a 100-topic picker as the default
findings.evidence: CurriculumPath.tsx:28-39 renders a continue panel, then PracticeCoach (its own level select), then 12 stage cards, each "Beschikbaar" with "0 / 4 vaardigheden · Eindtoets". The upper stage descriptions are disclaimers (path.json, pre-b2 to c2, e.g. "Oorspronkelijke, nog niet deskundig beoordeelde … geen volledige ERK-leerlijn"). CurriculumLesson.tsx:29 prepends Alfabet for pre-a1, but :31 defaults the section to "words". :32 sets showCore=false, so every skill opens on SkillTopicPractice: 100 topics, search, theme and status filters, 12 per page (SkillTopicPractice.tsx:52-67). The toggle labels "Onderwerpen" / "Startles" are unexplained (CurriculumLesson.tsx:83). 'Volgende vaardigheid' appears only after a core-lesson submit (:95). DECISIONS.md:189-190: the static topic and story libraries are "templated and heavily reused … every story in a stage asks the same question".
findings.detail: Instead of a guided lesson, the learner gets a library browser. Choice paralysis plus repetitive templated tasks give exactly the 'limited and boring' feel the owner reported.
findings.recommendation: Make /learn/[stage] a linear unit with a top stepper (Alfabet (pre-A1) → Woorden → Grammatica → Lezen → Luisteren → Spreken → Schrijven → Eindtoets) and a persistent 'Volgende stap' button. Default to the core lesson ('Startles', renamed e.g. 'Les'). Move topics under 'Meer oefenen met situaties' after the core step, preselected from /coach/plan. Default pre-A1 to Alfabet. On /leerpad, show the current stage large, the next one teased, and the others collapsed under 'Alle niveaus'. Remove the PracticeCoach level select in favour of the learner level.

findings.title: A wall of zeros and empty dead ends on day one
findings.evidence:
Fixture screenshot today-desktop.png: "0 dagen op rij", "0 / 20 punten", "Beste reeks 0 dagen", "Actieve dagen 0", 14 grey dots, "0 woorden om te herhalen · 0 bewaard · 0 stevig onthouden" (TodayHome.tsx:99-117). Dead ends:
- WordReview "Niets te herhalen." and "Bewaar woorden uit de verhalen…" with "Naar de verhalen" (WordReview.tsx:60, 75-78), which leads back to a pending episode.
- StoryLibrary "Nog geen afleveringen. Ga naar Vandaag" (StoryLibrary.tsx:60).
- VideoLibrary "Nog geen video's. Vraag hierboven je eerste." (VideoLibrary.tsx:130).
- ProgressOverview "Je geschiedenis verschijnt zodra je een oefensessie start." (ProgressOverview.tsx:101-104).
- LessonShell "nog geen records" and a separate "Start een oefensessie" button (LessonShell.tsx:284-306).
findings.detail: Every motivational widget starts at zero and points elsewhere. The Today → Woorden → Verhalen → Today loop is circular while the first episode is still being written.
findings.recommendation: Use day-one framing ("Dag 1 · begin vandaag je reeks") instead of zero stats, and hide 'Beste reeks' and 'Actieve dagen' until there are 2 or more active days. Seed the word bank with 5-10 starter words for the learner's level from the stage library (POST /words with source_kind 'starter'), so review works on day one. Give empty states one CTA plus an illustration. Offer suggested video topics as chips taken from the stage topic bank. Start the mission session automatically on first step interaction (ensureSession already exists in LessonShell).

findings.title: Honesty and technical notices are repeated everywhere and add noise; dev hints leak to learners
findings.evidence:
Unreviewed or synthetic notices:
- TodayHome.tsx:159; CurriculumPath.tsx:42; CurriculumLesson.tsx:96 (every section)
- AlphabetPractice.tsx:17 warn label and :35
- VocabularyRecall.tsx:38; EpisodeReader.tsx:79 (with model name)
- VideoLibrary.tsx:133-139 'Wat je ziet'; VideoPlayer.tsx:80, 99
- ProgressOverview.tsx:85-89 ("Geoefend betekent niet automatisch zelfstandig beheerst.") and :138-148
- ContentLabel on mission steps (ReadingStep.tsx:77, SpeakingStep.tsx:243, 258, WritingStep.tsx:154, ListeningStep.tsx:132, StepHeader.tsx:21, LessonShell.tsx:266, 362)
- upper-stage descriptions in path.json
Technical leaks:
- ConnectionBanner.tsx:48 "Draait `python scripts/run.py dev`?" shown in every environment
- failure reasons rendered as <code> (TodayHome.tsx:91; StoryLibrary.tsx:54; VideoLibrary.tsx:45)
- TodayHome.tsx:90 "Controleer of het taalmodel draait (Instellingen › Technische ondersteuning)"
- SpeechCheck.tsx:106-107 'MediaRecorder' format
- UsagePanel.tsx:85 "Prijstabel leeg: … tot fase B…"
- VideoLibrary.tsx:125 "Elke minuut video kost geld"
- brand caption at 8px (learning.css:19)
findings.detail: Honesty is a core decision (D-17), but repeating it on nearly every screen makes the product feel provisional and untrustworthy. Developer instructions confuse learners.

findings.title: Waiting states are passive: minutes of 'De schrijver is bezig…' with nothing to do
findings.evidence: Episode polling: POLL_MS 5000, POLL_LIMIT 48 (TodayHome.tsx:10-11). Video polling: 6000 ms × 150 = 15 min (VideoLibrary.tsx:11-12). Waiting UI is three 'writing-dots' (TodayHome.tsx:72; VideoLibrary.tsx:37; StoryLibrary.tsx:57); statusCopy 'wordt geschreven' (StoryLibrary.tsx:10). There is no ready notification outside the page and no stage progress (queued/writing/checking). The video form allows at most 2 pending (VideoLibrary.tsx:125; 409 at :82).
findings.detail: Generation time is the product's biggest built-in friction, and the UI turns it into dead time.
findings.recommendation: Show a staged progress indicator (queued → writing → checking → ready) using the existing status fields (episode queued/generating; video queued/writing/rendering). Pair it with a 'Terwijl je wacht' micro-activity: due-word review, a VocabularyRecall round on the theme's stage words, or AlphabetPractice. Add a nav badge or toast when an episode or video becomes ready; Today and VideoLibrary already poll. Make sure onboarding pre-queues episode 1.

findings.title: Motivational and progress data the API returns but the UI ignores
findings.evidence:
Unused or barely used fields:
- /today words.preview (3 due WordItems) is unused (routes_stories.py:83-84; TodayHome uses only due_count/total/learned_count, :113-115).
- words.new_count is unused.
- series.episode_count is unused on Today.
- recent_days carries points and goal_met but shows only as unlabeled dots (TodayHome.tsx:111).
- LearningDay stores episodes_read, words_reviewed, questions_correct, read_aloud and videos_watched per day (stories/models.py:105-122), but no endpoint exposes them (today.py:74-85 returns points/goal_met only).
- POINTS constants (stories/service.py:46; vocab.py:23; videos/service.py:55) are never explained.
- /curriculum returns cefr_reference and policy (curriculum/service.py:108-115), unused in UI (cefr_reference only typed, curriculum.ts:7).
- TopicPage.completed_count/total_topics is shown only inside one skill tab (SkillTopicPractice.tsx:55) and never aggregated.
- PracticePlan evidence_count, basis, history_count and mode are typed but unused (learning-agents.ts:25-30).
- /progress skill_records latest_assessment and evidence_ids are unused (grep: no hits in components).
- VocabItem interval_days, repetitions, lapses and learned appear only as text in the list (WordReview.tsx:94).
- Episode read_aloud per paragraph is shown only beside the paragraph (EpisodeReader.tsx:123).
- videos.pending is used only as a boolean (TodayHome.tsx:122).
findings.detail: The data for rich, honest progress feedback already exists; it simply isn't visualised.
findings.recommendation: Use words.preview for an inline 'warm-up' card of 3 words on Today. Expose the LearningDay counters (extend recent_days or add GET /progress/summary) and chart them weekly. Show cefr_reference as a plain-language can-do statement. Aggregate topic completion per stage/skill on /progress. Show PracticePlan reasons on Today. Visualise word-bank strength buckets (new / learning / strong, from interval_days and learned). Show a mission skill evidence count.

findings.title: Docs and previews are stale relative to the code
findings.evidence: LEARNING_DESIGN.md:65-66: "Generated video remains a future reviewed asset type … No video provider, empty video navigation…", but Video's is a nav item (AppShell.tsx:18). DESIGN_PREVIEW.md:3-5 uses fixture screenshots from 2 Oct: today-desktop.png has no video card and today-phone.png shows 5 mobile tabs, while the code has 6 (AppShell.tsx:16-33). IMPROVEMENT_REVIEW.md describes release 0.1 (22 Sept) with a single mission home. LEARNING_DESIGN.md:44 claims "A restrained navy/blue palette" as a design choice.
findings.detail: A planner reading the docs would get an outdated picture of first-run and navigation.
findings.recommendation: After the redesign, regenerate previews with a true first-visit state (no learner data, pending episode) as well as the ready state. Update LEARNING_DESIGN 'Design choices' to record the new palette and onboarding decisions, e.g. as a new D-23 in DECISIONS.md.

reusable_assets.what: LearningCopy {nl,en,fa} type, LearningText renderer (supportOnly variant), useLanguageSupport (showEnglish/showPersian), LanguageSwitcher
reusable_assets.how_to_reuse: Base a UiText/ui-copy dictionary on LearningText to gloss nav, buttons and headings. Extend the provider to initialise from and persist to the server.

reusable_assets.how_to_reuse: Extend next_step with 'lesson'/'speak' and add a session-steps array instead of creating a new endpoint. TodayHome already handles the polling and the act() error mapping.

reusable_assets.what: add_points (upsert per Europe/Brussels day with counters), streak(), recent_days(), DAILY_GOAL
reusable_assets.how_to_reuse: Call add_points from curriculum/topic/mission/conversation completions with new counter columns. Return the per-day counters for a weekly chart.

reusable_assets.how_to_reuse: Data source for the progress dashboard (activity mix, word-strength buckets) without new tracking.

reusable_assets.what: Six gradient cover tones (--tone-1..6), streak-ring, goal-bar gradient, day-dots, words-card
reusable_assets.how_to_reuse: Seed a more colourful design system: map tones to skills/sections, reuse the ring and bar for skill rings and session progress.

reusable_assets.how_to_reuse: Day-one onboarding activity and wait-state filler for absolute beginners.

reusable_assets.how_to_reuse: Warm-up step in the Today session and a wait-state micro-activity, fed with stage library words or words.preview.

reusable_assets.what: Per-stage/skill topic completion counts and a topic task reader

reusable_assets.how_to_reuse: Keep it when restructuring the nav. New nav components must stay inside the onClickCapture wrapper.

constraints: D-17 (docs/DECISIONS.md:170-175): no fictitious scores, certificates or reviewed-content claims. Unreviewed/generated content must stay honestly labelled. Consolidating labels is allowed; removing honesty is not.

D-19 (docs/DECISIONS.md:203-210): points reward doing and are never a judgement of the learner's Dutch. The daily goal is 20. The streak counts consecutive active days and a missed day resets it (today.py:52). Awarding points for curriculum/missions is an explicit extension of D-19's scope and should be recorded as a new decision.
D-20 / LEARNING_DESIGN.md:37-39: no pronunciation or accent score anywhere; transcripts are not pronunciation evidence.
D-16: typed input never counts as speaking practice.

D-18 (docs/DECISIONS.md:187-201): episodes are generated ahead with at most 2 pending (409). The next episode waits for the learner's choice or 12 hours. A failed draft is shown as a failure, never as a story.

LEARNING_DESIGN.md:31-35: Dutch remains the practice language. Final checks withhold translations, transcripts and model answers. A self-report never unlocks a stage (LEARNING_DESIGN.md:48), so self-placement may set a starting level but must not mark stages passed.

areas.area: Practice and exercise experience: why the practices feel limited and boring (web components, hosting routes, content JSON, practice docs)
areas.overview:
How it works today, end to end. A learner opens /leerpad (apps/web/app/leerpad/page.tsx). That page renders CurriculumPath, which shows a "suggested starting point" (the first stage not yet passed, so pre-A1 for a new learner), PracticeCoach with three recommended topics, and 12 stage cards. Opening /learn/[stageId] mounts CurriculumLesson. Its sidebar has 7 sections (8 at pre-A1, which adds Alfabet): Woorden, Grammatica, Lezen, Luisteren, Spreken, Schrijven, Story Time. It opens on Woorden by default (CurriculumLesson.tsx:31). Each skill tab defaults to SkillTopicPractice ("Onderwerpen"), a searchable grid of 100 topics per skill per stage, 12 tiles per page. Each tile shows only a title and category. The original single lesson sits behind a "Startles" toggle (CurriculumLesson.tsx:83-84).

Opening a topic mounts TopicReader (SkillTopicPractice.tsx:84-186). It is the same vertical stack for every topic:
- header and a collapsible "Wat oefen je hier?";
- then the skill-specific body:
  - Reading: a 2-paragraph text with a TTS button per sentence (SpokenPassage), then 2 radio multiple-choice questions.
  - Listening: a TTS clip (CurriculumAudio), an optional transcript, then 2 multiple-choice questions.
  - Speaking: the context texts, a long prompt, 3–4 criteria, CurriculumRecorder (click start/stop, server transcription), then submit for a model rubric.
  - Writing: a textarea, an optional WritingCoach model correction pass, then submit for a model rubric;
- a collapsed vocabulary list at the bottom;
- one submit button ("Rond lezen af" and similar);
- one pale feedback box.

Grading:
- Multiple choice is graded server-side by objective_result. With 75% required, both questions must be right (apps/api/src/dlp/domains/curriculum/service.py:34,160).
- Productive tasks go to the LLM rubric (assess_productive, service.py:206-246) and are always marked completed (topics.py:241).

After feedback, the only forward action is "Kies een ander onderwerp", which goes back to the grid (SkillTopicPractice.tsx:182).

Other practice surfaces:
- **Grammar:** CurriculumLesson.tsx:88. One multiple-choice question per grammar item, checked on the client, 55 questions in total.
- **WordLibrary:** 20 cards per page, each with a reveal toggle.
- **VocabularyRecall:** 5 sequential words with a typed answer that is never checked, then self-rating.
- **AlphabetPractice:** pre-A1 only. Listen, then tap a letter tile, with immediate feedback. Deterministic rounds.
- **Story Time:** the same texts as the topic readings, plus 1 multiple-choice question and a "mark read" button.
- **Missions** (/missions, LessonShell, 4 packs, all A2): reading, listening, push-to-talk conversation, writing and checkpoint steps, with HelpLadder and on-demand LLM FeedbackPanel.
- **/verhalen EpisodeReader and /videos VideoPlayer:** an LLM-generated serial and videos with read-aloud word matching, glossary save to the spaced-repetition deck, and 2–3 multiple-choice questions.
- **/woorden WordReview:** spaced repetition (SM-2) with reveal and 4 grade buttons, for saved words only.

Points and streak (apps/api/src/dlp/domains/stories/today.py) are awarded only by stories, videos and word review. Topic practice, lessons, grammar, missions and the alphabet award nothing.

Content shapes:
- **content/practice/<stage>.json:** {schema_version, stage_id, review_status, topics[100]}. Each topic is {id, title, category, objectives[], language_focus, vocabulary_ids[≈5], reading{text, questions[2]}, listening{text, questions[2]}, speaking{prompt, criteria[3-4], sample, sample_is_excerpt, min_words, max_words}, writing{same}}. Each question is {id, prompt, options[2|3]{nl,en,fa}, answer_index, explanation}.
- **content/library/<stage>.json:** {vocabulary[500]{id, term, topic, meaning{nl,en,fa}, example{nl,en,fa}}, stories[100]{id, title, topic, paragraphs[2], vocabulary_ids, question}}.
- **content/curriculum/path.json:** stages[12]{grammar[2-9]{explanation, examples, practice[1]}, vocabulary[20-43], lesson{story, reading_questions[3], listening, listening_questions[3], speaking, writing}, test{...}}.
- **content/conversations/pilot.json:** 10 blueprints only (a1 3, a2 3, b1 2, b2 2), with steps{goal, cue, hint, accepted, required_groups, choices[aliases, valid], example}.
- **content/missions/*/mission.json:** 5 steps with typed payloads, scenarios and help rungs.

Why it is monotonous: the measured facts.
- **Few mechanics.** The 4,800 topic activities use 3 mechanics: radio multiple choice, record-and-submit, and type-and-submit. Across the whole app there are 7 (those 3, plus conversation turns, reveal/self-rate cards, alphabet tile tap, and read-aloud match). Only the alphabet gives instant per-item feedback.
- **No randomisation.** There is none anywhere: Math.random appears only in request ids (lib/client/api.ts:20).
- **No adaptivity.** There is no difficulty adaptation and no in-topic session/round structure.
- **No typed-and-checked recall.** It does not exist anywhere; recognition multiple choice dominates.
- **Multiple choice is guessable.** At A1–B1 it has 2 options. The default nl-en mode prints the English translation under every option (LanguageSupport.tsx:9,40; CurriculumControls.tsx:16). That gives away the "Wat betekent ‘X’?" questions, which are 100 of 400 per stage at pre-A1, A1 and pre-A2. At pre-B2, B2 and pre-C1, 400/400 correct options are sentences copied verbatim from the text.
- **Heavy templating.** C1 has 4 distinct question prompts across 400 questions. Productive prompts and 2 of 3 criteria are boilerplate. Speaking sample equals writing sample in 100% of topics from pre-A1 to B1.
- **Heavy duplication.** Only 399 unique titles across 1,200 topic slots. Listening texts are identical across pre-A1/A1/pre-A2 and across A2/pre-B1/B1. Reading texts are identical across C1/pre-C2/C2. The library vocabulary is the same 500 terms for pre-A1, A1 and pre-A2. Story Time stories are the topic reading texts (100/100 at pre-A1).

These are the root causes of "limited and boring".

What can be generated without new authoring. The library vocabulary (term, meaning, example, topic grouping) and the topic bundle (5 vocab + 4 questions + 2 texts) can feed:
- match-pairs, cloze, listen-and-choose, dictation, typed recall, de/het sorting (strong at A–B levels), sentence-builder tiles, sentence ordering, odd-one-out, speed rounds and shadowing;
- mixed 8–12 item sessions.

Translate-to-Dutch and error-correction need an LLM judge or generator. Verb-conjugation drills are not feasible: the vocabulary banks contain 0–1 verbs per stage.

The base for a shared engine is already present:
- CurriculumQuestions/QuestionList (multiple-choice rendering);
- AlphabetPractice and letterQuestion (tile item with instant feedback);
- VocabularyRecall (round, missed-items retry, summary);
- WordReview plus the words API and SM-2 backend;
- PhraseAudio/PhraseAudioController (TTS with cache);
- CurriculumRecorder/useRecorder (capture and transcript);
- ReadAloud with read_aloud_result (word-match);
- HelpLadder, dutchSentences and today.add_points.

strengths: Large, fully trilingual content: every vocabulary card, question, option, explanation and task has nl/en/fa (library: 500 cards + 100 stories × 12 stages; practice: 100 topics × 4 skills × 12 stages) – ideal raw material for generated drills.

Per-topic bundles are self-contained: TopicDetail returns title, objectives, 5 linked vocabulary cards with examples, a reading text, a listening text, 4 questions with explanations and two productive tasks (apps/api/src/dlp/domains/curriculum/topics.py:174-195).

Robust audio stack: PhraseAudioController with tab cache (32 entries/8 MB), single-player audio focus across the app, 600-char chunking (apps/web/lib/client/phrase-audio.ts, audio-focus.ts) – any Dutch string can be spoken on demand.
Robust recording stack: useRecorder with mime negotiation, mic request gating, stop tail; CurriculumRecorder returns asset id AND transcript to the caller (CurriculumControls.tsx:96-163).
A working SM-2 spaced-repetition backend and UI (/woorden) plus daily points/streak/goal plumbing (stories/vocab.py, stories/today.py, TodayHome streak ring).
Server-side idempotency and evidence model (newRequestId, observation records with failed_refs in coaching service) – a ready signal for adaptivity.
Careful LLM safety pattern: model interprets, code validates quotes/choices (topic_conversations/workflow.py:69-86; curriculum/service.py:188-203).
HelpLadder provides graduated hints with evidence; WritingCoach gives categorised corrections (spelling, grammar, word_order, punctuation, word_choice).
Accessibility discipline (focus management after commit, aria-live, reduced-motion handling in stories.css:45) that a new engine should keep.

findings.title: Only 3 interaction mechanics in the 4,800-activity topic practice; 7 in the whole app
findings.evidence: apps/web/components/SkillTopicPractice.tsx:168-176 (reading text+MCQ, CurriculumAudio+MCQ, CurriculumRecorder, textarea); CurriculumControls.tsx:12-19 radio MCQ; whole-app extras: TopicConversation.tsx:167-188, VocabularyRecall.tsx:35-36, WordReview.tsx:64-73, AlphabetPractice.tsx:31, EpisodeReader.tsx:101-126
findings.detail: Distinct mechanics: (a) radio MCQ submit-then-check (5 separate renderers: CurriculumQuestions, QuestionList, EpisodeReader.Questions, VideoPlayer.Questions, CurriculumTest exam mode); (b) record open answer → LLM rubric; (c) type open answer → LLM rubric; (d) conversational turns (10 topic blueprints + 4 missions); (e) reveal-and-self-rate cards (WordLibrary, VocabularyRecall, WordReview); (f) listen-and-tap tiles with instant feedback (Alphabet only, pre-A1 only, 26 letters); (g) read-aloud word match (episodes only). Topic practice uses only a/b/c. No drag/drop, no tile building, no matching, no typing-with-checking, no timed or game-like item anywhere.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a shared item-based exercise engine with at least 8–10 item types (see feasibility findings) and make topic practice a short mixed session rather than a single form.

findings.title: No active recall that is actually checked; recognition MCQ and self-rating dominate
findings.evidence: apps/web/components/VocabularyRecall.tsx:35 input value never compared, :36 self-rate 'Nog eens oefenen'/'Ik herinnerde het me'; WordReview.tsx:72 reveal then 4 grade buttons; LearningLibrary.tsx:77 'Toon de betekenis' toggle; docs/LEARNING_DESIGN.md:16-19 self-assessment is a deliberate choice
findings.detail: Every vocabulary interaction is 'look, reveal, judge yourself'. The learner can type in VocabularyRecall but nothing checks it. Receptive skills are 2–3 option MCQ. The only production is long open tasks graded by an LLM after a single submit. There is nothing in between (cloze, typed recall, dictation, word order) – the layer where most beginner learning happens.
findings.recommendation: Add typed-and-checked recall (tolerant comparison) and auto-checkable production items; keep self-rating as an optional SRS grade after an objective check rather than instead of it.

findings.title: MCQ is trivially guessable: 2 options at A1–B1, translations printed under options, 'Wat betekent' giveaways, verbatim answers at B2
findings.evidence: Analysis of content/practice/*.json: options per question = 2 for all 400 questions at pre-a1..b1; 3 at pre-b2..pre-c1; 2/3 mixed at c-levels. 'Wat betekent ‘X’ in deze tekst?' = 100/400 at pre-a1, a1, pre-a2 (e.g. a1-t001-r2 options 'hier slaap je in' en:'bed'). Correct option verbatim in text: 400/400 at pre-b2, b2, pre-c1. LanguageSupport.tsx:9 default 'nl-en', :40 renders English under every LearningText; CurriculumControls.tsx:16 options rendered with LearningText (non-exam). Pass rule apps/api/src/dlp/domains/curriculum/service.py:34,160 (75% of 2 → both).
findings.detail: With two options and English support visible by default, a learner can answer most A-level questions without reading Dutch; vocabulary-meaning questions literally show the English word as an option gloss. At B2 the options are sentences copied from the text, so string-matching solves them. Random guessing passes a 2-question topic 25% of the time. Episode/video questions are Dutch-only (EpisodeReader.tsx:158-161) – inconsistent with topic questions.
findings.recommendation: In practice items hide support translations on options until after answering (or behind a hint), use 3–4 options with same-topic distractors, and shuffle option order per attempt.

findings.title: Massive templating and duplication in the topic and library banks
findings.evidence: content/practice: only 399 unique titles across 1,200 topics (each title reused in 3 stages: a1/pre-a1/pre-a2, a2/pre-b1/b1, pre-b2/b2/pre-c1, c1/pre-c2/c2); listening texts identical across pre-a1/a1/pre-a2 (100) and a2/pre-b1/b1 (100) → 800 unique of 1,200; reading texts identical across c1/pre-c2/c2 (100) and a2/b1 (96). c1 has 4 distinct question prompts across 400 questions; b1 has 'Welke uitleg past bij de aanpak in deze tekst?' and 'Welke reactie beantwoordt het verzoek in de boodschap?' 100× each; a2..b1 reading q1 == listening q1 in 100/100 topics. content/library: pre-a1, a1 and pre-a2 share the same 500 terms; pre-b2/b2/pre-c1 share 500; a2/pre-b1/b1 share 480; a2/pre-b1/b1 examples use only 54–57 sentence frames (e.g. 'Ik bewaar X zorgvuldig, zodat ik mijn aanvraag later kan opvolgen.' ×10). Story Time stories == topic reading texts (100/100 at pre-a1, 99 a1, 96 b1).
findings.detail: The learner meets the same texts and the same question stems repeatedly: moving from pre-A1 to A1 to pre-A2 gives the same listening clips, the same 500 words and the same topic titles; Story Time repeats the Lezen texts. docs/PRACTICE_LIBRARY.md:26-27 calls some reuse intentional spiralling, but the magnitude makes 'progress' feel like repetition.
findings.recommendation: Treat the banks as an item pool for generated drills (which tolerate reuse well) instead of as 1,200 'distinct' lessons; reduce visible duplication (e.g. hide Story Time when identical to the topic text, or present cross-stage reuse explicitly as review).

findings.title: Productive tasks are boilerplate-heavy, identical for speaking and writing, and always 'completed'
findings.evidence: pre-a1/a1: speaking prompt always starts 'Spreek in deze situatie:' and writing 'Schrijf een kort bericht voor deze situatie:' (100/100); 2 of 3 criteria per task are the same text in all 200 tasks ('Behoud de juiste personen, voorwerpen, plaats en tijd…', 'Spreek rustig en begrijpelijk…'/'Maak leesbare zinnen…'); speaking.sample == writing.sample in 100% of topics at pre-a1..b1; c1 has 6 distinct criteria across 700. apps/api/src/dlp/domains/curriculum/topics.py:241 'completed = True'.
findings.detail: The productive side repeats the same instructions every time and gives the same model answer for speaking and writing. Because any substantive attempt completes the topic, there is no sense of challenge or mastery, and every attempt costs one LLM call (assess_productive) with latency.
findings.recommendation: Precede open production with scaffolded auto-checked items built from the sample (sentence builder, cloze over the sample, shadow the sample), and show only the topic-specific criterion prominently.

findings.title: No rewards or feedback loop in practice: points/streak only from stories, videos and word review
findings.evidence: add_points callers: apps/api/src/dlp/domains/stories/service.py (6), stories/vocab.py (1), videos/service.py (3); none in curriculum/topics.py or curriculum/service.py or practice/*. POINTS stories/service.py:46 {read 10, answer 3, choose 2, read_aloud 5}; videos/service.py:55; vocab.py:23 REVIEW_POINTS=1; today.py:16 DAILY_GOAL=20. Only animation in CSS: stories.css:41-44 writing dots. SkillTopicPractice.tsx:182 feedback heading 'Een onderwerp verder.'
findings.detail: Completing topics, grammar checks, alphabet rounds, missions or Startles never moves the daily goal or streak shown on TodayHome. There are no sounds, no celebratory animation, no XP per item, no combo/streak within a session, no session summary in topic practice. Feedback is a single pale box (learning.css:166) with neutral copy.
findings.recommendation: Award points via today.add_points for topic/lesson/mission/exercise-engine items (D-19 permits 'points reward doing'), add per-item instant feedback states (correct/incorrect colours, micro-animation, optional sound), and an end-of-session summary card.

findings.title: No randomisation, no adaptivity, no session structure inside a topic
findings.evidence: Math.random only in apps/web/lib/client/api.ts:20 (request ids); no shuffle anywhere in apps/web; lib/alphabet.ts:64-70 deterministic (round*7+3)%26 with fixed offsets [0,5,11,17]; VocabularyRecall.tsx:21-24 takes next 5 words sequentially from the current page; SkillTopicPractice.tsx:39 topics paged 12 at a time in file order; PracticeCoach shows 3 items (coaching/service.py:208).
findings.detail: Option order, item order and word order are fixed in JSON, so retrying a topic is identical. Nothing adapts difficulty to errors (coaching observations record failed_refs but only influence the 3-item PracticeCoach suggestion). A topic is one form: no rounds, no progress bar within the activity, no hearts/lives, no summary.
findings.recommendation: Engine should shuffle items/options per attempt, re-queue missed items within the session (VocabularyRecall already does a missed-items loop), and use coaching observations to pick item types/words.

findings.title: Confusing entry and choice overload in the stage page
findings.evidence: CurriculumLesson.tsx:31 default section 'words' (500-card WordLibrary); :81 sidebar 'STAP VOOR STAP' but no enforced sequence; :83 'Onderwerpen'/'Startles' toggle without explanation; SkillTopicPractice.tsx:53-66 100 topics, 12 per page, tiles show only index/title/category; :182 after feedback only 'Kies een ander onderwerp' (back to grid); CurriculumPath.tsx:20 suggested start = first unpassed stage (no placement); AppShell.tsx:16-41 nine navigation destinations; TopicReader puts vocabulary preview last in a collapsed details (SkillTopicPractice.tsx:178) although docs/LEARNING_DESIGN.md:9 says 'Preview relevant words' first.
findings.detail: A new learner lands on a word bank, then on a 100-item grid per skill, with two parallel 'lesson' sources, and no 'continue/next' affordance. Nothing explains how a session helps them learn. The pedagogical loop in LEARNING_DESIGN.md (preview words → recall → read/listen → speak → write) is not what the UI sequences.
findings.recommendation: Replace the default with a single 'Start today's session' that runs the loop (vocab preview items → recall drills → comprehension → guided production) for the next topic, with an obvious 'Volgende' after the summary.

findings.title: Disclaimer-heavy, mixed-register copy inside exercises
findings.evidence: CurriculumControls.tsx:162 'Je opname wordt bij deze oefening bewaard…'; AlphabetPractice.tsx:17 'Nog niet nagekeken' badge and :35 course-note; VocabularyRecall.tsx:38 course-note; LearningLibrary.tsx:121; CurriculumLesson.tsx:96 'Nieuwe les · taalreview nog niet afgerond.'; ListeningStep.tsx:114 and FeedbackPanel.tsx:66 use formal 'u' while topic practice uses 'je'; StepHeader.tsx:21 ContentLabel on every mission step.
findings.detail: Nearly every practice panel ends with a caveat about review status, synthetic voice or not being a score. Combined with 2–3 stacked language lines (LearningText) the screens read as dense and cautious rather than playful.
findings.recommendation: Consolidate caveats into one 'about this content' info point per page; keep exercise surfaces focused on the task; unify register (je).

findings.title: Code duplication and inconsistencies a shared engine should remove
findings.evidence: Three MCQ renderers: CurriculumControls.tsx:12-19, QuestionList.tsx:26-129, EpisodeReader.tsx:147-168 + VideoPlayer.tsx:141-162 (near-identical, as are Glossary EpisodeReader.tsx:128-145 / VideoPlayer.tsx:122-139 and friendly() :13-20 in both); two countWords with different regexes (CurriculumControls.tsx:94 vs WritingStep.tsx:23); WritingStep.tsx:231 WritingCoach stageId hard-coded "a2"; CurriculumLesson and TopicReader each re-implement submit/feedback blocks (CurriculumLesson.tsx:61-69,94-95 vs SkillTopicPractice.tsx:129-152,181-182).
findings.detail: Each surface hand-rolls question state, check, and feedback. Word counts differ between mission writing and topic writing for the same text. Any new exercise type would currently have to be added in 3–5 places.
findings.recommendation: Extract a typed ExerciseItem model + renderer registry + session runner, and migrate existing MCQ/recall/alphabet into it.

findings.title: Instant per-item feedback blocked for topic items because answer keys are stripped
findings.evidence: apps/api/src/dlp/domains/curriculum/topics.py:177-180 pops answer_index and explanation for reading/listening; keys are only returned after whole-topic submit (topics.py:219-221). By contrast stage_view keeps keys (curriculum/service.py:136) and library story_detail keeps them (library.py:156-162).
findings.detail: A Duolingo-style 'check after each item' flow for topic questions needs either a per-item check endpoint or a practice-mode payload with keys. Generated drills from library vocabulary can be checked client-side because the vocabulary page returns term/meaning/example in full.
findings.recommendation: Add a lightweight practice-session endpoint that serves generated items with per-item check (or returns keys in practice mode only, keeping the final test withheld as today).

findings.title: Inventory: topic Reading (Lezen)
findings.evidence: SkillTopicPractice.tsx:168,170,181-182; CurriculumControls.tsx:12-19; LearningLibrary.tsx:19-22; topics.py:216-221
findings.detail: Component: TopicReader + SpokenPassage + CurriculumQuestions. Learner: reads 2-paragraph text (11–111 words), may press per-sentence TTS buttons, toggles 'Vertaling tonen', selects radio for 2 questions, presses 'Rond lezen af'. Check: server objective_result, both correct needed. Feedback: box 'Een onderwerp verder.'/'Probeer het nog eens.' + 'x van 2 juist' + per-question 'Goed gedaan.'/'Bekijk de uitleg…' with explanation. Audio: yes (TTS per sentence, per question, per option). Variation: none. Adaptation: none. Session: single form; library-level 'n / 100 onderwerpen geoefend' progress bar (SkillTopicPractice.tsx:55). Reward: 'Al geoefend' badge only.
findings.recommendation: Rebuild as a session of items (vocab preview → read → instant-feedback questions → sentence ordering/cloze from the same text).

findings.title: Inventory: topic Listening (Luisteren)
findings.evidence: SkillTopicPractice.tsx:169-170; CurriculumControls.tsx:21-92
findings.detail: Component: CurriculumAudio + CurriculumQuestions. Learner: presses 'Luister naar het fragment' (server TTS, multi-part select if long), can replay with native controls, can open transcript 'Lees mee als je hulp nodig hebt', answers 2 MCQ (questions visible before listening, with translations). Check/feedback identical to Reading. No dictation, no gap-listening, no speed control. Listening texts identical across 3 stages (see duplication finding).
findings.recommendation: Add listen-and-type and listen-and-choose items; hide transcript/translations until after an attempt.

findings.title: Inventory: topic Speaking (Spreken)
findings.evidence: SkillTopicPractice.tsx:165-172,176; CurriculumControls.tsx:96-163; topics.py:225-241; curriculum/service.py:206-246
findings.detail: Component: TopicReader + CurriculumRecorder (+ TopicConversation on 10 topics). Learner: reads open 'De situatie' (both texts), long prompt + 3–4 criteria, clicks 'Start de opname' (limit ≤58 s), stops, sees transcript and word-count check, clicks submit. Check: server transcript → LLM rubric per criterion (quote must appear in transcript). Feedback: criteria list 'Gelukt'/'Verder oefenen' with one-line feedback. Always completed. Sample answer in collapsed details. No shadowing, no model-then-repeat, no short utterance drills.
findings.recommendation: Add short shadowing/repeat items (TTS → record → word match) before the open task.

findings.title: Inventory: topic Writing (Schrijven) + WritingCoach
findings.evidence: SkillTopicPractice.tsx:171-176; WritingCoach.tsx:13-34; apps/api/src/dlp/domains/curriculum/writing.py:19-21
findings.detail: Learner types in textarea with live word count (target e.g. 4–60 at A1), optionally presses 'Controleer spelling en grammatica' (LLM, ≤5 corrections, categories spelling/grammar/word_order/punctuation/word_choice, 'Gebruik als nieuwe versie'), then submits for LLM rubric. Draft in sessionStorage per topic. Corrections not persisted server-side. No sentence-level scaffolding.
findings.recommendation: Reuse WritingCoach categories to generate personal error-correction items later; scaffold with sentence builder/cloze over the sample.

findings.title: Inventory: Topic conversation (10 blueprints) and missions conversation
findings.evidence: TopicConversation.tsx:17-28,167-188; topic_conversations/workflow.py:69-116; content/conversations/pilot.json (a1 3, a2 3, b1 2, b2 2); SpeakingStep.tsx:333-408
findings.detail: Learner types or records each turn (≤100 words), may press 'Herhaal de laatste vraag'/'Geef me een hint' (count as turns), sends; LLM interprets intent, code checks required_groups/choices, partner reply is authored (accepted line + next cue, or the same cue repeated on failure – no corrective feedback). Ends with goals met/assisted summary. Missions: push-to-talk hold button, appointment/choice checklist, turn budget, checkpoint transfer with no help. Most engaging mechanic but available on 10 of 400 speaking topics and 4 A2 missions.
findings.recommendation: Expose more blueprints (builder exists: scripts/content_build/build_conversation_pilot.py) and add an offline 'choose the right reply' item from cue/example/choices.

findings.title: Inventory: Grammar section, Startles, Story Time, Word library
findings.evidence: CurriculumLesson.tsx:87-95; content/curriculum/path.json grammar practice counts pre-a1 5, a1 7, pre-a2 8, a2 7, pre-b1 6, b1 9, others 2 (1 Q each; 55 total); LearningLibrary.tsx:54-128
findings.detail: Grammar: explanation + examples with TTS + 1 three-option MCQ per item, client-side 'Controleer je zin', no score/progress/reward. Startles: core lesson (3+3 MCQ, 1 speaking, 1 writing) with CommunicationCoach static tips. Story Time: same texts as topic reading, 1 MCQ client-check, 'Markeer als gelezen' (localStorage). Word library: 20 cards/page, reveal toggle, TTS; VocabularyRecall round above it.
findings.recommendation: Turn grammar examples into sentence-builder and cloze items; merge Story Time into the topic session or hide duplicates.

findings.title: Inventory: Alphabet, VocabularyRecall, WordReview (SRS)
findings.evidence: AlphabetPractice.tsx:27-33; lib/alphabet.ts:64-70; VocabularyRecall.tsx:10-40; WordReview.tsx:18-98; stories/vocab.py:21-23
findings.detail: Alphabet (pre-A1 only): tap TTS speaker, tap 1 of 4 letter buttons, instant 'Juist…'/'Je hoorde…' message, 'Volgende letter'; no score. VocabularyRecall: 'Woord n van 5', cue = meaning, optional unchecked input, reveal term+example, self-rate; summary + 'Herhaal de lastige woorden'; not persisted. WordReview: only words saved from episode/video glossaries or manually (no save button in WordLibrary/topic vocabulary – words.save used only in WordReview.tsx:51); reveal meaning, 4 SM-2 grades, +1 point per review.
findings.recommendation: Add 'Bewaar' to library/topic vocabulary and feed engine results into SRS grades automatically.

findings.title: Inventory: Episodes and Videos (generated content)
findings.evidence: EpisodeReader.tsx:22-168; VideoPlayer.tsx:22-162; stories/service.py:46,493-525; videos/service.py:55
findings.detail: Episode: read paragraphs (TTS per paragraph and whole episode), optional Persian translation on demand (LLM), 'Lees hardop' per paragraph (record → server bag-of-words match 'x van y woorden herkend · +5 punten', missed words listed), glossary 'Bewaar', 'Klaar met lezen' → 2–3 Dutch-only MCQ with evidence quote, A/B choice shaping next episode, rating. Video: watch with subtitles, click-to-seek transcript, glossary, MCQ. These are the only surfaces with points and narrative pull.
findings.recommendation: Reuse ReadAloud/read_aloud_result for shadowing items in the engine; link the episode word glossary to engine drills.

findings.title: Feasibility: Match pairs (word ↔ translation / definition) – no new authoring
findings.evidence: content/library/<stage>.json vocabulary[].term, .meaning.en/.fa/.nl, .topic.nl (A-levels 100 topics × 5 words; a2–b1 50 × 10; higher 10 × 50); content/practice topic.vocabulary_ids (≈5 per topic; a few have 1–4)
findings.detail: 5-pair boards per topic come straight from topic.vocabulary_ids or library topic groups. All 500 cards per stage have en and fa. At C-levels meaning.en is long (e.g. 'the opportunity to express a view on a decision') – use term ↔ meaning.nl or shorter boards. Missing: nothing.
findings.recommendation: Ship first; it is pure client logic over the library vocabulary endpoint (limit ≤50, topic filter).

findings.title: Feasibility: Cloze / fill-the-gap
findings.evidence: library vocabulary core term (without de/het) appears in example.nl for 93–100% of cards (pre-a1 500/500, b1 497/500, pre-b2 465/500, c1 500/500); grammar practice already cloze-style ('Vul aan: Ik … Noor.' path.json pre-a1 g1)
findings.detail: Blank the term in example.nl; distractors = other terms from the same topic. Typed-answer variant uses tolerant comparison. Caveat: a2/pre-b1/b1 examples use only 54–57 frames, so clozes there will feel repetitive; full term with article only in 211–500 examples (pre-b2 211) – match on the core noun.
findings.recommendation: Generate client-side; prefer A-level and pre-b2+ stages for variety; use topic reading sentences as a second source.

findings.title: Feasibility: Listen-and-choose (word or meaning)
findings.evidence: PhraseAudio/PhraseAudioController (apps/web/lib/client/phrase-audio.ts) + POST speech/synthesize (≤600 chars, apps/api/src/dlp/api/routes_speech.py:66); AlphabetPractice pattern
findings.detail: Play term TTS, learner taps the written term or meaning among 4 same-topic options. Exactly the AlphabetPractice mechanic generalised. Missing: nothing; TTS calls count against allowance (PhraseAudio error 'limit'), cache 32 clips per tab.
findings.recommendation: Generalise AlphabetPractice into an engine item type.

findings.title: Feasibility: Listen-and-type dictation
findings.evidence: Sources: vocabulary term, example.nl, topic reading/listening text split by dutchSentences (apps/web/lib/client/sentences.ts:2-6), sample.nl; TTS via PhraseAudio
findings.detail: Fully generatable. Missing: a tolerant comparator on the web (case/punctuation/diacritics normalisation, token-level diff, accept missing article) – server has normalise/lemma_key in apps/api/src/dlp/domains/stories/validator.py:59,74 that could be mirrored or exposed.
findings.recommendation: Add a small shared compare utility (token diff with highlighted errors) used by dictation, typed recall and translation items.

findings.title: Feasibility: Typed-recall flashcards
findings.evidence: VocabularyRecall.tsx:35 already renders an input; vocabulary meaning.en/fa → term
findings.detail: Cue meaning (support language), learner types Dutch term; check tolerant (article optional/required as a setting). Missing: synonym/variant list (LEARNING_DESIGN.md:17 notes synonyms can be valid) – fall back to 'I was right' override.
findings.recommendation: Check the existing input, then map result to SRS grade instead of pure self-rating.

findings.title: Feasibility: de/het sorting
findings.evidence: library vocabulary terms with article: pre-a1/a1/pre-a2 de 220 / het 89; a2 de 241 / het 89; b1 de 257 / het 93; pre-b2..pre-c1 de 344 / het 57; c1 de 491 / het 9; curriculum a1 grammar 'De, het en een' (path.json)
findings.detail: Strip the article and ask de or het (swipe/tap two bins). Strong pool at A–B2; C-levels are 98% de, so low value there. Missing: plurals/diminutive rules (none authored).
findings.recommendation: Offer as a speed round at pre-A1..B2.

findings.title: Feasibility: Sentence builder (word-order tiles)
findings.evidence: vocabulary example.nl median length 6–23 words (a2 median 6, a1 10, b1 16, pre-c1 23); grammar examples (path.json grammar[].examples[].nl); conversations steps[].example.nl; speaking/writing sample.nl; translation cues example.en/fa
findings.detail: Tokenise sentence, shuffle tiles, learner taps in order; cue = English/Persian translation. Best for ≤10 tokens (A-levels, a2 examples). Missing: accepted alternative orders (e.g. inversion 'Morgen ga ik…' vs 'Ik ga morgen…') – restrict to sentences where only one order is natural, or accept any order whose string equals an authored variant; punctuation/capitalisation normalisation.
findings.recommendation: Use for V2/inversion and subordinate-clause practice tied to grammar items (pre-b1 'want en omdat', b1 relative clauses).

findings.title: Feasibility: Sentence / paragraph ordering
findings.evidence: practice reading.text.nl has 2 paragraphs split by \n\n in all topics; b2 options are text sentences (b2-t001 questions); library stories paragraphs[2]
findings.detail: Split with dutchSentences and ask learner to restore order; at B2+ the narrative sequence questions already target this. Missing: nothing.
findings.recommendation: Use as a post-reading item, especially where MCQ answers are verbatim sentences.

findings.title: Feasibility: Odd-one-out and speed rounds
findings.evidence: library vocabulary topic groups; practice questions 400/stage; story question 100/stage
findings.detail: Odd-one-out: 3 terms from one topic + 1 from another. Speed round: timed batch of match/de-het/listen-choose/MCQ items with streak counter. Missing: client timer & scoring only.
findings.recommendation: Use as optional 'challenge' mode; points via today.add_points.

findings.title: Feasibility: Shadowing / repeat-after-me with the existing recogniser
findings.evidence: CurriculumRecorder onReady(assetId, transcript) CurriculumControls.tsx:139; SpeechCheck uses keep_recording=false (SpeechCheck.tsx:46); read_aloud_result apps/api/src/dlp/domains/stories/service.py:493-508 (bag-of-words match tied to StoryEpisode); D-20 docs/DECISIONS.md
findings.detail: Play TTS of a short sentence, record, compare transcript tokens to target, show matched/missed words. Missing: a generic endpoint (current read-aloud is episode-specific) or client-side comparison of the transcript returned by speech/transcribe; must not be presented as a pronunciation score (D-20).
findings.recommendation: Add POST speech/read-aloud {text} returning matched/missed using the same tokens()/matching logic; no storage.

findings.title: Feasibility: Translate-to-Dutch with tolerant checking
findings.evidence: example.en/.fa ↔ example.nl; sample.en ↔ sample.nl; assess_productive pattern curriculum/service.py:206-246 (LLM judge with grounded quotes)
findings.detail: Prompts exist; checking needs either strict comparison (too harsh – many valid translations) or an LLM judge (Azure OpenAI) using the existing quote-grounding validation. Missing: an endpoint and per-call allowance budget.
findings.recommendation: Use exact/near match first, LLM fallback only when the near match fails.

findings.title: Feasibility: Error correction
findings.evidence: No authored erroneous sentences in content; deliberately wrong grammar options exist (path.json pre-a1 g2 'Blauw tafel ik.'); WritingCoach corrections {original, replacement, category} (WritingCoach.tsx:9) not persisted (writing.py has no session.add)
findings.detail: Can be synthesised by deterministic corruption of example sentences (swap de/het, move finite verb out of V2, drop 'te') or by an LLM generator; personal error items would need WritingCoach corrections to be stored.
findings.recommendation: Start with deterministic de/het and verb-position corruptions; later persist learner corrections as personal items.

findings.title: Feasibility: Verb-conjugation drills – NOT feasible from current content
findings.evidence: library vocabulary terms glossed 'to …': pre-a1 1 ('links', mis-gloss), a1 1, all other stages 0; curriculum grammar has a handful of verb topics (zijn, heten, wonen, perfectum, separable verbs, irregular participles) with 1 practice question each
findings.detail: There is no infinitive/present/past/participle/auxiliary data. Conjugation drills require a new verb table (authored or LLM-generated then validated) – e.g. content/verbs.json {infinitive, present{ik,jij,hij,…}, imperfect, participle, auxiliary, separable_prefix, en, fa, stage}.
findings.recommendation: Add a small authored verb bank (100–200 verbs) via a content_build script; do not promise conjugation drills before that.

findings.title: Feasibility: Mixed 8–12 item session with progress, hearts and summary
findings.evidence: TopicDetail bundle (topics.py:174-195): 5 vocabulary cards (term/meaning/example), reading text, listening text, 4 MCQ, speaking/writing sample; VocabularyRecall round/missed/summary loop (VocabularyRecall.tsx:18-28,37); today.add_points (stories/today.py:23)
findings.detail: Per topic: 2 match/listen-choose items from the 5 words, 2 cloze/typed recall, 1 dictation from a text sentence, 1 sentence builder from the sample, 2–4 comprehension items with instant feedback, 1 shadowing item, optional open production at the end. Missing: session runner, per-item check endpoint for topic questions (keys are stripped), points endpoint, SRS hook. Hearts/lives would conflict with D-19 'never a judgement' – use non-punitive progress + retry queue instead, or consciously revise D-19.
findings.recommendation: Make this the default 'Start' action of every topic and of the leerpad.
