constraints: D-19 (docs/DECISIONS.md:203-209): points reward doing and are never a judgement of the learner's Dutch; the word bank only contains words the learner saved. Hearts/lives or score-shaming would need a conscious revision of this decision.

D-20 (docs/DECISIONS.md): read-aloud compares recognised words; no pronunciation or accent score may be shown. Shadowing items must keep that framing (also CURRICULUM.md:131-133, LEARNING_DESIGN.md recognition note).

Final-check answers, listening transcripts, translations and model answers must stay withheld before submission (curriculum/service.py:283-297; LEARNING_DESIGN.md 'Support and independent evidence'). Practice-mode keys must never leak into the final test.

Topic practice completion semantics: receptive completion requires the submitted answers to pass (75%); productive completion is a substantive attempt; completion is sticky (docs/TOPIC_PRACTICE.md:27-36; topics.py:247-251). Topic practice satisfies the stage prerequisite for the final check.

LLM calls are allowance-metered (usage.reserve in assess_productive, writing feedback, conversation turns) and TTS has a 'limit' error path; new item types should prefer client-side checking and cache audio.
Content is explicitly 'unreviewed'; generated drills inherit that status and must not claim CEFR calibration (TOPIC_PRACTICE.md:55-57, PRACTICE_LIBRARY.md:36-38).
Dutch is the practice language; English/Persian are optional support and Persian must keep lang=fa dir=rtl (LanguageSupport.tsx:41; LEARNING_DESIGN.md).
Belgian Standard Dutch (nl-BE) for TTS, sentence segmentation and LLM prompts.
Accessibility conventions already enforced by e2e/axe tests (focus after commit, aria-live status, reduced motion) – any animation must respect prefers-reduced-motion.
open_questions: Is the cross-stage reuse (same 500 terms for pre-A1/A1/pre-A2; same listening texts across three stages; Story Time == topic reading text) intentional product design or a builder shortcut? PRACTICE_LIBRARY.md:26-27 claims some intentional spiralling, but the extent was not discussed anywhere I found.
Does the owner accept non-punitive mechanics only (per D-19), or should hearts/lives be introduced as an explicit design change?

Is Azure Speech pronunciation assessment for nl-BE intended for production? Nothing in the repo uses it (not verified against the Azure adapter in apps/api/src/dlp/providers/speech_azure.py beyond its header).
What are the production TTS and LLM allowance limits per learner per day? Dictation- and shadowing-heavy sessions would multiply speech/synthesize calls. The values were not read from config.
Should practice-mode answer keys be sent to the client for instant feedback, or should a per-item check endpoint be added? This is a trade-off between security/evidence integrity and latency.

The runtime UI was not observed (no dev server run). Visual monotony is inferred from code and CSS (topics.css, learning.css), not from screenshots. docs/previews has PNGs only for the today/episode/video screens.
The content builders scripts/content_build/practice_*.py were not read in detail. Whether they can cheaply emit extra fields (accepted alternatives, verb forms, distractor sets) is unverified.

How do the multiple :root palettes (globals.css, design.css, learning.css all define --accent with different values, imported in that order in layout.tsx:10-19) interact on practice screens? The effective accent is likely learning.css #2455b5. Not visually verified.

areas.area: Visual design system and interactivity (apps/web CSS, shell, icons, Today home, feature component class usage, preview screenshots)
areas.overview:
The web app has no CSS modules, no utility framework and no design-token file. All styling lives in 10 global stylesheets imported in a fixed order by apps/web/app/layout.tsx:10-19: globals.css, design.css, learning.css, learning-tools.css, library.css, phrase-audio.css, topics.css, learning-agents.css, stories.css, videos.css. Together they are 2,845 lines, about 104 KB and about 1,190 rule blocks. Line counts: design 1711, globals 425, learning 317, stories 182, videos 53, library 41, topics 36, phrase-audio 36, learning-agents 25, learning-tools 19. learning-agents, library and topics are written minified with many rules per line, so their line counts understate their size.

The files are three historical redesigns stacked by cascade order, not one system.
(1) globals.css (17 Sep, release 0.1) is a functional base. Its :root has a beige/green palette: --accent #0b5d4b, --radius 10px, Segoe UI.
(2) design.css (22 Sep, "Redesign the learner workspace") redefines :root with sage green (--accent #225b49, --ink #223a35, --radius 18px, DM Sans). It adds the sidebar shell, a large illustrated "mission-hero" dashboard, a lesson layout, a speech studio, breakpoints and the reduced-motion and print blocks.
(3) learning.css (24 Sep) redefines :root a third time with navy/blue (--accent #2455b5, --ink #182c47, --radius 16px). It re-skins the shell (brand mark, nav current state, sticky header, button hover) and adds the curriculum path, lesson workspace, tests and results.
Later feature files add their own literal hex colours: library, topics, learning-agents, learning-tools and phrase-audio are all navy/blue, with 0 var() uses in four of them. stories.css (2 Oct) adds a warm orange token set and six gradient "tone" pairs for episode covers. videos.css reuses those tones.

Because the three :root blocks have equal specificity, the live tokens are a mix:
- from learning.css: bg, surface, ink, muted, line, accent, ok-bg/ink, radius
- from design.css: accent-ink, warn-bg/ink, fonts
- from globals.css: bad-bg/ink

There are no tokens for spacing, the type scale, weights, shadows, z-index, motion or breakpoints. The CSS contains 356 distinct hex values. Radii include 2–22px literals, 50% and 999px. There are 14 different breakpoints (430/480/520/600/640/650/700/767/768/850/960/1050/1250/1600).

Much of the green design.css layer is still live on screens the blue layer never re-skinned. Examples: the mission lesson step list (.step-list current #eaf2e9 / .step-number #315c45), checked answers (.question label:has(input:checked) #edf3e8), .dutch-text border #829c77, conversation bubbles (#f6f8f2/#e4edde), .mic-orbit, .information-callout, .label.neutral and the textarea borders. So the missions, speech-check, progress and settings pages mix sage green into a navy theme.

About 500 lines of design.css (about 30%) style an old dashboard that no longer renders: .mission-hero, .mission-art, .art-*, .hero-*, .focus-card, .skill-card, .skill-overview, .studio-card, .activity-card, .dashboard-top/bottom, .integrity-note, .text-link, .button.light, .step-segments, .status-dot, .sidebar-note, .language-pill. globals.css has dead .site-header, .site-nav, .mission-hero and .skill-overview rules. Many selectors are defined two or three times (.button, .card, .label, .brand, .site-main, .site-footer, .step-list button, .question label, .help-ladder .rung, .dutch-text, .conversation, .bubble, .lesson-layout, .eyebrow, h1/h2), and overrides depend on import order plus 11 !important declarations.

The shell is components/AppShell.tsx. It renders a fixed 224px white sidebar with a CSS text brand mark "t." and 9 nav links, each with a monochrome stroke icon from components/Icon.tsx (20 icons, stroke 1.65, currentColor). It also has a sticky header with a breadcrumb, a language select (LanguageSupport.tsx) and a profile button. Below 1050px a fixed bottom nav shows 6 items. Fonts are DM Sans Variable and Vazirmatn Variable, self-hosted through @fontsource-variable (layout.tsx:7-8); the CSP allows only font-src 'self'. html is fixed to lang="nl". Persian support text is set per element with lang="fa" dir="rtl" and the .fa class; layout CSS mostly uses physical properties. There is no dark mode and no color-scheme.

Motion is almost absent:
- one @keyframes (`dots`, the "writer is busy" indicator)
- five transitions (nav link background, .button, episode-card hover lift, goal-bar width, video scene highlight)
- no :active states anywhere
- no celebration moments

Reduced motion is handled by a universal kill switch at design.css:1684-1693.

Progress is shown as:
- a static border "streak ring" whose colour flips when active; it does not show the fraction of the goal
- linear bars: .goal-bar, .path-progress, native <progress> in topics
- 14 day dots
- a flat 3-column grid of 12 stage cards; there is no path map

Answer feedback in the curriculum and topic practice is a green or amber text block under each question (.practice-correct / .practice-hint). The options themselves are never marked correct or incorrect. Only the episode questions colour the whole question card (is-correct / is-wrong) and outline the right option. The .practice-feedback box has unused modifier classes complete/retry, so success and retry look identical.

What the screenshots in docs/previews show: a light grey canvas with uniform white cards (1px #dfe5ed border, almost no shadow), navy text and a single blue primary button. Colour comes only from the CSS gradient episode covers and video posters (orange tone-1, blue tone-3, gold tone-5) and the orange word count. That is 2–3 hues on mostly neutral surfaces. Hierarchy rests on type size alone. Rows of identical outline buttons ("Lees hardop", "Bewaar") make the reading pages monotonous. A first-run learner sees a home screen full of zeros: 0 dagen, 0/20 punten, 0 woorden, 14 grey dots. There are no images or illustrations: there is no public/ directory, and the CSP sets img-src to 'self' data: blob:. Many live labels are 7–10px (brand caption, step-skill, section eyebrows, .label, footer, mobile nav).

The e2e suite ties the design to the code. Ten specs run axe WCAG 2.1 AA checks, design.spec.ts screenshots at 1440/390/320 and asserts no horizontal overflow, and tests use about 70 distinct class selectors, 164 getByTestId calls and exact heading text.

key_files.role: Imports fonts (DM Sans Variable, Vazirmatn Variable) and the 10 global stylesheets in cascade order (lines 7-19); html lang=nl; metadata; wraps LanguageProvider + AppShell.

Release-0.1 functional base: first :root (lines 1-18, beige/green), skip-link, .card, .button, .label ok/warn/bad, .fa/.nl direction helpers, lesson/question/help-ladder/conversation/bubble/checklist/linklike/connection-banner base rules; contains dead .site-header/.site-nav/.mission-hero/.skill-overview.

Sage-green redesign layer (1711 lines): second :root (2-17), typography, :focus-visible #ad7b26, sidebar/header/mobile-nav shell, .button variants + hover, page-heading/eyebrow/quiet-badge, icon-tile sage/sand/lilac/peach, section-heading, card/label overrides, progress/settings/profile facts, lesson-layout/step-list/step-number, question/textarea/conversation/bubble/mic-orbit overrides, all main breakpoints (1250/1050/767/430), reduced-motion (1684-1693), print (1694-1711). ~30% dead dashboard CSS (lines ~336-840 plus media-query parts).

Navy/blue layer: third :root (2-12) that wins for bg/ink/muted/line/accent/radius/ok; re-skins shell, buttons, nav current state; curriculum path (continue-panel, stage-grid/stage-card), lesson workspace (unit-sidebar, vocabulary/grammar cards, curriculum-question/answer-options, practice-correct/hint/feedback, story-panel, curriculum-audio/recorder, writing-workspace), test (test-tabs, test-paper, result-banner, skill-result), course-progress rows.

Warm accent tokens (--warm, --warm-ink, --warm-bg) and 6 tone gradient pairs (lines 2-12); episode covers; Today grid, streak ring, goal bar, day dots, words-card, wish/cast cards; episode reader, glossary, episode questions is-correct/is-wrong, choice buttons; library tiles; flashcard + grade buttons; the only @keyframes (dots, line 44).
Video library tiles/posters (reuses tone-3/tone-5), player stage, scene list with .scene.is-active highlight and transition.
Practice-source segmented switch, topic library intro/progress summary (native <progress>), filters, topic tiles, topic reader details panels, feedback criteria; literal blue hex only.
Practice coach recommendations and topic conversation UI (messages, partner/learner bubbles, composer, summary); minified, literal blue hex only.

Word/story library intro, filters, pagination, story tiles/covers (cover-1..3), story reader paper, writing coach correction diff (del/ins); has a reduced-motion rule for transitions that do not exist.
Round phrase audio button (.is-playing state), its own focus colour #527baa, alphabet picker/focus/quiz/pairs.
Vocabulary recall tool and communication coach details panel.
Sidebar + header + mobile bottom nav; nav link list with labels/icons/mobile flags (lines 14-46); brand mark markup; footer; navigation guard.
Inline SVG icon set: 20 names, 24px viewBox, stroke 1.65, currentColor, aria-hidden.

Home screen: headline by next_step, episode card/pending/failed states with covers, streak ring (role=img), goal bar, day dots, words/video cards, wish form, cast list, bottom links; exports coverClass() and EpisodeCard.
Exports `skills` array (reading/listening/speaking/writing with icon and colour sage/sand/lilac/peach), the only per-skill colour mapping; used by ProgressOverview.
CurriculumQuestions (answer options with .selected only; after checking, a practice-correct/practice-hint block per question), CurriculumAudio, CurriculumRecorder (.record-symbol, is-recording).
Topic library and reader for the four skills; feedback box with unstyled complete/retry modifiers; per-skill icon map (line 16).
Episode reading page: paragraphs with PhraseAudio and ReadAloud (returns points), glossary Bewaar buttons, questions with is-correct/is-wrong, choice buttons.
Leerpad: continue panel with path-progress bar, PracticeCoach, flat 12-card stage grid.
Regression gate: axe WCAG 2.1 A/AA = 0 violations and no horizontal overflow at 1440/390/320 on 5 screens plus the lesson; asserts heading texts and the streak role=img name.
CSP: style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline', font-src 'self', img-src 'self' data: blob:. Limits what assets a redesign may load.
Six Chromium renders with fixture data (today desktop/phone, episode, videos, video desktop/phone).
Line 44 records the deliberate decision: 'A restrained navy/blue palette; high-contrast text…'

strengths: Accessibility is enforced: axe WCAG 2.1 A/AA with zero violations at 1440/390/320 across 10 e2e specs, a no-horizontal-overflow assertion, a skip link, focus-visible outlines, 44px minimum touch targets on .button (globals.css:153), visually-hidden labels, a role=img streak with an aria-label, and aria-pressed/aria-current used as state hooks.
Reduced motion is handled globally (design.css:1684-1693) and for the writing-dots animation (stories.css:45). A print stylesheet exists (design.css:1694-1711).
Fonts are self-hosted variable fonts (DM Sans, plus Vazirmatn for Persian) through @fontsource-variable, which fits the strict CSP font-src 'self'.
Bilingual and RTL support text is handled with lang plus dir=rtl and the .fa class (globals.css:203-208; LanguageSupport.tsx:35-43). HelpLadder uses dir=auto for mixed glosses.

A few genuinely engaging patterns already exist to build on: gradient episode covers with pseudo-element art (stories.css:16-26), video posters with a play disc (videos.css:16-22), the transcript scene that tracks playback (.scene.is-active, videos.css:39-43), grade buttons tinted by intent (stories.css:154), branching-story choice buttons on a navy panel (stories.css:120-130), and the writing-coach del/ins diff (library.css:32).

Responsive behaviour is thought through: the sidebar becomes a bottom nav at 1050px, step lists turn into horizontal scroll-snap strips on phones (design.css:1531-1547), and the unit sidebar becomes a segmented control on mobile (learning.css:237-241).
Components consistently use semantic HTML (fieldset/legend for questions, dl for facts, ol for steps and path, details/summary for optional help), which keeps restyling safe.

findings.title: Three competing :root token layers; the live palette depends on import order
findings.evidence: globals.css:1-18 (--accent #0b5d4b, --radius 10px); design.css:2-17 (--accent #225b49, --radius 18px, fonts); learning.css:2-12 (--accent #2455b5, --ink #182c47, --radius 16px); stories.css:2-12 (--warm, --tone-1..6); import order layout.tsx:10-19. Live values: bg #f5f6f8, surface #fff, ink #182c47, muted #58667a, line #dfe5ed, accent #2455b5, accent-ink #fff, radius 16px, ok #eaf4ef/#216045 (learning.css); warn #faf1d9/#735218 and fonts (design.css); bad #fbe6e3/#8a2a1c (globals.css). ContentReviewQueue.tsx:101 references an undefined --border.
findings.detail: No single file owns the tokens. There are no tokens for spacing, type scale, font weight, shadow/elevation, z-index, motion or breakpoints. The CSS holds 356 distinct hex values (design 116, learning 83, stories 38, library 33, topics 27, phrase-audio 24, learning-agents 22). Four feature files make 0 var() calls and hard-code the navy/blue palette. Radii are literals from 2 to 22px. --radius is effectively used only by the remaining globals.css rules.
findings.recommendation: Create one tokens file (for example app/tokens.css imported first) with primitive scales (colour ramps, space-1..8, radius-sm..xl/pill, text-xs..3xl, weight, shadow-1..4, dur-fast/base/slow, ease-standard/emphasized, z-index) and semantic aliases (--surface-1/2/sunken/inverse, --text-strong/muted, --border, --accent, --success/warning/danger/info with -bg/-ink/-border, and per-skill accents). Wrap the stylesheets in @layer tokens, base, components, features, utilities so overrides stop depending on import order. Delete the :root blocks in globals.css, design.css and learning.css after migration.

findings.title: Legacy sage-green styles still render inside the navy/blue theme
findings.evidence: design.css:1012-1016 (.step-list current #eaf2e9/#2d593f), 1029-1033 (.step-number #315c45), 1117-1120 (.question label:has(input:checked) #edf3e8/#8aa782), 1085 (.dutch-text border #829c77), 1170/1187 (.conversation #f6f8f2, .bubble.learner #e4edde), 1235-1244 (.mic-orbit greens), 937-938 (.information-callout #ecf2ec/#48634f), 645-660 (.sage/.sand/.lilac/.peach), 871-874 (.label.neutral), 1147-1148 (textarea #fcfdfa/#dce4d7), 1131 (.help-ladder .rung #f6f6ee). These are used by LessonShell.tsx, SpeakingStep.tsx, SpeechCheck.tsx, ProgressOverview.tsx, AccountSettings.tsx, StepHeader.tsx and the speech-check, progress and settings pages.
findings.detail: learning.css re-skinned only the shell and the curriculum screens. The mission lessons (/missions/[id]), speech studio, progress and settings still show green highlights next to blue buttons and links. The brand also disagrees: app/icon.svg uses #245d4c green with a gold dot, while the sidebar .brand-mark is navy #1d365d with a #9cc3fc dot (learning.css:17-18).
findings.recommendation: When introducing semantic tokens, map each of these legacy selectors to tokens (for example selected = --accent-subtle, current step = --accent, learner bubble = --accent-subtle). Update icon.svg to the chosen brand palette. Screenshot /missions/appointment-change, /speech-check, /progress and /settings before and after, since docs/previews has no captures of them.

findings.title: About 500 dead lines and widespread duplicate selectors
findings.evidence: Class-usage grep across components and app TSX returned 0 for: mission-hero, mission-copy, mission-art, art-card/orbit/calendar/message/spark, hero-eyebrow/meta/foot/level, live-dot, step-segments, focus-card, focus-note, skill-card, skill-overview, skill-index, status-dot, studio-card, circle-arrow, activity-card, dashboard-top, dashboard-bottom, integrity-note, little-orbit, sidebar-note, language-pill, text-link, button.light, review-count, stage-locked, site-header, site-nav. Ranges: design.css ~336-408, 437-630, 676-755, 791-840 plus parts of the media queries at 1273-1313, 1418-1517 and 1596-1668; globals.css 52-72, 116-127, 130; library.css:35 targets transitions that do not exist. Duplicated selectors across files include .button (globals:144, design:409, learning:37), .card (globals:101, design:855), .site-main (globals:78, design:276, learning:32), .brand, .label, .step-list button, .question label, .dutch-text, .conversation, .bubble, .help-ladder .rung, .eyebrow, h1/h2. design.css has 11 !important declarations.
findings.detail: Dead and overlapping rules make it hard to predict what a change will affect. Several global names are reused across unrelated features: .wish-card and .cast-card (stories.css) are used by VideoLibrary.tsx:110/133 and WordReview.tsx:80; .stage-link (learning.css:79) is used by VideoLibrary.tsx:46 and EpisodeReader.tsx:78; .words-card is used for the video card in TodayHome.tsx:118. The class names no longer describe what they style.
findings.recommendation: Delete the dead blocks first (no test references them, and curriculum.spec.ts:10 asserts .stage-locked has count 0, so removing its CSS is safe). Then collapse each duplicated selector into one component-layer rule. Rename the cross-feature classes to neutral primitives (for example .panel, .tile-link, .action-row) while keeping the old class names as aliases wherever e2e tests select them.

findings.title: Palette is effectively monochrome; colour appears only on covers
findings.evidence: docs/previews/today-desktop.png, episode-desktop.png, videos-desktop.png, video-desktop.png: white cards on #f5f6f8 with navy text and a single blue (#2455b5) primary button. Saturated colour appears only in .episode-cover tone gradients (stories.css:19-24), .video-poster (videos.css:16-17) and .words-count warm-ink (stories.css:68). Per-skill colour exists only in LearningOverview.tsx:7-42 (sage/sand/lilac/peach), and only ProgressOverview.tsx:60 uses it. The unit sidebar (learning.css:99-101), test tabs (learning.css:176-179) and topic tiles (topics.css:17-20) all use the same blue.
findings.detail: Across the screenshots there are 2–3 hues: navy/blue, orange, and gold on the videos page. Green appears only in small 'ok' labels. Every card has the same weight (white, 1px #dfe5ed border, shadow 0 2px 3px #243c3302). Primary and secondary actions differ only by fill. The four skills, words, grammar, stories and video have no visual identity, so a learner cannot tell sections apart at a glance. This matches the owner's 'boring' feedback and the deliberate 'restrained navy/blue palette' in docs/LEARNING_DESIGN.md:44.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a semantic accent per section and skill. Suggested starting points that reuse existing hues: Lezen = blue (tone-3), Luisteren = teal/green (tone-2), Spreken = violet (tone-4), Schrijven = orange (tone-1), Woorden = gold (tone-5), Verhalen = rose (tone-6), each with -solid/-subtle/-ink variants checked for AA contrast. Apply them through a data-skill or data-section attribute that sets --accent-local on the container, so components such as .unit-sidebar nav button[aria-current], .topic-tile, .stage-card, .practice-recommendations li, .test-tabs, IconTile and progress bars inherit the colour. Files: the new tokens.css, learning.css, topics.css, learning-agents.css, CurriculumLesson.tsx (sections array lines 20-25), SkillTopicPractice.tsx:16, AppShell.tsx links (lines 14-46: add a colour per link for the nav icon tile). Record the decision change in docs/LEARNING_DESIGN.md:44.

findings.title: Almost no motion, micro-interaction or celebration
findings.evidence: The only @keyframes is `dots` (stories.css:44). Transitions: design.css:140-142 (.primary-nav a), design.css:420-423 (.button; its transform transition is never triggered), stories.css:33-34 (a.episode-card hover translateY(-2px)), stories.css:59 (.goal-bar width), videos.css:39 (.scene). No :active rules exist in any CSS file. Hover-only changes without transitions: stories.css:67, 126, 153; phrase-audio.css:3; videos.css:42. Completion is plain text: CurriculumLesson.tsx:95 ('Een stap verder.'), SkillTopicPractice.tsx:182, TodayHome.tsx:110 ('Dagdoel gehaald…'), WordReview.tsx:60 ('Klaar voor vandaag.').
findings.detail: Pressing a button, choosing an answer, revealing a flashcard (WordReview.tsx:68-72 swaps content instantly), finishing a skill or reaching the daily goal gives no motion feedback. ReadAloud already returns points (EpisodeReader.tsx:122 '+N punten') but shows them as inline text. Recording states change only colour (.is-recording .record-symbol, learning.css:156; .mic-orbit.recording, design.css:1241).
findings.recommendation: Add motion tokens and a small keyframe library in the component layer: press (scale .97 on :active), lift (hover translateY plus shadow step for tiles), pop (correct option), gentle shake (incorrect, ≤4px), fill (ring and bar progress), flip (flashcard reveal), pulse (recording ring around .record-symbol/.mic-orbit/.button.talk[aria-pressed=true]), shimmer (skeleton loading to replace the .path-loading text boxes), and a lightweight CSS/SVG burst for daily-goal and stage completion. Toast the points gain. Keep everything inside the existing prefers-reduced-motion block (design.css:1684), which already neutralises durations. Pure CSS is enough; adding a library such as Framer Motion would be a new dependency decision (package.json has only next, react, fontsource and jose).

findings.title: Answer feedback does not mark the options themselves; success and retry boxes look the same
findings.evidence: CurriculumControls.tsx:16-17: an option label only gets class 'selected' (learning.css:127, blue). After checking, a separate .practice-correct (learning.css:130, green) or .practice-hint (learning.css:131, amber) block appears. SkillTopicPractice.tsx:182 and CurriculumLesson.tsx:95 render `practice-feedback complete|retry`, but no CSS defines .complete or .retry; .practice-feedback is always light blue (learning.css:166). Only EpisodeReader.tsx:157-159 colours whole questions (stories.css:114-118: .is-correct, .is-wrong, label.is-answer outline). Mission QuestionList.tsx:92 uses .label ok/bad pills.
findings.detail: Three different correctness patterns exist (curriculum/topics, episodes, missions). None marks the chosen wrong option against the right one with icon and colour. .practice-hint (amber, meaning 'hint/warning') is also used for neutral or success notices: TodayHome.tsx:145 ('Je wens staat in de wachtrij'), EpisodeReader.tsx:143 ('staat in je woordenlijst'), WordReview.tsx:88 and VideoPlayer.tsx:137, which blurs the meaning of the colours.
findings.recommendation: Extract an AnswerOption primitive with states default / hover / selected / correct / incorrect / reveal-correct / disabled, each with an icon (check/close) and not colour alone. Use it in CurriculumQuestions, the episode and video questions, and QuestionList. Extract a Notice/Callout primitive with tone info/success/warning/danger (replacing .practice-correct, .practice-hint, .error, .information-callout, .practice-feedback, .connection-banner), and style .practice-feedback.complete as success and .retry as warning. Keep the existing class names (.practice-correct, .practice-hint, .practice-feedback) as aliases because skill-topics.spec.ts:92-102, curriculum.spec.ts:43-50 and library-writing.spec.ts:143-146 select them.

findings.title: Weak progress visualisation and no path map
findings.evidence: The streak ring is a static 8px border whose colour flips (stories.css:49-52; TodayHome.tsx:100-103) and does not show goal completion. Linear bars: .goal-bar (stories.css:58-59), .path-progress (learning.css:63-64), native <progress> (topics.css:10-11). Day dots: stories.css:61-64. The stage grid is 12 equal cards, 3 columns (learning.css:68-82; CurriculumPath.tsx:34-39), current stage shown by a border ring only (learning.css:70). Skill completion is the text '0 / 4 vaardigheden' (CurriculumPath.tsx:37). The unit test card shows the text 'N van 4 vaardigheden geoefend' (CurriculumLesson.tsx:81).
findings.detail: The data for richer progress is already loaded: goal.points/target, streak, recent_days (TodayHome.tsx:48-49), stage.passed and practice_completed per stage (CurriculumPath.tsx), topic completed_count/total_topics per skill (SkillTopicPractice.tsx:55). It is shown as numbers and thin bars, so learners cannot see where they are on the journey. That fits the owner's 'not sure how it helps me learn' feedback.
findings.recommendation: Build ProgressRing (SVG with conic or stroke-dasharray, role=img or progressbar with the same aria text) for the daily goal inside the streak card, keeping role=img and the aria-label /dag(en)? op rij/ that design.spec.ts:48 needs. Add a four-segment skill meter (per-skill colours) to each stage card and to the unit sidebar. Replace or augment .stage-grid with a connected path map (nodes plus connector line, current node pulsing, passed nodes filled) while keeping data-testid='curriculum-path' and 12 li children (design.spec.ts:46, curriculum.spec.ts:7).

findings.title: Tiny typography in live components
findings.evidence: brand-caption 8px (design.css:113, learning.css:19); .step-skill 8px (design.css:1035); .section-heading .eyebrow 8px, and 7px under 767px (design.css:673, 1486); .vocabulary-card .eyebrow 8px (learning.css:112); .label 9px (design.css:866); .site-footer 10px, and 8px under 767px (design.css:291, 1392); .mobile-nav a 9px (design.css:1350); .eyebrow 10px (learning.css:36); .skill-card/.record-note 10px. 61 font-size declarations are 10px or below, 18 of them 7–8px.
findings.detail: The body is 15px, but the many uppercase micro-labels at 7–10px read as faint metadata clutter. 'NIEUWE WOORDEN' in episode-desktop.png and the footer in every screenshot are examples. axe does not flag font size.
findings.recommendation: Define a rem-based type scale with a 12px floor for labels and eyebrows (11px only for uppercase with letter-spacing), and use clamp() for display sizes. Replace the literal px sizes in design.css and learning.css when migrating to tokens.

findings.title: Four different focus-ring colours; the amber ring is low contrast on white
findings.evidence: globals.css:163-169 and 286 (#f2b233, 3px, for .button, a, input, textarea, .table-scroll); design.css:59-62 (#ad7b26 for all other :focus-visible); phrase-audio.css:5 (#527baa); learning-agents.css:19 (#245d9b, 2px).
findings.detail: Computed relative luminance gives roughly 1.9:1 for #f2b233 against white #fff, below the 3:1 non-text contrast generally expected for focus indicators (WCAG 1.4.11). #ad7b26 is about 3.7:1. axe does not test focus indicators, so CI would not catch this.
findings.recommendation: Use a single --focus-ring token (for example a 2px ring of --accent with a 2px white offset, or a darker amber of at least 3:1 on both white and accent fills) applied once through :focus-visible in the base layer. Remove the per-component outlines.

findings.title: Limited iconography and no illustration assets
findings.evidence: Icon.tsx:3-23 has 20 names. 'book' means Verhalen (AppShell.tsx:17), the Woorden/Lezen/Story Time sections (CurriculumLesson.tsx:21-24) and Praktijkgesprekken (TodayHome.tsx:156, CurriculumPath.tsx:41). 'check' is the Woorden nav icon (AppShell.tsx:19). 'chart' means both progress and Mijn leerpad (TodayHome.tsx:155). There is no apps/web/public directory; the only art is CSS (covers, the Belgian flag at design.css:204-217, the dead .mission-art at design.css:473-588). The CSP allows img-src 'self' data: blob: and font-src 'self' (proxy.ts:11-13).
findings.detail: Icons cannot carry meaning or delight: there is no flame (streak), star/trophy, lock, chat bubble, sparkle, lightbulb (hint), bookmark (save word), refresh or x-circle (incorrect). Empty and first-run states have no visuals.
findings.recommendation: Extend Icon.tsx with the missing glyphs and give each section one distinct icon. Add an IconTile primitive that colours the icon with the section accent (generalising .icon-tile + .sage/.sand/.lilac/.peach at design.css:631-660). Ship any illustrations as local inline SVG components, or files in a new public/ directory, to stay within the CSP.

findings.title: First-run and empty states are zero-heavy and unexplained
findings.evidence:
today-desktop.png and today-phone.png show '0 dagen op rij', '0 / 20 punten', '0 dagen', '0', 14 grey dots, an empty goal bar and '0 woorden om te herhalen'. Empty patterns differ: .empty-state is used only in error.tsx and not-found.tsx (design.css:841-854); .topic-empty is a dashed box (topics.css:24; SkillTopicPractice.tsx:64); the video library uses a plain muted

(VideoLibrary.tsx:130); progress uses a plain muted p (ProgressOverview.tsx:102-104). Loading is always a white text box (.path-loading, learning.css:50, in 7 places).
findings.detail: Nothing on the home screen explains the learning loop (story → words → conversation → review) or how the sections relate. With 9 nav destinations (AppShell.tsx:14-46) and two story concepts ('Verhalen' serial vs 'Story Time' in CurriculumLesson.tsx:24), a new learner has no orientation.
findings.recommendation: Create an EmptyState primitive (icon or illustration, title, one sentence, primary action) and a Skeleton primitive. On TodayHome, when streak.active_days === 0, show a first-run 'Zo werkt Taalstudio' strip: 3–4 coloured step tiles using the section accents, linking to the episode, words and conversation. Replace zero stats with an encouraging starting state instead of '0'.

findings.title: Breakpoint sprawl, physical CSS properties and no dark mode
findings.evidence: Max-width breakpoints 430/480/520/600/640/650/700/767/850/960/1050/1250 and min-width 768/1600 (from a grep of all @media rules). Physical properties: .word-example border-left (learning.css:116), .grammar-examples border-left (learning.css:120), .conversation-learner margin-left 12% (learning-agents.css:18), .communication-phrases li border-left (learning-tools.css:17), .step-list button text-align:left (globals.css:233). Only about 4 logical-property uses (globals.css:188, 269; design.css:1670; plus inline styles in LessonShell.tsx:300, ListeningStep.tsx:103, WritingStep.tsx:214). No prefers-color-scheme or color-scheme declaration anywhere.
findings.detail: The app chrome is LTR and Persian appears only as inline support text, so physical properties are not broken today. They would matter if a Persian UI locale were ever added. Dark mode cannot be added cheaply until colours are tokenised (356 literal hex values).
findings.recommendation: Standardise on 3–4 breakpoints (for example 480/768/1050/1280) or container queries for tiles. Prefer logical properties (border-inline-start, margin-inline-start, text-align:start) in new primitives. Treat dark mode as a follow-up once semantic tokens exist ([data-theme] or prefers-color-scheme overriding only the semantic layer).

findings.title: Inline style attributes bypass the system
findings.evidence: About 30 inline style props: LessonShell.tsx:259, 262, 284, 299, 300; SpeakingStep.tsx:276, 293, 358, 370, 402, 405, 437, 450; FeedbackPanel.tsx:65, 91; HelpLadder.tsx:64, 72; QuestionList.tsx:96; ListeningStep.tsx:103, 113; WritingStep.tsx:157, 184, 214; SpeechCheck.tsx:127, 156, 171; UsagePanel.tsx:83; ProgressOverview.tsx:44; progress/page.tsx:6; ContentReviewQueue.tsx:84-127 (including the undefined var(--border, #dce4df)).
findings.detail: Ad-hoc font sizes (0.8–1.25rem) and spacing in inline styles ignore any future type or spacing scale.

findings.title: Many e2e tests depend on class names and exact copy

areas.area: Stated principles, decisions, status and known limits (docs/*.md, README.md, apps/api/README.md, benchmarks/language/README.md, .env.example, git trajectory) — the constraints any plan must respect or consciously revise
areas.overview:
TRAJECTORY (git log -40, 18 Sep → 2 Oct 2026): it started as "release 0.1", a single A2 appointment mission (dentist base plus hairdresser transfer) built around evidence and honesty: the model proposes and code validates, typed input never counts as speaking, and feedback must cite evidence. Later commits added three more service missions, then release 0.2 (Taalstudio shell, Azure preparation, then private Azure runtime and guarded releases). After that came the 12-stage curriculum, the open library (500 cards and 100 stories per stage), topic practice (100 topics × 4 skills × 12 stages = 4,800 activities) and "learning support" (guided topic conversations, a practice coach, an admin content-review queue). On 2 Oct alone the project added the story serial "De Lindestraat", the SM-2 word bank, the daily plan with points and streak, live Azure tuning, the D-21 direct-order fix, the GitHub-deploy setup script and video lessons (Azure avatar). Breadth grew very fast. Every feature carries heavy honesty and limits text. The UX (onboarding, motivation, variety) was never the focus of a review.

DONE (STATUS.md "What works today"):
- Daily plan (/), story serial (/verhalen), video lessons (/videos), word bank (/woorden), 12-stage path (/leerpad, /learn/<stage>), topic practice, guided conversations, coach, admin queue, 4 missions (/missions), speech (push-to-talk → ffmpeg → whisper/Azure STT; Piper/Azure TTS).
- Azure deployed to RG dlp-production (West Europe) on 2 Oct. VERIFICATION lists release a6833ee as verified_live. Signed-in checks covered episodes by gpt-4.1-mini, grading, word review, nl-BE-DenaNeural synthesis plus recognition, and one typed lunch turn.
- Test counts: API 514 tests, web unit 27, Playwright 96 checks with axe scans.

KNOWN LIMITS (STATUS.md):
- All fixed Dutch and every generated episode is unreviewed.
- The static story libraries are templated and reused. D-18 says the serial is "the path forward".
- The local 8B model's Dutch and Persian are only "serviceable".
- There is no pronunciation scoring, by design.
- The phone acceptance run has not been done.
- deploy.yml has no production environment yet, so releases run from the laptop.
- The live avatar render has not been done.
- The Bicep video-seconds parameters only take effect on the next template deploy.

STATUS "Next steps, in order":
1. Do the first live video, then read the serial daily for two weeks and tune it.
2. Phone run (GO_LIVE §6).
3. Belgian Dutch reviewer, using DEMO.md.
4. Run setup_github_deploy.sh.
5. "Only then: more content, more missions."

Live checklist still open: the phone run, `verify_live.py --mode authenticated`, and the PostgreSQL point-in-time-restore drill.

IMPROVEMENT_REVIEW (22 Sep), "Next improvements, in order", and whether the code did each:
1. Real-device speaking/checkpoint run and Belgian Dutch review — NOT done. VERIFICATION: spoken turns and the checkpoint have not been run with real providers; phone acceptance is "not started"; all content is review_pending.
2. Benchmark real models on the 40 labelled cases before selecting a model — NOT recorded. benchmarks/language/README says numbers go into DECISIONS.md before a model is chosen, yet gpt-4.1-mini is live and DECISIONS has no benchmark entry.
3. Version-aware cross-tab draft conflict handling — NOT done. apps/web/lib/client/draft-saver.ts has no version, ETag or If-Match. The only `storage` listeners are in LanguageSupport.tsx:20 and LearningLibrary.tsx:25.
4. Attempt deletion with verified blob cleanup and a restore exercise — NOT done. The only DELETE route is routes_stories.py:212 (/words/{item_id}), and the restore drill is still in the STATUS checklist.
5. Confirm cloud allowance and real Azure auth, speech and storage — DONE (2 Oct live).
6. "Only then expand content or introduce another mission. Teacher workspaces and formal level assessments remain separate product work" — this ordering was overridden: 3 missions, 12 stages, 4,800 topics, the serial and videos were all added before items 1–4.

The earlier table rows (CI DB name, hint/evidence ordering, draft serialisation, session locking, learner-creation race, side-effect-free rejection, _test DB guard, deploy-input injection, home panel) are documented as fixed with tests.

AZURE SETUP (GO_LIVE, main.bicep, parameters.example.json, deploy_current.sh, VERIFICATION):
- Region and naming: West Europe; RG dlp-production; prefix dlp; ACR dlpacrhofmzccgjnr4s (Basic, no admin user); GitHub repo MahmoudAsadi97/Dutch_Learning_Platform.
- Hosting: one Container Apps environment (Consumption, VNet).
  - dlp-web: external ingress, 0.25 vCPU / 0.5 GiB, 0–1 replicas, built-in Easy Auth for Entra.
  - dlp-api: internal ingress only, 0.25 vCPU, exactly 1 replica so the PostgreSQL job loop stays warm.
  - Manual migration job dlp-migrate: 15-minute limit, no retry, separate identity.
- Database: PostgreSQL Flexible Server 16, B1ms, 32 GB, 7-day backup, no HA. It has a public endpoint disabled and is VNet-private. The runtime uses DML-only role dlp_app with TLS verify-full.
- Storage: Standard_LRS, private container learner-audio, shared-key access off, 14-day soft delete.
- Speech: S0 with local auth disabled and a custom subdomain; nl-BE STT; voice nl-BE-DenaNeural. The avatar is available in West Europe at about $1 per minute of video.
- Azure OpenAI: account kind 'OpenAI' (not a Foundry project), local auth disabled.
  - Deployment chat-small. VERIFICATION shows gpt-4.1-mini live.
  - Optional chat-strong. When it is absent, AZURE_CHAT_DEPLOYMENT_STRONG = chat-small.
  - SKU default 'Standard' (regional), capacity default 1, versionUpgradeOption NoAutoUpgrade.
  - Reached via the v1 endpoint with managed identity.
- Key Vault: RBAC, purge protection, per-secret grants to the api, web and migration managed identities.
- Monitoring: Log Analytics (30 days, 0.1 GB/day cap) and Application Insights.
- Budget: Cost Management alert at 80% and 100% (monthlyBudget default 50). This is an alert, not a cap.
- Auth: a single-tenant Entra app registration. Easy Auth `allowedPrincipals` is limited to the owner's object IDs, plus the email allowlist (OWNER_ALLOWLIST) in both the proxy and the API. CURRICULUM_ADMIN_EMAILS grants tester previews.
- Paid use: PAID_USAGE_ENABLED=true has been set live.
- Bicep usage defaults: 80 calls/day, 2,000 total; 80k tokens/day, 2M total; 1,200 audio s/day; 300 video s/day, 7,200 total. The actual production overrides are unknown.
- Deploy flow: from WSL with a signed-in `az`, `bash scripts/deploy_current.sh`. It requires a clean tree and green main CI for the exact SHA. It then runs ACR builds (RELEASE_SHA build-arg), azure_release.py deploy (migration job first, then `az containerapp update --image` for api and web, setting only MAX_AUDIO_SECONDS and CURRICULUM_ADMIN_EMAILS), and finally verify_live anonymous. The OIDC deploy.yml exists but its GitHub environment has not been created.

strengths: Every decision is recorded with its reason and cost (DECISIONS D-01..D-22), so a planner can tell which rules are principled and which are expedient.

The trust boundary is consistent and well explained: the API is never public, a 60 s HS256 assertion with CSRF header, identity headers are stripped, Easy Auth plus an email allowlist, and production refuses fixtures at startup (ENGINEERING §5, config.py:149-176).
Strict honesty vocabulary: VERIFICATION statuses separate fixture/CI evidence from live evidence; ContentLabel marks unreviewed content; synthetic audio and virtual-presenter labels.

Cost control is real: SQL-enforced reserve/commit/release counters, a PAID_USAGE_ENABLED gate in every paid path (stories, videos, coach, content review, topic conversations), and production refuses to start without it.
The existing 'agent' patterns are bounded and testable: linear 3-node LangGraph graphs (interpret → validate → compose) and complete_once with output ceilings and no automatic paid replay.

Azure infrastructure is codified (Bicep) with managed identities, a VNet-private DB, a separated migration identity, a migration-first release, readiness tied to the migration head, and a live commit visible at /health.
A deterministic story validator plus a rewrite loop is a reusable 'models propose, code validates' gate for generated content (D-18, STORY_ENGINE).
Accessibility is taken seriously: axe WCAG A/AA scans run in the Playwright suites at 1440/768/390/320 px.

findings.title: The daily plan promises a conversation, but practice never appears in it or earns points
findings.evidence: README.md:3-5 ('one conversation to practise'); TodayHome.tsx:60 ('Eén aflevering, een paar woorden, één gesprek'); routes_stories.py:66-76 (next_step ∈ read/choose/review/wait/explore); add_points is called only in stories/service.py:396-520, videos/service.py:493-516 and stories/vocab.py:123; POINTS in stories/service.py:46 and videos/service.py:55
findings.detail: The streak, points and daily-goal loop (D-19) only rewards stories, videos, read-aloud and word reviews. Topic practice, curriculum lessons, missions and guided conversations (the 'practice' the owner found boring) give no points, have no place on Today and have no next_step. The coach (PracticeCoach) sits on /leerpad (CurriculumPath.tsx:32), not on the home page as LEARNING_AGENTS.md says. A first-time user sees a waiting screen ('De schrijver is bezig…', 1–3 min locally) and a set of links, with no explanation of how the parts fit together.
findings.recommendation: Plan a unified daily plan that includes one practice/conversation step and awards points for completed practice actions. D-19 allows this as long as points reward doing and never judge the learner's Dutch. Update README, LEARNING_AGENTS ('Home: Jouw volgende oefening') and STATUS after the change.

findings.title: Honesty rules limit what gamification can show
findings.evidence: README.md:44-46 'No pronunciation scores, no aggregate level, no certificate'; D-17 'No fictitious scores, certificates or reviewed-content claims'; D-19 'Points reward doing and are never a judgement'; D-20 'No accent or pronunciation score is computed or shown, because a transcript cannot carry one'; ENGINEERING 'Learning-path boundary' 'There is no aggregate score'; CURRICULUM 'no aggregate score that can conceal an unpassed skill'; DEMO 'never a level'
findings.detail: XP, streaks, badges for actions, goals and progress rings are compatible with these rules. An overall level, a 'fluency %', CEFR badges, pronunciation stars or an accuracy-based leaderboard are not. D-20's reason is tied to the transcript-only design. Adding Azure Speech pronunciation assessment would need a new decision that revises D-20 and the README honesty rules; whether nl-BE is supported was not verified.
findings.recommendation: Design gamification around effort and completion (actions, streaks, per-skill 'practised' counts, words reviewed). If a pronunciation or level signal is wanted, record a new D-number decision that consciously revises D-20 and README §Honesty, and keep the four skill records separate.

findings.title: A tool-using AI agent goes against the explicit LEARNING_AGENTS boundaries and infra assumptions
findings.evidence: LEARNING_AGENTS.md:47-48 'It has no open tool loop, arbitrary database tool, web access or ability to write lesson files'; :41-45 roles table (the model may only interpret, reorder exactly three activities, or suggest issues); :96-97 'No new queue service or agent hosting resource is needed'; D-12 rejects a single call that both decides and replies; practice/workflow.py:123-131 and topic_conversations/workflow.py:118-126 are linear graphs; the chat client uses JSON mode via chat/completions (chat_openai_compatible.py:180-184), with no tools parameter; GO_LIVE §2.4 says reasoning-only deployments are not interchangeable; main.bicep:237-243 kind 'OpenAI' (not a Foundry project); pyproject has no openai or agent SDK
findings.detail: Today's 'agents' are bounded single-call interpreters with code as the authority. A real tutor agent with tools (look up the learner's history, choose or generate exercises, schedule reviews) is possible only if the tools are code-validated, read-mostly and learner-scoped. It needs a recorded decision revising LEARNING_AGENTS 'Responsibilities and limits'. It also needs: tool-calling support in providers/base.py and chat_openai_compatible.py; usage reservations per step (an agent loop can take many calls against an 80/day Bicep default); a stated ceiling on loop length or recursion; and possibly a new Azure resource (Foundry project or Agent Service), which breaks the repeated 'no new Azure service' pattern (LEARNING_AGENTS, TOPIC_PRACTICE, PRACTICE_LIBRARY, GO_LIVE §1 'There is no … Service Bus …').
findings.recommendation: If agents go ahead: keep 'models propose, code validates' (tools return validated data; the agent cannot award passes, mark content reviewed or write content files), add a D-23 decision, extend usage accounting to multi-step loops, update LEARNING_AGENTS, ENGINEERING §4 and §7, GO_LIVE §1/§2.4, and main.bicep (raise usage defaults and capacity, possibly a Foundry resource).

findings.title: No onboarding, and the interface chrome is Dutch-only (docs make Dutch UI a stated choice)

The interface is in Dutch.'; LEARNING_DESIGN 'Dutch remains the practice language'; LanguageSupport.tsx:5-9 (modes nl-en / nl-fa / nl-fa-en only; Dutch always shown); AppShell.tsx:16-42 Dutch-only nav labels; app/layout.tsx:41 lang='nl'; no onboarding or placement found (grep 'onboard|welkom' in apps/web); identity/models.py:13-27 Learner has no goals or level fields; stories/service.py:55-58 default_stage falls back to a1; AccountSettings shows only name, email and support language

constraints: Models propose, code validates: dates, availability, bookings, task completion, usage limits, submissions, passes and points are decided in application code; the model never decides (README 'Architecture'; ENGINEERING §1; D-12; ARCHITECTURE_WALKTHROUGH §2 'Where the truth lives').

Conversation turn shape: LangGraph propose_action (model) → validate_action (code, apply_action) → compose_reply (model, anchored on the fixed line). A reply that contradicts the code is replaced by the fixed line. If the first call fails, the turn fails with a 502 (no simulated conversation). Failed turns do not count against the turn limit. 2 model calls and 1,800 tokens are reserved per turn. Prompt versions are stored. Reason: the code must stay the authority over the appointment (D-12; ENGINEERING §6.1).

Service missions: character replies use authored phase lines and validated choices (no invented prices or remedies); one interpretation call per turn; a valid option named straight away counts as stating the need, unless the scenario sets reason_before_choice; the 'not on offer' line is only for options that are not on offer (D-21; FOUR_SKILL_CONTENT 'Implementation and boundaries').

Learning agents (LEARNING_AGENTS 'Responsibilities and limits'): the conversation partner only interprets and quotes; the coach only reorders exactly three allowed activities; the content-review assistant only suggests issues. The application decides ownership, turn order, facts, assistance, replies, completion, candidates and review status. 'No open tool loop, arbitrary database tool, web access or ability to write lesson files.' Reason: language understanding is fallible; code anchors give a conservative check.

Single-call rules: complete_once means one attempt, no repair, no retry (topic conversation 400 output tokens; coach 600; editorial batch 1,600; 1–5 topics). Story episode at most two model calls. Feedback is one call. Browsing, starting a conversation, hint/repeat and the default coach plan make no model call. No automatic paid replay after uncertain failures (LEARNING_AGENTS 'Cost and recovery'; STORY_ENGINE 'Cost and limits'; D-14).

Paid use is switched on deliberately with PAID_USAGE_ENABLED, never because credentials are present. Production refuses to start without it (config.py:162). Story, video, coach, content-review and topic-conversation generation refuse Azure calls without it (D-17; README 'Going live'; STORY_ENGINE).

Usage counters reserve before every external call and are enforced inside the SQL UPDATE. Counters are application estimates, not an invoice. A budget alert is not a hard currency cap. Video seconds are a counter ($1 per minute avatar) and a failed render returns them. At most two videos in progress per learner (D-07; D-17; D-22; ENGINEERING §7; GO_LIVE §2; VIDEO_LESSONS 'Cost and limits').

No pronunciation or accent score anywhere, 'because a transcript cannot carry one'. Read-aloud only reports recognised words; points are given once per paragraph at ≥50% recognised (D-20; README 'Honesty rules'; CURRICULUM 'Language and assessment review'; LEARNING_DESIGN 'Support and independent evidence').

No aggregate level or score, no certificate, no CEFR mastery claim, no fictitious scores. Skill records show practised/checkpoint_passed with their evidence, never a level. Stage names are 'not an independently validated CEFR award' (README; D-17; DEMO 'What not to claim'; CURRICULUM; ENGINEERING 'Learning-path boundary'; LEARNING_AGENTS 'No helper awards a final-check pass, locks a stage or declares CEFR mastery').
Points reward doing and are never a judgement of the learner's Dutch. Daily goal 20 points per Europe/Brussels day. The streak counts consecutive active days (D-19).

Four separate skill records, never merged. Typed input never counts as speaking practice. Feedback may only contain points that cite resolvable evidence; the rest is dropped and counted. Feedback is on a step, never an assessment of the skill (D-14; D-16; ENGINEERING §6).

Labelling: every fixed Dutch text is a LocalizedText with review_status, and the UI labels anything not 'reviewed'. Everything the model writes is labelled as generated. Synthetic voices are labelled. The video presenter is labelled virtual ('geen echte persoon'). Never mark content reviewed because tests pass (README; ENGINEERING §3; VIDEO_LESSONS 'Honesty'; FOUR_SKILL_CONTENT; TOPIC_PRACTICE).

Learner-facing screens must not show model/provider IDs, prompt versions, evidence UUIDs, model latency or session UUIDs; diagnostics stay in Settings › Technische ondersteuning and the export (FOUR_SKILL_CONTENT; CURRICULUM; LEARNING_AGENTS 'What the learner sees').

Assessment integrity: reading and listening are graded on the server. Final-check answer keys, listening scripts and sample responses are withheld before submission. Submitted final work is immutable during a retry. A model or provider failure never awards a pass. Admin previews never become student passes. A self-report never unlocks a stage. Reading/listening 75% thresholds are internal course rules (CURRICULUM; ENGINEERING 'Learning-path boundary'; LEARNING_DESIGN 'Design choices').

Session semantics: one active session per learner, mission and variant. A checkpoint with retry:false allows exactly one session. A retried request ID replays the stored turn. Failed turns are kept (D-13).

Trust boundary: the web app is the only public entry; the API is never public (internal ingress). Every proxied request carries a 60-second HS256 assertion (issuer dlp-web, audience dlp-api, jti). The X-Requested-With: fetch header plus Sec-Fetch-Site/Origin checks are enforced in both tiers. Browser-sent Authorization, Cookie and X-MS-CLIENT-PRINCIPAL* headers are dropped (D-03; D-04; ENGINEERING §5; README architecture table).

Identity: fixture identity only in development or test, bound to localhost. Production refuses DEV_AUTH_ENABLED, fixture providers, the fixture video renderer and the memory blob store. Production requires Azure chat, speech and blob, a real allowlist, and TLS to PostgreSQL (D-05; config.py:145-178).

Privacy: Application Insights exports route template, status and duration only. There are no request bodies, identities, prompts or recordings in telemetry, and Uvicorn access logs are disabled in the cloud. The content-review model sees only authored content, never learner answers, recordings or history. No real recording is committed. Scans and OCR stay in .local/ and outside Git. Agree retention and deletion before inviting anyone else (ENGINEERING 'Release 0.2 conventions'; GO_LIVE §6, §8; LEARNING_AGENTS 'Admin editing workflow'; D-09; SOURCE_COVERAGE).

Belgian Dutch norms: Belgian Standard Dutch is the target (nl-BE locale; nl-BE-DenaNeural or Piper nl_BE-nathalie). Regional gij/ge only when labelled in the glossary. Do not label a shared standard form wrong just because it is also used in the Netherlands. Dutch remains the practice language; English and Persian are support languages, and Persian is rendered RTL (D-18; STORY_ENGINE; SOURCE_COVERAGE step 3; LEARNING_DESIGN; README).
Interface language: 'The interface is in Dutch' (README 'What it does'). Support translations follow the header choice; changing support mode preserves current work (LEARNING_DESIGN).

Content provenance: OCR output is never promoted into lessons. Source scans, illustrations and text are not redistributed. All published content is original. Dated facts from the sources must not be copied as current guidance (SOURCE_COVERAGE; CURRICULUM 'Relationship to the supplied scans').

The story serial is the chosen way forward over more templated content. The model proposes and validator.py decides. A failed draft is rewritten once, and a second failure is shown as a failure. The next episode waits for the learner's choice or 12 hours. At most two unread episodes are written ahead (D-18; STORY_ENGINE).
The word bank is the learner's own choice: nothing enters it unless they save it. SM-2 scheduling; a lapse returns after 10 minutes (D-19).

Generative video models were rejected: they are English-first, produce seconds-long clips without Dutch narration, cost $0.10–0.50 per second and are not available in the region used. The Azure avatar is used instead, and video scripts go through the story validator plus a 20-second minimum (D-22).

Test-database safety: API and E2E test databases must end in _test; destructive setup refuses anything else. Tests use the real PostgreSQL and fixture providers (IMPROVEMENT_REVIEW findings table; README 'Checks'; ENGINEERING §3).

Evidence vocabulary: verified_local, verified_ci, verified_live, integration_pending, review_pending. Never infer real provider validation from a fixture, a dry run, a configured endpoint or a compiled template (VERIFICATION; ENGINEERING 'Release 0.2 conventions'; D-10).

Release discipline: migration-first. Both images are always built. dlp.release migrate is the only schema path. The runtime uses a DML-only role. Migrations must be additive and backward-compatible; no blind Alembic downgrade. Release only after green main CI for the exact commit. Never set publicWeb=true at bootstrap, and keep publicWeb=true with real image refs on later template deploys (GO_LIVE §4–§8; D-17).

Model deployment rules: the client needs Chat Completions with JSON mode, temperature and max_tokens. Reasoning-only deployments are not interchangeable. Do not silently use a Global deployment if regional processing matters. Pin model and version with NoAutoUpgrade. A strong model needs both name and version (GO_LIVE §2.4; main.bicep:32-40, 244-256).

Owner's ordered roadmap: phone run, live video, Belgian Dutch reviewer, GitHub deploy setup — 'Only then: more content, more missions' (STATUS 'Next steps'). IMPROVEMENT_REVIEW item 6 says the same, and 'Teacher workspaces and formal level assessments remain separate product work'.

Design choices: one visible next step, separate four-skill progress, support tools inside the relevant practice section rather than more main navigation, a single native audio player (no overlapping playback), recording and submission guard navigation, restrained navy/blue palette with high contrast, WCAG 2.2 as the target with automated axe checks as a supplement only (LEARNING_DESIGN 'Design choices'; ENGINEERING; D-17).

Web security and CSP: nonce-based scripts; style, font, img, media and connect sources are 'self' only (plus data: and blob: for images and media); fonts are self-hosted (@fontsource). No CDN or remote assets (ENGINEERING 'Release 0.2 conventions'; apps/web/proxy.ts:10-15).

Code conventions: Python 3.11, type hints, Pydantic extra='forbid' for content, ruff line length 130. TypeScript strict, ESLint Next rules, no state-setting inside effect bodies. Every request has an X-Request-Id (^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{8,64}$) used for idempotency. All DB connections are pinned to UTC. scripts/run.py is the cross-platform task runner (ENGINEERING §3; D-11; D-14).

Effectiveness claims: completion and app usage alone do not show learning. Evaluate transfer, delayed recall, help used, correction accuracy and learner experience before claiming effectiveness (LEARNING_DESIGN 'Sources and validation boundaries').

Which commit is live. VERIFICATION records release a6833ee, but later 2 Oct commits (D-21 fix, Azure adapter reporting, video lessons 795697b) may or may not have been deployed; STATUS says the live avatar render has not been done.
The owner's monthly budget amount and remaining Azure credits or allowance. The docs only say monthlyBudget defaults to 50 as an alert amount.
Whether the owner wants to keep the 'interface is in Dutch' rule or wants English or Persian UI chrome during onboarding.
Whether the owner accepts revising D-20, for example Azure Speech pronunciation assessment. Its nl-BE locale support was not verified here.
