areas.area: External research: the current (October 2026) way to build production AI agents on Azure for a language-learning tutor, checked against the repo's existing Azure chat and speech providers
areas.overview:
REPO GROUNDING. The API reaches models through one hand-written httpx client, `OpenAICompatibleChatModel` (apps/api/src/dlp/providers/chat_openai_compatible.py). Ollama and Azure use the same client. For Azure it posts to `{endpoint}/openai/v1/chat/completions` when `api_version == "v1"` (lines 42-48), which is the Bicep default (infra/main.bicep:344). Every request sends `temperature` and `max_tokens`. When a schema is given, the client puts the Pydantic JSON schema into a system message and sets `response_format={"type":"json_object"}` (JSON mode, not strict structured outputs) (lines 174-184). It then validates on the client and runs a bounded "repair" retry loop (lines 194-215). `complete_once` (lines 142-161) sends at most one request for the newer flows. Authentication uses managed identity with the `https://ai.azure.com/.default` scope (.env.example:55, registry.py:41-54). Two tiers exist, `chat` and `chat_strong` (registry.py:57-77). Speech uses the REST short-audio endpoints with `nl-BE` STT and the `nl-BE-DenaNeural` voice, with no Speech SDK and no pronunciation header (speech_azure.py:58-93, 117-168). The "agents" are deliberately not autonomous. `topic_conversations/workflow.py` is a 3-node linear LangGraph (interpret → validate → compose, lines 89-126). The model only interprets; code validates quoted evidence and picks authored replies (docs/LEARNING_AGENTS.md:47-52, DECISIONS.md D-12). The infrastructure is Bicep with these pieces: West Europe, a `Microsoft.CognitiveServices/accounts` kind OpenAI, deployments `chat-small`/`chat-strong` with `chatDeploymentSku` defaulting to `'Standard'` (regional) and `versionUpgradeOption: 'NoAutoUpgrade'` (main.bicep:35-36, 244-256), Speech S0, a single-replica 0.25 vCPU API with internal ingress, App Insights, and a budget alert. Per-learner caps are enforced in SQL with reserve/commit/release (domains/usage/service.py). Telemetry is privacy-first: azure-monitor-opentelemetry with httpx and FastAPI auto-instrumentation disabled and 10% sampling (observability.py:12-28).

WHAT THE PRIMARY SOURCES SAY (Oct 2026). (1) Microsoft Agent Framework reached 1.0 GA on 3 Apr 2026 for Python (`pip install agent-framework`, provider package `agent-framework-openai`) and .NET. It is the direct successor to Semantic Kernel and AutoGen. Its concepts are agents, sessions, context providers/memory, middleware, tools/MCP, and graph workflows with checkpointing and human-in-the-loop. It emits OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic-convention spans (`invoke_agent`, `chat`, `execute_tool`); prompt and response capture is off by default (`ENABLE_SENSITIVE_DATA=false`). Its own guidance says: "If you can write a function to handle the task, do that instead of using an AI agent." Its Python `OpenAIChatClient` targets the Responses API and is the recommended client. (2) Foundry Agent Service is GA in West Europe and Sweden Central. Prompt agents carry no extra charge (you pay for tokens and tools). Hosted agents went GA on 9 Jul 2026, run per-session VM sandboxes, and are billed per vCPU-hour and GiB-hour. Agent state lives either in Microsoft-managed storage (Basic setup) or in your own Cosmos DB, AI Search and Storage (Standard setup). The structured-outputs doc states that structured outputs are NOT supported with Foundry Agents Service. (3) The Responses API is GA under `/openai/v1/responses` in westeurope and swedencentral, and Microsoft recommends it for new apps. Chat Completions is not deprecated. Both support strict `json_schema` structured outputs, with these limits: all fields required, `additionalProperties:false`, no min/max/pattern keywords, at most 100 properties and 5 nesting levels. (4) Model reality for this repo: in westeurope, regional "Standard" offers only gpt-4.1-mini among chat models. gpt-4.1-mini and gpt-4o-mini are already "Deprecated" (closed to new customers) and retire on 2027-04-14; gpt-4.1-nano retires on 2026-10-14. Newer models (gpt-5.4-mini/nano, gpt-5.5, gpt-5.6-luna/terra/sol, gpt-6-luna/sol) are available in westeurope only as Data Zone Standard (EU) or Global Standard. GPT-5.x reasoning models reject `temperature` and `max_tokens`, so the current client is incompatible with them. GPT-6 Luna is priced at $0.10/$0.50 per 1M tokens Global and $0.12/$0.60 EU Data Zone; GPT-5.6 Luna at $0.20/$1.20 Global. (5) Real-time voice: GPT Realtime 2.1 and 2.1-mini are GA over WebRTC, WebSocket and SIP, but in Europe they are deployable only in swedencentral and francecentral, not westeurope. Their voices are OpenAI voices, not Belgian ones, and Dutch is "supported" only in the sense that it passed a WER below 50% bar. Voice Live, a managed STT + LLM + TTS pipeline, runs in westeurope with text models over the EU data zone plus Azure Speech voices, so nl-BE-DenaNeural/ArnaudNeural work there. Its automatic multilingual mode excludes Dutch, so the language must be set explicitly. It is billed per token in Pro, Standard and Lite tiers (about 10 input and 20 output audio tokens per second), and its content filtering cannot be disabled. Pronunciation assessment supports nl-NL but NOT nl-BE. It works on the REST short-audio endpoint via the `Pronunciation-Assessment` header with at most 30 s of audio, prosody is en-US only, and it costs the same as standard STT. (6) Evaluation and observability: Foundry evaluations, monitoring and tracing are GA (March 2026, per a techcommunity post whose body could not be fetched). Cloud evaluation can score your own datasets or traces. Default guardrails filter at Medium severity in four harm categories and turn on jailbreak Prompt Shields, but the classifiers are trained on EN, DE, JA, ES, FR, IT, PT and ZH, not Dutch. Prompt caching is automatic for prefixes of at least 1,024 identical tokens; GPT-5.6 and later also charge for cache writes and accept `prompt_cache_key`. API Management's `llm-token-limit` and semantic-cache policies exist, but this app's SQL counters already cover per-user caps. (7) Language-tutor patterns: Duolingo's Roleplay, Video Call and Explain My Answer use curriculum-expert-written scenarios and several narrow prompts per turn (ask, state, change subject, close) inside a flow chart with a beginning, middle and end. They give post-conversation feedback on accuracy and complexity, use adaptive length (about 1 to 3 minutes), apply no penalties, and keep humans reviewing AI content. Duolingo says plain "chat with a chatbot" practice lacks level calibration and structure.

NET IMPLICATION. The repo's "model interprets, code decides" design already matches current best practice. The upgrades that actually move the product forward are not a new agent platform. They are: (a) migrate the client to the v1 Responses API with strict json_schema and a currently supported EU Data Zone model (Luna-class for interpretation and grading, a Sol or Terra-class model for writing); (b) add tutor behaviours as bounded, code-orchestrated steps (explain-my-mistake, post-conversation feedback, adaptive next activity), optionally with Agent Framework in-process inside FastAPI; (c) optionally add a Voice Live "live conversation" mode in westeurope with nl-BE Azure voices; (d) optionally add nl-NL scripted pronunciation assessment for read-aloud, with an explicit caveat that it uses Netherlands Dutch. Foundry hosted agents add a second state store, cost and network complexity, and give nothing a single-owner app needs.

key_files.role: The only LLM client (Ollama and Azure). Calls Chat Completions on /openai/v1, uses JSON mode plus a prompt-injected schema and a client-side repair loop, and sends temperature and max_tokens (lines 42-48, 174-215).
Vendor-neutral interfaces ChatModel (complete/complete_once), SpeechToText, TextToSpeech, BlobStore, VideoRenderer, plus ChatResult with token usage.
Chooses local, Azure or fixture providers; builds the small and strong chat tiers; managed-identity token provider with scope from settings (lines 41-77).
Azure Speech REST short-audio STT (nl-BE, detailed format) and TTS (nl-BE-DenaNeural); Entra tokens in aad#resourceId#token form. No pronunciation-assessment header today.
3-node linear LangGraph interpret→validate→compose. One complete_once call with temperature 0 and a 400-token cap; code validates the quoted evidence and picks authored replies.
Azure Monitor OTel setup with httpx/FastAPI auto-instrumentation disabled and 10% sampling; never exports prompts.
Dependencies: langgraph>=1.0, httpx; the azure extra pins azure-identity and azure-monitor-opentelemetry>=1.8.10. No openai SDK and no agent-framework.
Azure resources: OpenAI account with chat-small/chat-strong deployments (sku default 'Standard', NoAutoUpgrade), Speech S0, single-replica internal API, App Insights, budget alert.
location westeurope; chatModelName and chatModelVersion are placeholders; chatDeploymentSku is Standard.
Config contract: AZURE_CHAT_API_VERSION=v1, AZURE_CHAT_TOKEN_SCOPE=https://ai.azure.com/.default, MAX_AUDIO_SECONDS=60, usage caps.
Defines the three bounded roles (conversation partner, practice coach, content reviewer); no open tool loop, DB tool or web access; no new Azure agent-hosting resource.
D-12 (model interprets, code decides), D-16 (typed input never counts as speaking), D-17 (explicit paid use), D-20 (no pronunciation score).
Release guide; lines 49-53 state the client needs Chat Completions, JSON mode, temperature and max_tokens, and warns against silently choosing a Global deployment.
Atomic SQL reserve/commit/release of per-learner daily and total allowances (model calls, tokens, audio seconds, video seconds).
Settings for the Azure chat endpoint, deployments, usage limits and the paid_usage_enabled gate (lines 42-80, 125-131, 162-166).

strengths: The 'model interprets, code decides' pattern (DECISIONS.md D-12; topic_conversations/workflow.py validate_meaning) is exactly what current guidance recommends over open agent loops. Microsoft's Agent Framework overview says: 'If you can write a function to handle the task, do that instead of using an AI agent.' Duolingo Roleplay also uses expert-authored scenarios with several narrow prompts per turn.

It already uses the GA v1 surface (/openai/v1/chat/completions, no dated api-version) and the documented Entra scope https://ai.azure.com/.default with managed identity (chat_openai_compatible.py:44-46; .env.example:54-55; main.bicep:344). That makes a move to /openai/v1/responses small.

The narrow provider interface (providers/base.py ChatModel/SpeechToText/TextToSpeech) and the single registry (registry.py) mean a Responses-API or Voice Live adapter can be added without touching domain code.

Per-learner cost caps already exist as atomic SQL reserve/commit/release (usage/service.py:1-4, 104-172), with complete_once preventing hidden retries. An API Management AI gateway is unnecessary for a single owner.

Telemetry is already privacy-safe (observability.py docstring and lines 20-28) and pins azure-monitor-opentelemetry>=1.8.10 (pyproject.toml:35), the version Microsoft's Agent Framework docs require for HTTPX/OpenAI span correlation.

Speech already uses nl-BE STT and nl-BE-DenaNeural TTS through REST with Entra tokens (speech_azure.py). The REST short-audio endpoint is also where pronunciation assessment would plug in, through a single header.
The Bicep deployment SKU parameter already allows 'DataZoneStandard' (main.bicep:35), so moving to EU Data Zone models is a parameter change, not a redesign.

findings.title: The deployable model set has moved: in West Europe 'Standard' offers only deprecated gpt-4.1-mini, and NoAutoUpgrade means a hard stop at retirement
findings.evidence: Repo: infra/main.bicep:35-36 (chatDeploymentSku default 'Standard'), :248 and :254 (versionUpgradeOption 'NoAutoUpgrade'); infra/parameters.example.json:6 (westeurope). https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/models-sold-directly-by-azure-region-availability (ms.date 2026-09-03): the westeurope Standard/Regional table lists only gpt-4.1-mini (2025-04-14) among chat models; westeurope Data Zone Standard and Global Standard list gpt-5.4, gpt-5.4-mini, gpt-5.5, gpt-5.6-luna/sol/terra, gpt-6-luna/sol, gpt-6.1-sol. https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/openai/concepts/model-retirement-schedule (2026-09-21): gpt-4.1-mini and gpt-4o-mini are 'Deprecated', retiring 2027-04-14; gpt-4.1-nano retires 2026-10-14; gpt-5.4-mini retires 2027-09-21; gpt-5.6-luna 2028-01-11. https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/openai/concepts/model-retirements: 'Deprecated' means new customers and new subscriptions cannot deploy; NoAutoUpgrade means the deployment stops working at retirement.
findings.detail: Any fresh deployment, such as a new subscription or a rebuilt environment, may be unable to create gpt-4.1-mini at all. An existing deployment will return 410 after 2027-04-14. Current-generation models in West Europe require DataZoneStandard (EU processing, which honours GO_LIVE.md:50-51 'Do not silently select a Global deployment if regional processing matters') or GlobalStandard. GPT-6 announcement (https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/blog/gpt-6-astra-sol-and-luna-for-production-agents-in-microsoft-foundry/, 22 Sep 2026), short-context prices per 1M tokens: Luna $0.10 in / $0.50 out Global, $0.12 / $0.60 EU Data Zone; Sol $2.00 / $10.00 Global, $2.40 / $12.00 EU. The post describes Luna as built 'for high-volume work … extraction, summarization, request routing'. GPT-5.6 (https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/blog/gpt-5-6-now-available-in-microsoft-foundry/, 9 Jul 2026): Luna $0.20/$1.20, Terra $2/$12, Sol $5/$30 Global (Sol temporarily $4/$20 from 1 Sep to 30 Nov 2026).
findings.recommendation: Plan to switch chatDeploymentSku to 'DataZoneStandard' and pick a Luna-class model (gpt-6-luna or gpt-5.6-luna) for chat-small, which handles interpretation, grading and translation. Pick a Sol or Terra-class model for chat-strong (stories, video scripts, content review, writing feedback). Prefer a versionUpgradeOption that will not silently break at retirement, or add a Models-API lifecycle check to preflight. Expect roughly a 20% EU Data Zone premium over Global for GPT-6 pricing.

findings.title: The current chat client is incompatible with current reasoning models (temperature, max_tokens) and uses JSON mode rather than strict structured outputs
findings.evidence: Repo: chat_openai_compatible.py:177-184 sends 'temperature', 'max_tokens' and response_format {type: json_object}; :174-176 injects the schema as a system prompt; :194-215 retries truncation and repairs invalid JSON. docs/GO_LIVE.md:49-51 already notes the dependency on JSON mode, temperature and max_tokens. https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/openai/how-to/reasoning (ms.date 2026-09-21): 'Reasoning models other than GPT-6 Astra don't support … temperature, top_p … max_tokens'; Chat Completions requires max_completion_tokens and Responses uses max_output_tokens; gpt-5.6 + tools on Chat Completions only works with reasoning_effort 'none'; gpt-5.1+ and 5.6 support reasoning_effort 'none' for latency-critical work. The same page's GPT-6 table shows temperature as supported for gpt-6-sol/luna (contradiction, see open questions). https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/openai/how-to/structured-outputs (2026-08-24): both Chat Completions (response_format json_schema) and Responses (text.format) support strict structured outputs, unlike JSON mode, with limits: every field required, additionalProperties false, no minLength/maxLength/pattern/minimum/maximum/minItems/maxItems, at most 100 properties and 5 nesting levels.
findings.detail: Moving chat-small to any GPT-5.x model, without code changes, would produce HTTP 400s for temperature and max_tokens. Strict json_schema would remove most of the repair loop (fewer billed retries, simpler accounting in complete_once). Pydantic constraints such as max lengths must still be checked in code, because strict mode cannot express them.
findings.recommendation: Write a new provider (or extend OpenAICompatibleChatModel) for the Azure path. It should call /openai/v1/responses with text.format json_schema strict, use max_output_tokens, omit temperature unless the model supports it, set reasoning_effort 'none' or 'low' for interpretation calls, and read usage from usage.input_tokens/output_tokens (including cached_tokens). Keep the Ollama path on Chat Completions with JSON mode. Generate strict schemas from the existing Pydantic models (TopicInterpretation, PlanRanking, ProductiveReply, Translation) and keep server-side validate_meaning and length checks.

findings.title: Responses API is the recommended surface for new Azure work; Chat Completions remains supported
findings.evidence: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/openai/how-to/responses (last updated 18 Aug 2026): GA; endpoint https://<resource>.openai.azure.com/openai/v1/responses; available in westeurope and swedencentral; built-in tools code interpreter, web search, file search, function calling, MCP, image generation; stateful via previous_response_id or the Conversations API, with 30-day default retention (store=false for stateless); streaming event response.output_text.delta; server-side compaction. https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/openai/api-version-lifecycle: 'For Azure OpenAI models we recommend using the Responses API'. https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/developer/ai/how-to/azure-openai-to-responses (2026-06-01): mapping messages→input, max_tokens→max_output_tokens, response_format→text.format, choices[0].message.content→output_text; there is a migration skill at github.com/Azure-Samples/azure-openai-to-responses.
findings.detail: The app owns conversation state in PostgreSQL (append-only attempts and evidence), so server-side Responses state (store / previous_response_id) adds a second copy of learner text kept for 30 days by default. Stateless use (store=false, history passed in input) keeps PostgreSQL authoritative and matches the privacy stance in observability.py.
findings.recommendation: Use Responses in stateless mode (store=false), with input built from the existing messages_for() helpers. Do not adopt the Conversations API or hosted tools such as web search; they conflict with LEARNING_AGENTS.md:47-49 (no web access, no open tool loop).

findings.title: Keep the agent loop inside FastAPI; Foundry Agent Service and hosted agents are not worth it for this app
findings.evidence: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/limits-quotas-regions (ms.date 2026-09-07): Agent Service is GA; Agents and Responses API are available in West Europe and Sweden Central; Basic setup stores threads and files in Microsoft-managed storage, Standard setup requires your own Cosmos DB, AI Search and Storage. https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/pricing/details/foundry-agent-service/: 'No additional charge' for prompt agents and workflows; hosted agents are billed per vCPU-hour and GiB-hour (rates rendered as '$-' on fetch). https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/hosted-agents (updated 2026-09-29): per-session VM-isolated sandboxes, 0.5 vCPU/1 GiB minimum, idle timeout 2-60 min, own agent identity and endpoint, OTel to App Insights; supports Agent Framework, LangGraph or custom code. https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/openai/how-to/structured-outputs: 'structured outputs aren't supported with … Foundry Agents Service'. https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/agent-framework/overview/ (2026-07-29): 'If you can write a function to handle the task, do that instead of using an AI agent.'
findings.detail: The repo's invariants (evidence-backed grading, append-only attempts, usage reservations before calls, one active session, typed never counts as speech) all live in PostgreSQL transactions next to the model call (D-12, D-13, D-16; usage/service.py). Moving the loop into Foundry would split state, lose strict structured outputs on the agent path, add hosted compute cost on top of the warm 0.25 vCPU API, and require new identity and VNet wiring. The current graphs are linear and deterministic; Agent Framework workflows or Foundry would add nothing at runtime.
findings.recommendation: Run any new tutor behaviour in-process in the existing API container. If an orchestration library is wanted, Microsoft Agent Framework 1.0 Python (agent_framework.Agent with agent_framework.openai.OpenAIChatClient against Azure, middleware for allowance checks, sensitive data off) is the current Microsoft-supported choice. Keep LangGraph, or replace the 3-node graphs with plain functions, rather than migrating them for its own sake. Treat Foundry as optional only for evaluations and tracing dashboards.

findings.title: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.0 is the GA successor to Semantic Kernel/AutoGen; adopt it only for open-ended tutor turns, with sensitive-data telemetry off
findings.evidence: https://devblogs.microsoft.com/agent-framework/microsoft-agent-framework-version-1-0/ (3 Apr 2026): 1.0 GA for Python (`agent-framework`) and .NET (`Microsoft.Agents.AI`); graph workflows (sequential, concurrent, handoff, group chat, Magentic) with checkpointing and hydration; pluggable memory; middleware for safety, logging and policy; human-in-the-loop; DevUI, AG-UI adapters and Foundry Tools integration still preview. https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/agent-framework/agents/providers/openai (2026-10-02): Python `OpenAIChatClient` = Responses (recommended); `OpenAIChatCompletionClient` = Chat Completions; Azure routing via azure_endpoint + credential, or base_url .../openai/v1; package agent-framework-openai; Assistants client removed. https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/agent-framework/agents/observability (2026-09-19): OTel GenAI semconv spans invoke_agent/chat/execute_tool; metrics gen_ai.client.token.usage; ENABLE_SENSITIVE_DATA default false; use configure_azure_monitor() then enable_instrumentation(enable_sensitive_data=False).
findings.detail: Agent Framework's value here is limited to a future free-form conversation partner or explain-my-mistake tutor that needs tool calls into vetted app functions such as lookup_vocab, get_learner_errors or schedule_review. The deterministic coach and conversation graphs do not need it. Its OTel output plugs into the existing App Insights resource.
findings.recommendation: If adding an open-ended tutor, implement it as an Agent Framework Agent with function tools that wrap existing read-only domain services. Put a middleware in front that reserves usage via usage.reserve before each model call, caps turns, and keeps sensitive-data capture off in production. Do not adopt hosted MCP or web tools.

findings.title: Real-time speech-to-speech: Voice Live in West Europe can use nl-BE voices; native gpt-realtime cannot run in West Europe and has no Belgian voice
findings.evidence: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/openai/concepts/realtime-2 (ms.date 2026-09-21): gpt-realtime-2.1 and 2.1-mini (2026-07-07) GA; WebSocket wss://<resource>.openai.azure.com/openai/v1/realtime, WebRTC, SIP; Global Standard and Data Zone Standard; PCM16 24 kHz; voices alloy, ash, ballad, coral, cedar, echo, marin, sage, shimmer, verse. Region table (models-sold-directly-by-azure-region-availability): Europe Global Standard realtime models only in francecentral and swedencentral. https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/speech-service/regions?tabs=voice-live (2026-09-30): westeurope Voice Live supports gpt-4.1-mini, gpt-5.6-luna, gpt-5-mini etc. (Data zone standard) with agent support, no realtime models; swedencentral adds gpt-realtime-2.1-datazone. https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/speech-service/voice-live-language-support (2026-09-24): Dutch is not in the multilingual auto-detect list, so language must be set; gpt-realtime lists Dutch among languages with WER < 50%; MAI-Transcribe-2 supports 'nl' (preview); Azure TTS voices usable. https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/speech-service/voice-live (2026-09-29): tiers Pro (gpt-realtime*, gpt-5.6-terra, gpt-4.1…), Standard (gpt-realtime-2.1-mini, gpt-5.6-luna, gpt-4.1-mini, gpt-5-mini), Lite (gpt-4.1-nano, gpt-5-nano); about 10 input / 20 output audio tokens per second; WebSocket server-to-server; noise suppression, echo cancellation, semantic VAD, avatar. Language support page: nl-BE has only nl-BE-DenaNeural and nl-BE-ArnaudNeural (no HD/MAI voices). Voice Live FAQ: content filtering cannot be disabled; 100k tokens/min default quota.
findings.detail: The existing push-to-talk flow (record → STT nl-BE → model → authored reply → TTS) yields a transcript per turn, which the evidence model depends on (D-16 spoken evidence, D-20 read-aloud). A Voice Live session can also emit transcripts (text output events), but it is a continuous WebSocket. The API has internal-only ingress behind the Next.js proxy (main.bicep:321) and one 0.25 vCPU replica, so a WebSocket relay path through web→API would be needed. Push-to-talk keeps per-turn cost and allowance accounting exact; Voice Live is billed per token for audio and text.
findings.recommendation: Keep push-to-talk as the default, evidence-producing mode. If a 'live chat' mode is wanted, prototype Voice Live in westeurope with a Standard-tier text model (gpt-5.6-luna or gpt-4.1-mini), input transcription set explicitly to nl-BE, and output voice nl-BE-DenaNeural/ArnaudNeural. Relay the WebSocket through the backend, enforce MAX session seconds through the existing audio_seconds allowance, and store the transcript as evidence. Avoid gpt-realtime unless a Sweden Central resource and non-Belgian voices are acceptable.

findings.title: Pronunciation assessment exists for Dutch only as nl-NL (not nl-BE), at most 30 s on REST, prosody en-US only
findings.evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs/main/articles/ai-services/speech-service/includes/language-support/pronunciation-assessment.md: 33 locales including nl-NL; nl-BE absent. https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/speech-service/rest-speech-to-text-short (updated 2026-06-05): optional 'Pronunciation-Assessment' header (base64 JSON: ReferenceText, GradingSystem, Granularity Phoneme|Word|FullText, Dimension Basic|Comprehensive, EnableMiscue, EnableProsodyAssessment); 'For pronunciation assessment, the audio duration should be no more than 30 seconds'; returns AccuracyScore, FluencyScore, CompletenessScore, PronScore and per-word ErrorType (None/Omission/Insertion/Mispronunciation). https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/speech-service/how-to-pronunciation-assessment: cost equals the speech-to-text baseline; 'Prosody assessment is only available in the en-US locale'; syllable-level results en-US only. https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/speech-service/language-learning-with-pronunciation-assessment: the chat + assessment (grammar/vocabulary) language-learning feature 'currently supports only en-US'.
findings.detail: D-20 (DECISIONS.md:212-217) says no pronunciation score is computed 'because a transcript cannot carry one'. Scripted pronunciation assessment against nl-NL is technically available through the same REST endpoint and auth already used in speech_azure.py, but it would judge Belgian speakers against Netherlands Dutch phonetics. MAX_AUDIO_SECONDS=60 (.env.example:107; main.bicep:348) exceeds the 30 s pronunciation-assessment limit.
findings.recommendation: If the owner wants pronunciation feedback for read-aloud or shadowing, add an opt-in scripted assessment: a separate method on AzureSpeechToText that adds the header with ReferenceText = the authored sentence, Granularity=Word, Dimension=Comprehensive, locale nl-NL. Show only word-level 'try again' highlights, cap audio at 30 s, and label the result 'NL-Dutch reference, not a Belgian accent judgement'. This consciously revises D-20 and must never feed CEFR claims or skill completion.

findings.title: Evaluation and observability: reuse App Insights with the OTel GenAI conventions and add an offline eval set; Foundry cloud evaluation is optional
findings.evidence: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/agent-framework/agents/observability: spans and metrics per GenAI semconv; azure-monitor-opentelemetry >=1.8.10 instruments HTTPX so OpenAI-SDK and service spans correlate; sensitive data off by default. https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/how-to/develop/cloud-evaluation (2026-09-25): needs a Foundry project, a judge-model deployment and the Foundry User role (`pip install azure-ai-projects>=2.2.0`); evaluates JSONL/CSV datasets, stored responses or traces, and simulated conversations; results can be routed to App Insights. Techcommunity post 'Microsoft Foundry Observability Generally Available' (https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/azure-ai-foundry-blog/generally-available-evaluations-monitoring-and-tracing-in-microsoft-foundry/4502760, March 2026 per search snippet; body not retrievable). Repo: observability.py:20-28 disables httpx/FastAPI instrumentation and samples 10%; main.bicep:68-82 caps Log Analytics at 0.1 GB/day.
findings.detail: A Foundry project is an extra resource and judge-model calls cost tokens. For a single owner, a versioned JSONL of real or synthetic Dutch learner turns with expected goal_met/intent labels, run against the fixture and live models, gives most of the value. Turning on httpx auto-instrumentation would risk URL and identifier leakage, which the repo deliberately prevents.
findings.recommendation: Add custom spans around each model call with low-cardinality attributes only (prompt_version, model, tokens, latency, outcome). Keep prompts out of telemetry. Build an offline eval harness, a pytest marker plus a CLI, over the existing prompts and validate_meaning to score interpretation accuracy before any model swap. Consider Foundry cloud evaluation only if a Foundry project is created for other reasons.

findings.title: Default guardrails apply, but the classifiers are not trained on Dutch; keep the code-level validation
findings.evidence: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/openai/concepts/default-safety-policies (2026-05-31): defaults filter hate, violence, sexual and self-harm at Medium for prompts and completions; jailbreak Prompt Shields on prompts; protected material on completions; audio models covered. Note: classifiers 'specifically trained and tested on … English, German, Japanese, Spanish, French, Italian, Portuguese, and Chinese', other languages 'quality might vary'. Voice Live FAQ: content filtering is included and cannot be modified. Repo: workflow.py:28-40 treats learner text as untrusted; :75-76 regex rejects 'ignore/negeer … instructions'.
findings.detail: Filter blocks surface as HTTP 400 content_filter or finish_reason content_filter. The current client maps any 4xx to a generic ProviderError (chat_openai_compatible.py:115-117), so a learner would see a generic failure rather than a friendly message.
findings.recommendation: Detect content_filter responses explicitly and show a learner-friendly message without charging a turn. Keep the authored-reply and quote-validation design as the primary guardrail.

findings.title: Cost controls: the existing SQL allowances plus model tiering and prompt caching are enough; an API Management AI gateway is overkill
findings.evidence: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/openai/how-to/prompt-caching (2026-08-11): automatic for prompts of at least 1,024 tokens with an identical prefix; cached tokens are billed at a discount; GPT-5.6+ charge for cache writes and support prompt_cache_key and breakpoints; models before 5.6 return 400 if given prompt_cache_options. https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-management/genai-gateway-capabilities: llm-token-limit per key and llm-semantic-cache-lookup/store (needs Redis). Repo: usage/service.py reserve/commit/release; main.bicep:83-95 budget alerts (not caps); main.bicep:41-62 daily and total call/token/audio/video limits.
findings.detail: The app's prompts (system prompt plus JSON schema) are mostly short, so caching only helps the strong-tier story and review prompts. Model routing is simplest as fixed tiers: small (Luna) for interpret, rank and translate; strong (Sol/Terra) for generation. Foundry model-router exists only in limited regions (swedencentral/northeurope per the region tables) and adds unpredictability.
findings.recommendation: Keep the usage counters as the hard per-user cap and recalibrate token reservations for reasoning-token overhead (max_output_tokens covers reasoning and visible output). Put stable instructions first so long prompts can be cached. Do not add API Management, semantic cache or model-router.

findings.title: Published AI-tutor patterns that worked use structured, authored role-plays with feedback afterwards, not open chat
findings.evidence: https://blog.duolingo.com/duolingo-max/ (14 Mar 2023): curriculum experts write Roleplay scenarios and initial prompts aligned with the course; humans review AI content; after Roleplay learners get 'AI-powered feedback on the accuracy and complexity of their responses, as well as tips'; Explain My Answer gives context-specific explanations of mistakes. https://blog.duolingo.com/chatbot-language-practice/ (20 Mar 2024): a plain 'practice with me' chatbot isn't targeted or personalized; Roleplay uses several specialized prompts per turn (question, statement, change subject, close) in a flow chart with beginning, middle and end, calibrated to CEFR level. https://blog.duolingo.com/video-call/ (24 Sep 2024): adaptive conversation length (about 1 to 3 minutes), no penalties for errors, learner can ask for repetition, can skip and return. https://blog.duolingo.com/large-language-model-duolingo-lessons/ (22 Jun 2023): templated prompts with fixed rules plus variable parameters, with human experts reviewing before publishing.
findings.detail: Taalstudio already has the authored scenario plus validator core (content/conversations/pilot.json, 10 topics; LEARNING_AGENTS.md:22-37). Compared with these patterns, it lacks: (a) post-conversation feedback on accuracy and complexity with concrete better phrasings; (b) explain-my-mistake on any wrong answer; (c) adaptive difficulty and length; (d) enough scenarios (10 of hundreds of topics). These are product and UX gaps, not platform gaps.
findings.recommendation: Prioritise bounded tutor features that each make one or two calls through the existing ChatModel and usage path: a post-conversation 'Feedback' card that cites learner quotes (reuse the evidence-citation rule from D-14), an 'Explain this' button on wrong reading/listening/writing items (small model, cached per item and answer), and adaptive next steps from the coach. Scale role-play coverage with templated generation plus owner review, following the Duolingo pattern.

reusable_assets.what: ChatModel ABC with complete/complete_once and ChatResult (tokens, latency, attempts, raw)

constraints: D-12 / LEARNING_AGENTS.md:41-49: the model interprets and phrases, the application decides. No open tool loop, no arbitrary database tool, no web access, no ability to write lesson files. Any 'agent' must respect this or the owner must consciously revise it.
D-16: typed input never counts as speaking practice; spoken evidence must come from a transcript. A live voice mode must still produce stored transcripts.

D-20: no pronunciation score is computed. Adding Azure pronunciation assessment (nl-NL only) consciously revises this decision and must be labelled as NL-Dutch reference, never as CEFR or skill completion.
D-17 and GO_LIVE.md:44-47: paid usage is switched on only by PAID_USAGE_ENABLED, never by the presence of credentials; budgets are alerts, not caps.
GO_LIVE.md:50-51: do not silently select a Global deployment if regional processing matters. Prefer DataZoneStandard (EU) over GlobalStandard for new models.

main.bicep:321, 376: the API has internal-only ingress behind the Next.js signed proxy and exactly 1 replica at 0.25 vCPU / 0.5 GiB. Long-lived WebSockets (Voice Live/Realtime) need a relay path and resource sizing.

observability.py:1 and LEARNING_AGENTS.md:19-20: never export prompts, bodies, headers, full URLs or user identifiers; raw model names, prompt IDs and evidence UUIDs stay out of learner-facing feedback.
Every provider call must reserve usage before and commit or release after (usage/service.py). complete_once semantics (no hidden retries) apply to newer flows.
MAX_AUDIO_SECONDS=60 (Azure short-audio REST ceiling); pronunciation assessment on REST requires at most 30 s.

Pydantic schemas used with strict json_schema must have all fields required (nullable instead of optional), additionalProperties false, and no length/pattern constraints enforced by the service; keep those checks in code.
